Zero-Card support needs a few frontend changes, not a schema change. A full persisted `initialBaseline` also looks unnecessary for Deck publication. For Cards, however, constants alone cannot reconstruct every current creation path after reload.

## 1. Zero-Card support

| Area | Current behaviour | Narrow change |
|---|---|---|
| Creator | Both `canDeleteActiveCard` and `deleteCreatorCard()` prevent removing the last Card. | Remove both minimum-one-Card guards. |
| Creator transformations | Columns, cells, graph conversion and adding a Card already accommodate zero Card columns. Themes remain independently present. | Add regression coverage; no redesign. |
| My Decks membership | Membership derives from DeckData, without filtering out empty Decks. | None. |
| My Decks layout/tile | Sorting and rendering accept zero Cards. The tile displays `0 cards`; its normal Open action remains available. | None for basic support. |
| Working resolver/DTO | Empty Card references resolve to an empty array. Empty version-query cases are guarded. | None. |
| Working open | Creates no CardData, persists `activeCardId: null`, and still establishes the cadence anchor. | Preserve this. |
| Progress/confidence | Empty progress returns `0`; empty confidence returns `null`. No division-by-zero problem. | Preserve existing calculations. |
| Dates/completion/signals | Initialization loops execute zero times. Personal Card mutations require a resolvable Card. | None. |
| Card stack | Mapping an empty array creates no Cards, but still renders decorative stack/table elements. | Skip Card-stack rendering when empty so the Card area is simply empty. |
| Navigation/focus | Active index defaults to `0`, final index becomes `-1`. Navigation can calculate invalid indices; focused rendering assumes an existing Card. | Guard navigation and focus against absent Cards; lock Card gestures when empty. |

The main locations are [Creator deletion](./src/components/creator/creatorBoardState.ts:267), [DeckDetail](./src/components/decks/DeckDetail.tsx:185), [CardStack](./src/components/decks/CardStack.tsx:293) and [working-open persistence](./src/lib/cards/repository.ts:259).

The direct first-Card lookup in working-open persistence is already safe:

```ts
version.content.cards[0]?.cardTemplateId ?? null
```

The potentially unsafe focused lookup is:

```ts
optimisticDeck.cards[activeCardIndex]
```

It is currently behind `isFocusModeOpen`, which starts false. An empty stack offers no normal focus trigger, so this is a latent assumption rather than evidence that initial empty rendering necessarily crashes.

Legacy `deckData`/reconciliation helpers also use optional first-Card access, but the Phase 2 flow bypasses those helpers.

**Coverage needed:** deleting the final Card, adding one back, renamed zero-Card publication, membership listing, working open/reload, null active identity, no CardData initialization, empty calculations, and archive/restore. Existing integration journeys predominantly use nonempty Decks and do not prove this complete flow.

## 2. Initial/default-state reconstruction

### What is deterministic

Centralized factories can reproduce the default **values**:

- Deck title: `My Next Path`;
- four starter Card titles;
- subsequently added Card title: `My New Card`;
- Theme titles;
- null introduction/media;
- three empty Step structures;
- private-flow empty suggested dates;
- weekly cadence and `Card` label prefix.

The legacy helpers contain dated defaults and date generation, but the Phase 2 adapter explicitly clears suggested dates for initial and subsequently added Cards. Those legacy dates therefore do not require preservation in the new comparison rule.

### What is not recoverable today

[Creation defaults](./src/components/creator/creatorBoardState.ts:111) differ between starter Cards and subsequently added Cards. Their origin is not persisted.

For example, these histories can produce indistinguishable current content:

- a starter Card originally titled `Get started`, later renamed `My New Card`;
- an added Card originally titled `My New Card`, never edited.

The first should be outstanding; the second should not. Current position cannot reliably distinguish them after deletion, reordering or later reuse.

Generated Card, Step and Theme IDs also cannot be reproduced by calling the factory again. Existing IDs can be supplied to comparison factories, but that does not recover original reference membership or original Step order.

### Revised recommendation

**Deck publication does not need a full initial baseline.** For a never-published Deck, its saved, trimmed title differing from `My Next Path` already guarantees a difference from the initial state. The published-Card reference prerequisite is then checked separately.

An untouched new board can be compared against its original **in-memory** board, preserving the same generated IDs. That requires no database field or write on opening.

**For Cards, a full baseline is not automatically necessary either.** Centralized factories plus a small creation-default identifier could reconstruct default values. But exact reconstruction from the currently persisted fields alone is not reliable for every path.

That leaves the explicit comparison decision below.

## 3. Scoped publication flush

[The current implementation](./src/components/creator/cardArchitectureAdapter.ts:89) works as follows:

1. `publish(board, target, notes)` calls `save(board)`.
2. `save()` walks all Cards and writes every changed/new Card.
3. It then saves changed Deck content.
4. Any failure rejects the save and prevents publication.
5. Only afterward does publication restrict itself to the selected target.

An earlier failed queue operation does not permanently poison the queue because its rejection is caught. The problem is that the next individual Publish attempts those unrelated saves again.

**Smallest change:**

- add internal entity-scoped save operations;
- serialize the selected entity’s flush, confirmation and publication together;
- Card Publish saves/confirms only that Card;
- Deck Publish saves/confirms Deck content and verifies referenced roots/versions without saving unrelated Card drafts;
- keep aggregate coordination for `Publish and leave`;
- schedule automatic retry delays outside the mutation queue;
- preserve revision checks and independent publication transactions.

Deck publication already accepts an older published Card version while that Card has an outstanding newer draft. Keep that behaviour.

There is one creation-time exception: first persistence currently creates the graph atomically, and a newly added Card’s mutation route requires it to be referenced by the saved Deck. That dependency needs the decision below; changing only the client save loop would not fully achieve isolation.

## 4. Constants cleanup

Use a shared, client/server-safe defaults module for values that affect both construction and publication:

- `DEFAULT_CREATOR_DECK_TITLE`;
- `DEFAULT_CREATOR_CARD_COUNT`;
- `DEFAULT_CREATOR_STARTER_CARD_TITLES`;
- `DEFAULT_CREATOR_NEW_CARD_TITLE`;
- a Theme-title factory;
- default cadence and label prefix.

Retain separate legacy defaults where necessary rather than changing legacy characterization behaviour incidentally.

Two inconsistencies also need attention:

- [The private adapter](./src/components/creator/cardArchitectureAdapter.ts:9) initializes `Theme 1`–`Theme 3`, but clearing a Theme uses the legacy helper that restores `Stream 1`–`Stream 3`.
- [The reload adapter](./src/components/creator/cardArchitectureAdapter.ts:20) sets `defaultCardTitle: ""`, defeating nonblank default restoration after reload.

The actual persisted Card property is `intro.title`; no field rename is required.

## 5. Remaining significant ambiguities

### QUESTION FOR USER — Card default origin and identity comparison

Should never-published comparison preserve each Card’s exact creation preset, or compare against one common default definition?

Also, should rearranging otherwise empty Steps count as outstanding solely because their identity order changed?

**Options:**

- preserve exact initial state, requiring enough persisted information to recover its preset and identity order;
- reconstruct preset values and compare default content independently of generated identities;
- standardize all new Card defaults, changing the current starter/default distinction.

**Recommendation:** retain starter and added-Card defaults, record only a small creation-preset identifier, and exclude generated identity differences from the never-published default comparison. Preserve identities in actual persisted content and published-version comparisons. This requires your approval; it is not equivalent to adding a full baseline.

### QUESTION FOR USER — Default title restoration after reload

For an existing Card, should clearing its title restore its original creation default or the title loaded when Creator opened?

The original transformation assigns the loaded title as the fallback; the Phase 2 adapter currently replaces that fallback with an empty string.

**Recommendation:** preserve the loaded title as the fallback for existing Cards, and the creation default for new Cards. Keep Theme restoration on `Theme N`.

### QUESTION FOR USER — Publication during incomplete structural persistence

A newly added Card may have a persisted root but no successfully saved Deck reference. Its current save/publish endpoint rejects it with `CARD_OUTSIDE_DECK`.

**Options:**

- require the necessary Deck-reference save before publishing it;
- permit owner-authorized Card publication before Deck attachment is saved.

**Recommendation:** retain the attachment prerequisite, but flush only the necessary reference change—not unrelated Deck metadata. Keep first graph creation as a coordinated initialization exception. If complete isolation must include these construction stages, the server authorization/API boundary needs an explicit adjustment.

### QUESTION FOR USER — Zero-Card introduction preview in My Decks

The introduction thumbnail/play control currently lives inside the first miniature Card. With zero Cards, it disappears; the ordinary Open action and introduction playback inside Deck detail remain available.

**Recommendation:** keep that minimal behaviour for this change, without inventing a synthetic Card or new preview surface. Confirm whether “appears normally” requires introduction preview on the zero-Card tile too.

No files, database records, migrations or commits were changed.

I read the attachment completely. The lifecycle is broadly compatible with the Phase 1 foundations, but **two parts change existing contracts**: unpublished Deck membership, and publishing a composition different from the retained Creator draft.

The new zero-Card start and common Card title also remove the earlier reason to persist a full `initialBaseline` for publication eligibility.

## 1. Specification versus current implementation

| Area | Current Phase 2 behaviour | Required change |
|---|---|---|
| Enter Create | Allocates IDs locally, but creates four starter Cards. Opening itself performs no writes. | Start with zero Cards and retain local Deck identity. |
| Defaults | `My Next Path`; starter titles; added Cards use `My New Card`. | Shared constants for `My Next Path`, `My Next Card` and Theme defaults. |
| First completed edit | Autosaves through the persistence queue. | Preserve; distinguish untouched/no-op edits from actual changes. |
| First persistence | Creates roots/drafts and lightweight DeckData membership atomically. | Revisit membership presentation/storage as discussed below. |
| Add Card | Allocates Card/Step IDs immediately and autosaves. Later additions create the Card, then save Deck references in separate operations. | Preserve deliberate persistence; strengthen structural atomicity/recovery. |
| Card/Step editing | Updates the existing Card draft; identity stays stable. | Preserve. |
| Top-level Save Draft | Still present. | Remove. |
| Autosave recovery | One attempt; errors share publication feedback. | Add bounded, entity-specific retry coordination. |
| Publication cues | Entity-specific, but include unsaved local changes and treat every non-null draft as outstanding. | Derive readiness from confirmed saved state and first-publication title rules. |
| First Card publication | Structural validation only; default title can publish. | Enforce the approved first-title rule in UI and repository publication. |
| First Deck publication | Requires published referenced Cards, but does not enforce the default-title rule. | Add trimmed, nonblank, nondefault title validation. |
| Individual publication | Saves the entire board before publishing the selected entity. | Flush only the selected entity and necessary creation dependencies. |
| Deck publication with newer Card drafts | Already allowed; does not publish those drafts. | Add conditional warning/confirmation. |
| Card removal | Removes references, retaining Card roots; final Card cannot be removed. | Allow final removal; retain roots, versions and personal data. |
| Reload | Creator resolves current drafts/latest published content; working mode resolves adopted versions. | Preserve the distinction; repair fallback inconsistencies. |

The principal implementation seams are [CreatorDragLab](./src/components/creator/CreatorDragLab.tsx:1085), [CreatorPersistence](./src/components/creator/cardArchitectureAdapter.ts:89), [repository publication](./src/lib/cards/repository.ts:167) and [Creator resolution](./src/lib/cards/resolvers.ts:71).

No generic completeness validation should be introduced. Keep structural validation, ownership checks, stable Step identity, valid references and revision protection.

## 2. Defaults and initial-state comparison

With this specification, **a persisted initial baseline is unnecessary for first-publication eligibility**:

- a first-publishable Deck must have a nonblank, nondefault title;
- a first-publishable Card must have a nondefault introduction title;
- those title changes necessarily distinguish the content from the standard initial state.

An entity can still be outstanding but ineligible—for example, Step edits while its Card title remains `My Next Card`. Track those states separately.

For an untouched local board, retain its initial in-memory snapshot to detect no-op saves and leaving without persistence. Generated IDs should remain stable throughout that local session.

After publication exists, use the repository’s existing comparison with the latest immutable version. Reverting published content already clears the draft.

Centralize constants/default factories in a module usable by both browser and server. Do not change IDs or rewrite existing content to adopt the new defaults.

Two current fallback defects remain:

- clearing a Theme restores `Stream N`, rather than the private Creator’s `Theme N`;
- the [reload adapter](./src/components/creator/cardArchitectureAdapter.ts:20) sets `defaultCardTitle: ""`.

The persisted Card field is currently `intro.title`; the specification’s `introduction.title` should map to that existing field, without a schema rename.

## 3. Add Card persistence

I endorse persisting Add Card immediately. It is an explicit structural edit, and postponing it would complicate reload, uploads and dependent saves.

The safer implementation is:

```text
Allocate identities locally
→ render Card immediately
→ atomically persist Card root and Deck reference
→ confirm structural save
```

For the first addition to an unsaved Deck, the existing initial-graph transaction provides an appropriate foundation. For later additions, the current separate Card-create and Deck-save requests can leave an unattached root after partial failure.

A narrow repository operation should create the default Card and attach its reference in one transaction, using stable IDs and the Deck revision. This does not make subsequent Card editing/publication dependent on Deck publication.

Card edits made while creation is pending should queue behind that creation, rather than create another identity.

## 4. Independent Card authorization and publication flush

### `CARD_OUTSIDE_DECK`

It is **not needed to establish Card ownership**. Repository Card saves/publication already independently verify the Card owner and expected revision.

It currently enforces membership in the route’s Deck context. Importantly, it does **not** require that Deck to be published: publishing a Card inside a never-published saved Deck already works.

For genuinely independent Card operations, ownership can authorize saving/publication without a persisted Deck reference. The narrow boundary should:

- authenticate the actor;
- load the target Card;
- independently verify ownership;
- validate content/revision;
- return the target Card state without requiring the whole Deck DTO.

Deck reference mutations retain their own ownership/access validation.

Do not remove all Deck-context authorization indiscriminately:

- personal CardData uploads still require legitimate working-Deck context;
- Deck introduction media remains Deck-authorized;
- canonical Card media currently also requires Creator Deck membership through [upload authorization](./src/lib/cards/uploadAuthorization.ts:6).

Canonical Card upload/status authorization would need corresponding owner-based resolution if saving/publication can proceed before attachment or after removal. Preserve asset-membership checks for status requests and strict upload validation. No storage namespace or Cloudflare delivery redesign is necessary.

### Scoped flush

Replace the whole-board pre-publication save with target-specific operations:

- Card Publish: confirm creation, flush that Card, confirm its authoritative revision/content, publish it;
- Deck Publish: flush Deck content, verify published referenced versions, handle the warning, publish Deck;
- Publish and leave: retain aggregate coordination and independent transaction recovery.

An unrelated failed save must not be retried as a prerequisite. Delayed retries must not occupy the queue or replay obsolete snapshots over newer edits.

## 5. Positional Card numbering

The architecture already supports different labels for the same Card in different Deck compositions.

[layoutCardLabels()](./src/lib/cards/layout.ts:2) derives labels from array position. Creator uses its draft reference order; working rendering uses the adopted Deck version’s reference order.

Neither Card roots/versions nor CardData persist `Card 3` as identity. Deck content persists ordered `cardTemplateId` references and a label prefix.

Local Creator identifiers such as `card-3` are grid-column addresses. They can change when columns are rebuilt; the underlying global Card identity remains unchanged. The legacy template conversion helper emits labels, but the active first-class persistence path uses `privateGraph()`, which excludes them.

**However, the specific publication example conflicts with the current publication contract.**

If Creator still references Cards A, B and C, and A/B have never been published, Deck publication must fail. Current publication neither filters them out nor publishes a separate subset. It publishes the exact saved draft and clears that draft.

Different numbering works naturally when the compositions actually differ—for example, published version `[C]` and a later draft `[A, B, C]`.

## 6. Warning about newer unpublished Card drafts

The repository already publishes using referenced Cards’ latest published versions while leaving their newer drafts untouched.

The required warning should occur:

```text
Flush Deck only
→ read authoritative references/Card publication state
→ identify referenced published Cards with outstanding drafts
→ obtain confirmation if necessary
→ publish Deck without publishing Cards
```

For the private flow, saved outstanding Card drafts are identifiable by `latestVersion >= 1` and non-null `draft`, given the repository’s existing equality/reset behaviour.

Tie confirmation to the Deck revision and published Card versions being used. If those change while the confirmation is open, refresh the decision rather than silently using a different selection.

For `Publish and leave`, perform this check after required Card publications. Do not warn unnecessarily about drafts that the flow has just published successfully.

The recorded `cardVersionAtPublish` remains historical. Working mode still honours personal adopted Card versions; the warning must not imply that Deck publication updates everyone’s CardData.

## 7. Zero-Card rendering and recovery

Backend publication, membership resolution and working-open persistence already accommodate zero Cards. Working open creates no CardData and retains `activeCardId: null`.

Frontend changes remain narrow:

- remove both final-Card deletion guards;
- leave Themes and Add Card available in Creator;
- omit the decorative Card stack when empty;
- guard navigation/focus against absent Cards;
- preserve existing empty progress/confidence results: `0` and `null`.

Removing references must not remove Card roots, versions or CardData. Older published Deck versions can continue referencing removed Cards.

Reload/recovery also needs to distinguish:

- locally allocated but unpersisted entities;
- persisted default Cards;
- outstanding saved drafts;
- failed pending edits;
- uncertain writes that may already have committed.

Stable IDs support retry, but revision recovery must distinguish a lost response from genuine concurrent editing. Browser reload currently loses unsaved local edits; no durable local recovery mechanism exists.

## 8. Tests and compatibility

Add coverage for:

- untouched zero-Card open/leave: no writes;
- first Deck edit and first Add Card persistence;
- common defaults and fallback behaviour before/after reload;
- title-based first publication with empty Steps and duplicate Card titles;
- zero-Card publish/open/reload/archive/restore;
- published Card plus newer draft satisfying Deck prerequisites;
- warning confirm/cancel and changed confirmation state;
- scoped flush despite unrelated save failures;
- atomic Add Card and uncertain-response recovery;
- removal retaining independent Card state;
- draft/published positional labels for the same Card identity;
- retries, conflicts and recoverable Publish and leave.

The browser journey currently assumes four starter Cards and explicitly clicks Save Draft. Those assumptions must be replaced. Relevant suites include `phase2.test.ts`, `phase2.integration.ts`, `card-foundation.integration.ts` and the Phase 2 browser journey.

There is no reason to migrate existing published templates to the new defaults. Preserve their content. Existing never-published disposable fixtures may require adjustment; do not automatically rename existing saved drafts.

## 9. QUESTION FOR USER items

### QUESTION FOR USER — Saved drafts outside My Decks

The attachment explicitly says an unpublished saved Deck should not appear in My Decks. Current first persistence creates null-adoption DeckData, and My Decks displays it as a draft.

**Options:** retain that bookkeeping but hide unpublished entries, or defer DeckData creation until first publication.

**Recommendation:** retain lightweight DeckData to avoid changing adoption/archive foundations, but exclude null-adoption entries from My Decks. Confirm how users should reopen saved drafts while the future My Drafts view does not exist: minimal draft navigation now, or an explicitly accepted temporary URL-only path?

### QUESTION FOR USER — Publishing a subset while retaining the larger draft

Should Deck publication always use the exact saved composition, or may it publish `[C]` while retaining draft `[A, B, C]`?

**Recommendation:** preserve exact-composition publication. Removing A/B from the draft does not delete their CardTemplates, and C becomes Card 1. If retaining the larger draft during subset publication is required, that introduces an explicit publication-selection contract; the remaining draft would stay outstanding rather than become `null`.

### QUESTION FOR USER — Card title comparison and restoration

The Deck rule explicitly requires trimmed, nonblank, nondefault text. Should first Card publication use exactly the same comparison against `My Next Card`?

Also, for already-published Cards, should clearing the title restore `My Next Card` or the title loaded when Creator opened?

**Recommendation:** use the same trimmed/nonblank first-publication test; restore `My Next Card` for never-published Cards and the loaded title for existing published Cards. Apply no first-title restriction to later publications.

### QUESTION FOR USER — Warning for unsaved Card changes

A referenced Card can have failed local edits while its persisted root has no draft. A saved-root-only check would not warn.

**Recommendation:** warn for either saved outstanding Card drafts or known pending/failed local Card edits, without flushing those unrelated saves. Confirm whether that broader warning matches the intended wording.

### QUESTION FOR USER — Removal while Card autosave is failing

Should removal wait for the Card’s pending save, or detach immediately while saving continues independently?

**Recommendation:** detach immediately, retain the owner-authorized Card save queue, and keep exhausted failure/Retry Save feedback accessible in Creator even after its column disappears. Do not silently discard a completed edit because its Card was removed.

> Please treat the following as agreed product/architecture decisions unless you find a genuine contradiction that makes one impossible:
>

> - Opening a brand-new Creator session should not persist anything by itself.
> - The new Deck default title remains `My Next Path`.
> - New Cards use `card.intro.title = "My Next Card"` as the common default.
> - Repeated/default values such as `My Next Path`, `My Next Card`, Theme defaults, etc. should be centralized in an appropriate shared client/server-safe defaults/constants module rather than repeated as magic strings.
> - IDs may be allocated locally before persistence.
> - IDs remain stable through draft and publication.
> - Completed edits autosave the relevant entity draft.
> - There is no permanent top-level Save Draft button.
> - Modal Save buttons still mean “apply this edit and close”.
> - Save Draft never creates a published version.
> - New Deck first publication requires a trimmed, nonblank title different from `My Next Path`.
> - New Card first publication requires a trimmed, nonblank intro title different from `My Next Card`.
> - No generic completeness rule should be introduced.
> - Steps may remain sparse/blank.
> - Duplicate Card titles are allowed.
> - Zero-Card Deck publication is valid.
> - A Deck can contain unpublished Cards in draft form, but the Deck cannot publish until every currently referenced Card has at least one published version.
> - A Card having a newer unpublished draft does NOT block Deck publication.
> - Before Deck publication, if any referenced Card has newer unpublished changes, the user must receive a warning/confirmation rather than a block.
> - That warning should also include known local Card changes that are pending or have failed to save, if those changes would not be represented in the published Card version.
> - Deck publication uses the exact saved Deck composition. We do NOT want subset publication.
> - Card numbering is positional, derived from the Deck composition, and is not Card identity.
> - The same Card may have a different positional label in different Deck versions/drafts.
> - Publishing a Deck must not silently publish Card drafts.
> - Individual Card Publish should flush/confirm only the relevant Card and necessary creation dependencies.
> - Individual Deck Publish should flush/confirm only the Deck itself and necessary publication preconditions.
> - Unrelated failed saves must not block another entity’s publication.
> - `Publish and leave` may remain an aggregate orchestration flow.
> - Add Card is an intentional structural edit and should persist immediately.
> - Preferred Add Card design: allocate Card/Step IDs locally, render immediately, then atomically create the Card root/default draft and attach its reference to the Deck.
> - A Card root should remain first-class and independent after removal from a Deck.
> - Removing a Card removes only the Deck reference; it does not delete CardTemplate, versions, or CardData.
> - Removing the final Card is allowed.
> - If a Card is removed while its autosave is pending, detach it from the Deck immediately and let the Card save continue independently.
> - If that independent save ultimately fails after the normal automatic retries, fail silently for now. Add a later TODO for a better recovery mechanism.
> - Canonical Card save/publication should not require Deck membership if Card ownership/revision is sufficient.
> - Preserve Deck-context authorization where it is genuinely required for personal CardData, working-mode access, or media/security flows.
> - Unpublished Creator drafts must NOT appear in My Decks.
> - We are adding a minimal Creator-only `My Drafts` entry point now.
> - `My Drafts` should be a small unobtrusive link/button in the top Creator area which opens a modal/pop-up.
> - The modal should minimally list persisted Deck drafts and allow the user to reopen one in Creator.
> - Do not turn this into a full draft-management product yet.
> - A completely untouched local Creator session should not appear in My Drafts.
> - A persisted Creator draft should become reopenable there.
> - We may eventually decide that drafts belong only inside Creator, so keep this intentionally minimal.
> - Existing published content should not be migrated or renamed merely to adopt the new defaults.
> - Preserve immutable published versions and stable first-class Card/Step identity.
> - Preserve the existing architecture decisions around ownership, nullable adoption, independent DeckData/CardData, immutable versions and drafts.

## 1. Executive assessment

**The existing foundation can support this workflow without a new persistence model or production migration. The main work is replacing whole-board orchestration with entity-scoped persistence.**

The important findings are:

- Independent Card/Deck roots, drafts, immutable versions, revisions and publisher adoption already exist.
- The current Creator adapter still treats saving and publication as whole-board operations. That is the principal incompatibility.
- Initial creation is transactional, but **adding a Card to an existing Deck is currently two separate operations**.
- Canonical Card save/publication is unnecessarily coupled to Deck membership at the HTTP boundary; the repository itself already authorizes by Card ownership and revision.
- Zero-Card Decks already work at the domain/repository level. Creator deletion guards and working-view navigation need narrowly scoped changes.
- Positional labels are already excluded from first-class persisted Card content. However, positional **UI column IDs** still drive upload callbacks and React keys, creating a separate identity risk.
- My Drafts can be an ownership-based, read-only list without becoming another membership system.
- No persisted `initialBaseline` is needed for the agreed publication rules.

I inspected the current working tree and the attached lifecycle specification. I made no changes, ran no migrations, connected to no database and did not run tests/builds that generate artifacts. The existing staged Phase 2 changes remain untouched.

---

## 2. Confirmed current-vs-intended gaps

The main implementation points are [CreatorDragLab.tsx](./src/components/creator/CreatorDragLab.tsx), [cardArchitectureAdapter.ts](./src/components/creator/cardArchitectureAdapter.ts), [creatorBoardState.ts](./src/components/creator/creatorBoardState.ts), and [repository.ts](./src/lib/cards/repository.ts).

| Lifecycle | Current implementation | Required change |
|---|---|---|
| Enter Create | `NewCreatorPage` constructs `blankPrivateBoard()`. It allocates ephemeral IDs without writing, but creates four starter Cards. | Construct a zero-Card board. Retain allocation without persistence. |
| Local Deck ID | Allocated by the board factory before persistence. In the current route this factory runs during server rendering and passes the board to the client. | No database change required. Keep the allocated ID stable throughout that editor session. |
| Untouched leave | `creatorPublicationState()` marks any board without a DTO outstanding. The leave flow can then call whole-board save. | Untouched local defaults must neither prompt as outstanding nor persist on departure. |
| First Deck edit | Both `updateBoardAndSaveDraft()` and misleadingly named `updateBoardLocally()` trigger whole-board persistence. | Submit only Deck content. With zero Cards, first persistence creates no Card roots. |
| First persistence | `createPrivateGraph()` atomically creates supplied roots and lightweight null-adoption DeckData. | Reuse for initial persistence, including an empty graph. Keep this separate from My Decks visibility. |
| Add Card | Immediate local rendering. For an existing Deck, `CreatorPersistence.save()` creates the Card first, then saves Deck references separately. | One transaction for Card creation plus reference attachment. |
| Card/Step edits | Modal Save applies and closes, then saves the whole board. | Save the containing Card only. |
| Deck edits | Title, themes and introduction changes save the whole board. | Save Deck only. |
| Autosave feedback | Automatic saves and the top-level Save Draft button share `persistSavedDraft()` and “Draft saved” feedback. | Remove the button; retain restrained autosave feedback and entity-specific failure state. |
| Autosave failure | One attempt, generic error, no bounded retries. One global queue serializes all entities. | Per-entity queues, bounded transient retries and explicit conflict handling. |
| First Card publication | Any non-null draft can publish. No first-title rule. A default Card is shown outstanding immediately. | Shared first-publication title rule and saved-state publication cue. |
| Later Card publication | Repository creates an immutable version, clears the draft and advances existing publisher CardData. | Preserve this contract; change orchestration and API coupling. |
| First Deck publication | Repository rejects references to never-published Cards; accepts zero references. No default-title rule. | Add the first-title rule. Preserve the existing reference prerequisite. |
| Later Deck publication | Publishes the exact saved draft references and records each Card’s current published version. | Preserve; do not manufacture a Deck change because a Card changed. |
| Deck publish with Card drafts | Allowed by repository, without a warning. Client saves all Card drafts first. | Warn without flushing those drafts; include known pending/failed local Card edits. |
| Card removal | Changes Deck composition; does not delete Card roots. Whole-board queue still couples subsequent saves to membership. | Retain independent Card jobs after detachment. |
| Final Card removal | Blocked in both `canDeleteActiveCard` and `deleteCreatorCard()`. | Remove both guards. |
| Reload | Edit route resolves Deck draft/latest baseline and each owned Card’s draft/latest baseline. | Preserve resolution; extend DTOs with explicit published baselines where needed. |
| My Drafts | Does not exist. | Add a minimal owner-based resolver/API/modal. |
| My Decks | `membershipDTO()` returns null-adoption records; `AppShell` renders them as draft entries. | Exclude Creator-only/null-adoption entries from both active and archived My Decks lists. |
| Publish and leave | Saves everything, publishes Cards, then Deck through independent transactions. Earlier successful publications survive failure. | Preserve independent transactions; replace the initial whole-board operation with aggregate coordination of scoped queues. |
| Media | Upload startup and completion invoke whole-board saves. Canonical upload authorization currently requires Deck context. | Scope persistence, preserve security checks, and target callbacks by stable Card identity. |

### Behaviour already correct and worth preserving

- `saveCardDraft()` and `saveDeckDraft()` update the single root draft.
- Reverting content to the latest published content clears the draft.
- Publication does not create draft history.
- Card publication does not create a Deck version.
- Deck publication does not publish Card drafts.
- Publisher adoption updates existing personal data only, including archived DeckData without restoring it.
- Working resolution uses adopted versions.
- Duplicate Card titles are not prohibited.
- Blank Step content is structurally valid.
- Globally stable Step IDs and reservation rules already exist.

### Obsolete behaviour to remove, not work around

- Four starter Cards and their starter titles/dates in the new-board path.
- `"My New Card"` as the added-Card default.
- Whole-board saving before every publication and upload.
- `!dto` and `draft !== null` as sufficient first-publication cues.
- Top-level Save Draft.
- Creator draft tiles in My Decks.
- Canonical Card membership checks in the nested save/publication endpoint.
- Positional column IDs as the identity of asynchronous upload targets.

## 3. Remaining QUESTION FOR USER items

These are the remaining meaningful choices. The rest of the plan can proceed without inventing additional product behaviour.

### QUESTION FOR USER 1 — Which published Decks belong in My Drafts?

**Settled:** never-published Decks with persisted drafts belong there.

Two further cases need confirmation:

1. Published Deck with an outstanding Deck draft.
2. Published Deck whose Deck is clean but whose referenced owned Cards have outstanding drafts.

**Options**

- Literal Deck-draft list: include never-published Decks and outstanding Deck drafts; exclude Card-only work.
- Creator unfinished-work list: include all three cases.

**Recommendation:** include all three. Otherwise, saving a Card edit inside a published Deck creates unfinished Creator work that the new entry point cannot recover conveniently.

This would still be a minimal list: one row per owned Deck, not a Card-management interface. If a Card eventually appears in several owned Decks, several Decks could qualify; that does not duplicate the Card draft.

**Archive interaction:** I recommend DeckData archival does not hide owned unfinished work from My Drafts. Archiving personal use and owning editable content are separate concerns.

**Can work proceed?** Yes, except the final My Drafts query and inclusion tests.

### QUESTION FOR USER 2 — What should clearing a previously published Card’s title restore?

The specification explicitly settles newly created Cards: clearing restores `My Next Card`.

For previously published Cards, current behaviour is inconsistent:

- The older board helper uses a loaded title as `defaultCardTitle`.
- The current Phase 2 adapter overrides `defaultCardTitle` to `""`.
- A Card created and published in the same session can retain a different fallback from one reopened later.

**Options**

- Always restore `My Next Card`.
- Restore the latest published nonblank title, falling back to `My Next Card`.
- Restore the title present when the editor opened.

**Recommendation:** restore the latest published nonblank title, otherwise `My Next Card`. That gives consistent behaviour before and after reload and avoids tying behaviour to when the editor opened.

This affects an explicit clearing action only; opening old content must not rewrite it.

**Can work proceed?** Yes, except this fallback and its tests.

### QUESTION FOR USER 3 — Removing a Card during an upload

The locked behaviour covers pending **Card saves**. An upload still in progress is a distinct operation.

Currently, removal can cause a Step upload callback to find no pair and omit the metadata update. Introduction uploads have an additional positional-target risk described below.

**Options**

- Let the upload finish and save its metadata to the independent Card.
- Abort/drop the upload result after detachment, leaving asset cleanup to the deferred cleanup work.

**Recommendation:** let an already-authorized upload finish and save to the original Card by stable identity. Do not attach it to another Card or keep the removed Card visible. Preserve the existing modal-cancel behaviour.

**Can work proceed?** Yes, except the detached-upload completion policy. Fixing stable targeting is required either way.

### QUESTION FOR USER 4 — Selecting another My Drafts entry while visible edits cannot save

My Drafts introduces an additional navigation path. The current editor only guards its explicit return link.

**Options**

- Finish pending saves before switching; if visible edits exhaust retries, remain in the current editor.
- Offer an explicit discard-and-switch action after failure.
- Switch immediately and rely on background saves.

**Recommendation:** finish saves before switching and remain if visible changes cannot be saved. Do not introduce a discard workflow in this change. Detached Card jobs remain subject to the already-agreed silent-failure rule.

Saved unpublished work does not itself need to prevent switching; it is recoverable through Creator.

**Can work proceed?** Yes, except the final switch-navigation behaviour.

## 4. Proposed state model

Use the existing persisted fields and a small per-entity client coordinator. Do not add persisted workflow flags.

### Persisted versus derived state

| State | Deck | Card | Representation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Local-only identity | Local Deck ID and content | Local Card/Step IDs awaiting Add transaction | Client only |
| Persisted root | Root exists | Root exists | Existing root |
| Persisted default draft | Possible after an intentional action | Normal after Add Card | `latestVersion: 0`, default `draft` |
| Never-published | No immutable version | No immutable version | `latestVersion === 0` |
| Saved outstanding draft | Content differs from defaults/published content | Same | Derived |
| Published and clean | Published baseline, `draft: null` | Same | Existing fields |
| Published plus draft | Non-null draft differing from baseline | Same | Existing fields |
| Pending local save | Desired content exceeds acknowledged content | Same | Client queue |
| Failed local save | Pending content could not be confirmed | Same | Client queue/error |
| Publication in progress | Selected Deck command executing | Selected Card command executing | Client only |
| Conflict | Expected revision no longer valid | Same | Client error with retained local content |
| Publishable | Saved outstanding + first-title rule if applicable + published references | Saved outstanding + first-title rule if applicable | Derived |
| Outstanding but not publishable | Default/blank first title, or unpublished references | Default/blank first title | Derived reasons |

Keep these distinct:

- **Local dirty:** desired content differs from the acknowledged saved content.
- **Saved outstanding:** saved content differs from the appropriate baseline.
- **Publishable:** saved outstanding plus publication requirements.
- **Busy/failed/conflicted:** execution state, not content state.

A publish button should not become dark merely because a root exists or `latestVersion === 0`. It also must not say “Published” for an untouched, never-published entity.

### Per-entity client state

A coordinator needs approximately:

- stable entity ID;
- persistence/creation status;
- last acknowledged root revision and content;
- latest published baseline;
- latest desired content;
- local edit generation;
- acknowledged generation;
- in-flight command;
- retry count/timer;
- structured error;
- publication status;
- attachment status for Cards.

These are operational state, not new database fields.

### Defaults and `initialBaseline`

Use pure default factories with caller-supplied IDs:

- default Deck content with zero references;
- default Card content with three sparse Steps;
- shared title, theme, cadence and label defaults.

Compare content using those factories without treating newly allocated identity values as content edits. Published comparisons must continue to include actual Step identity and order.

There is no need to reconstruct the historical allocation order of initially empty Step IDs to enforce first publication: the nondefault title requirement already guarantees a substantive difference from the default content.

**Do not add `initialBaseline`.** It would duplicate deterministically known content and introduce compatibility work without solving a requirement in this workflow.

| `globals.css` | **Minimal additions only:** My Drafts/warning presentation if existing modal styles cannot be reused. | No broad Creator layout rewrite. |
| Tests listed below | **Update/add focused coverage.** | Keep real disposable Mongo and mocked external media boundaries. |
| Migration tooling | **No functional migration change expected.** | Preserve published content and existing migration policy. |

### Obsolete adapter behaviour to remove

`privateGraph()` is useful as a projection, but should no longer be the save unit. Split it so saving a Card does not require extracting every Card from the current board.

Likewise, whole-Deck refreshes after every Card operation should be replaced with entity acknowledgements. Otherwise a refresh can replace metadata or revisions belonging to another pending operation, or lose a detached Card from the coordinator.

## 6. Detailed lifecycle/orchestration plan

### A. Entering and editing a new Deck

1. Build default zero-Card state and allocate a Deck ID.
2. Do not enqueue anything on mount.
3. Modal Cancel does nothing.
4. Modal Save computes the resulting content.
5. If the edit produces no effective change, enqueue nothing.
6. A completed Deck change enqueues Deck persistence.
7. First persistence calls `createPrivateGraph()` with an empty Card graph.
8. On acknowledgement, retain the same Deck ID and change the URL to its edit route.
9. The persisted draft becomes eligible for My Drafts.

Keep creation of existing lightweight null-adoption DeckData for now. It supports current publisher adoption without making that record a visible My Decks entry.

### B. Add Card: exact transaction and recovery

**Unsaved Deck**

Use `createPrivateGraph()` for the first committed creation snapshot:

- Deck root and current Deck content;
- new Card root/default draft;
- its three Step reservations;
- Deck reference;
- lightweight DeckData.

These already fit one transaction.

**Persisted Deck**

Add a narrow repository operation, conceptually:

```ts
createAndAttachCard(actor, {
  deckTemplateId,
  expectedDeckRevision,
  cardTemplateId,
  stepIds,
  nextDeckContent
})
```

The server constructs/validates default Card content using shared defaults.

Inside one transaction:

1. Validate actor and Deck ownership/revision.
2. Validate the proposed Deck composition and existing references.
3. Validate the new Card identity and Step identities.
4. Create the private Card root/default draft and reservations.
5. Save the Deck draft with the new reference.
6. Increment the Deck revision.
7. Return scoped Deck and Card acknowledgements.

If Step reservation or Deck validation fails, neither half commits.

**Client ordering**

- Allocate IDs and render immediately.
- Retain an immutable creation command until its outcome is established.
- Card edits made immediately afterward update that Card’s desired content.
- They wait behind **that Card’s creation**, not behind every other Card.
- Later Deck changes serialize behind the structural Add command.
- Two rapid Adds become ordered structural operations; neither may overwrite the other’s reference.

**Lost response**

The transaction prevents “Card committed but reference did not” for the new operation. It does not prevent an HTTP response being lost after both commit.

Recovery must read the known IDs and reconcile:

- Neither exists: retry the same creation command.
- The expected Card and Deck attachment exist consistently: acknowledge creation.
- Only part exists, identity/ownership differs, or subsequent changes make the result ambiguous: stop with a conflict/recovery error.
- Do not allocate replacement IDs or blindly reattach a Card after another tab removed it.

The existing `createPrivateGraph()` already has exact-content retry recognition. Keep the original creation snapshot for retries; do not replace it with newer local edits.

No durable idempotency entity is necessary for this bounded workflow. Where concurrent changes prevent proving the outcome, a safe explicit conflict is preferable to guessing.

**Deck revision changes**

An actual competing edit must not be silently rebased over. Preserve local content and report the conflict. Independent existing Cards can continue saving/publishing.

### C. Entity-scoped autosave

Use one lane per Deck/Card and explicit multi-entity barriers for structural transactions.

Each lane:

1. Holds the newest desired content.
2. Allows only one request in flight.
3. Captures content, expected revision and local generation for that request.
4. On success, updates acknowledged content/revision.
5. If newer desired content exists, submits the newest content next.
6. Never replaces newer local content with an older response.

Retries should use delays of approximately **1, 3 and 8 seconds after successive failures**, following the immediate attempt. These timings fit the repository’s revision model.

Important distinctions:

- **Known failed request:** retry the latest desired snapshot against the last confirmed revision.
- **Uncertain outcome:** read first and determine whether the submitted snapshot committed.
- **Conflict:** stop blind retries; retain local edits.
- **Validation/authorization failure:** stop automatic retries.
- **Transient network/server failure:** bounded retries.

`creatorRequest()` currently discards structured response information. Fixing that is necessary to implement this distinction.

Do not let each newly coalesced edit restart an unlimited retry cycle during an outage. After exhaustion, show the entity’s persistent failure and temporary Retry Save control.

Keep successful autosave feedback compact. Do not add permanent “draft outstanding” labels again.

### D. Individual Card Publish

1. Select the Card by `cardTemplateId`.
2. Wait only for its creation dependencies.
3. Flush its latest completed edits.
4. Acquire that Card’s publication barrier.
5. Re-evaluate eligibility from the confirmed saved state.
6. Publish with its confirmed revision and optional note.
7. Accept the Card publication acknowledgement.
8. Release the barrier.

Do not save the Deck or another Card.

If edits arrive during the request, retain them as a subsequent draft. They must not disappear when publication returns.

An uncertain publication response requires checking the expected immutable version/content before retrying. A stale revision alone is not proof that publication failed.

### E. Individual Deck Publish and warning

1. Flush Deck content and outstanding structural creation dependencies.
2. Do **not** flush unrelated Card drafts.
3. Check first-title eligibility if necessary.
4. Resolve the **exact saved** ordered Card references.
5. Require a published version for every reference.
6. Prepare publication information for those published versions.
7. Determine whether a warning is needed.
8. Confirm when required, then publish through the repository transaction.

The warning set is the union of:

- referenced Cards with saved outstanding drafts;
- referenced Cards with known pending local changes not represented in their published content;
- referenced Cards with known failed local changes not represented there.

The Creator DTO needs each Card’s latest published baseline to make this comparison accurately. `resolveCreatorDeck()` already fetches latest versions, but currently returns only the effective draft-or-published content.

**Suggested message**

> One or more Cards have unpublished changes. Publish this Deck using their current published versions anyway?

List affected positional Card labels, optionally with titles. No embedded editors or extra publication wizard.

**Authoritative server check**

Add a read-only publication preparation result and checked publication input containing:

- Deck revision;
- ordered Card references;
- referenced published versions;
- relevant Card revisions/draft state.

The publish transaction recomputes and validates this snapshot.

If the Deck composition or referenced publication state changed, return a structured “review again” response without writing a version. The client also invalidates confirmation if its relevant local edit generations change while the modal is open.

The server cannot independently know failed, unsaved browser edits. That part must remain a client check.

The publication transaction’s snapshot is the final consistency point. A later Card publication does not invalidate the immutable Deck version already created.

**Cancellation** cancels publication, not previously completed draft saves.

### F. Publish and leave

Retain independent publication transactions:

1. Flush relevant Deck/Card queues.
2. Check known first-publication/reference failures before starting publication.
3. Publish outstanding eligible Cards individually.
4. Publish the outstanding Deck.
5. Navigate only when the requested work is complete.

If a later operation fails:

- keep earlier immutable versions;
- remain in Creator;
- retain notes for outstanding operations;
- retry only outstanding work.

Do not add a “publish subset of Deck references” fallback.

If the Deck is clean and only Cards changed, publish the Cards and leave without manufacturing a Deck version.

If new Card edits appear during orchestration, either they remain outstanding and prevent claiming complete success, or the Deck warning is presented where appropriate. Never silently treat them as included.

### G. Removal during persistence

On removal:

- remove the reference from local Deck composition immediately;
- enqueue Deck persistence;
- mark the Card detached in the coordinator;
- retain its desired content, request, revision and retry state;
- continue pending Card saves independently.

After retry exhaustion, suppress failure UI for that detached Card and retain a clear code TODO for future recovery.

Current whole-board snapshots cannot provide this safely: later saves iterate only current Deck Cards, and the route rejects detached Cards.

If removal happens before Add completes, finish the ordered Add transaction and then detach. This preserves the intentionally created independent Card. Do not cancel only one side of creation.

### H. Positional numbering

The first-class persistence path is already correct:

- `DeckContent.cards` contains ordered Card IDs.
- `CardContent` does not accept a label field.
- `layoutCardLabels()` derives labels from position.
- `cardVersionAtPublish` is historical version information, not positional identity.

Retain this.

Fix the separate UI identity issue:

- `deleteCreatorCard()` renumbers `column.id`.
- Creator sections use `key={column.id}`.
- Introduction uploads use those IDs to identify their completion target.

A Card upload started in column 2 can finish after deletion renumbers columns and target the wrong Card. Use stable Card identity for async targeting, component keys and edit-session identity; grid coordinates can remain positional.

There is also a prefix inconsistency: Creator layout hardcodes `"Card"` while working layout uses Deck metadata. New Decks should default to `"Card"`; existing persisted metadata should not be rewritten merely by opening Creator.

### I. Zero-Card support

The exact required changes are small:

- Remove both final-Card deletion guards.
- Preserve the Themes column and Add Card control with no Card columns.
- Clear any selected edit/drag target belonging to a removed Card.
- Guard focus and navigation against an absent Card.
- Avoid producing active index `-1` through “next” navigation.
- Render `FocusedCardView` only when the selected Card exists.
- Leave the Card area empty instead of showing an empty Card-stack scene.

Already safe:

- `assertDeckContent()` accepts `cards: []`.
- Deck publication’s `every()` prerequisite accepts zero references.
- Creator and version resolvers handle empty reference arrays.
- `openWorkingDeck()` creates no CardData and sets `activeCardId: null`.
- Progress on an empty Step set is `0`.
- Empty confidence resolves to no confidence value.
- My Decks thumbnails map an empty array and Card count is zero.
- Migration’s first-Card fallback uses optional access.

The first successful working open still establishes the cadence anchor, even with zero Cards. Preserve the settled anchor rule; later opens must not reset it.

## 7. Authorization/media implications

`CARD_OUTSIDE_DECK` has two materially different uses.

| Operation | Recommended authorization |
|---|---|
| Canonical Card read/save | Authenticated Card owner; revision required for mutation. No Deck membership requirement. |
| Canonical Card publication | Card owner, revision and publication rules. No Deck membership requirement. |
| Add/attach/remove reference | Deck owner and Deck revision; validate referenced Cards. |
| Construction-time cross-Card Step move | Keep Deck membership, both Card ownership checks, all revisions and never-published/fork restrictions. |
| Personal CardData mutation | Keep adopted working-Deck context and personal-data ownership. |
| Personal media upload | Keep `authorizeWorkingCard()` and current metadata validation. |
| Canonical instructional upload | Preserve the current valid Deck-context authorization where used; require the target Card’s owner. |
| Video status | Preserve the persisted-media asset membership check; never authorize arbitrary asset IDs from ownership alone. |

The nested canonical mutation route’s `CARD_OUTSIDE_DECK` should go. The same error in `moveConstructionStep()` should remain: that operation genuinely involves a particular Deck and two referenced Cards.

Removing the nested route guard alone is insufficient because the route first loads the entire Deck via `creatorDTO()`. Introduce a Card-owned endpoint/resolver rather than retaining an unnecessary prerequisite that can fail because of another Card.

For uploads:

- Replace whole-board pre-upload persistence with the required target creation/save dependency.
- Capture stable Card/Step identity before starting the upload.
- Complete metadata saves through the Card lane.
- A Card A upload must not globally disable unrelated Card B publication.
- A Deck introduction upload concerns the Deck lane.
- Preserve trusted existing media, current object keys and strict validation of new uploads.
- Keep abandoned/replaced video deletion in the deferred cleanup TODO.

No Cloudflare delivery or privacy redesign is needed.

---

## 8. My Drafts plan

Use **Deck ownership and persisted Creator work**, not DeckData, to determine the list.

Minimal proposed response:

```ts
{
  deckTemplateId: string;
  title: string;
}
```

Server-side timestamps can order results without becoming additional UI.

The modal should:

- open from a small Creator-area control;
- fetch an authenticated, non-cached list;
- display Deck titles as reopen actions;
- show simple loading, empty and failure states;
- navigate to `/creator/edit/{deckTemplateId}`.

Do not create content merely by opening the modal.

For the inclusion policy approved in Question 1:

- Never-published persisted roots qualify.
- Outstanding Deck drafts can qualify directly.
- Card-only work requires inspecting Cards referenced by the effective Creator composition.
- Never expose another owner’s private draft.
- Clean published content does not become a “draft” merely because it is owned.

Existing owner indexes are sufficient to begin with; do not introduce an index deployment requirement without evidence.

### Keep membership separate

Retain existing null-adoption DeckData as bookkeeping, but filter it out before constructing My Decks display records.

This avoids:

- creating personal state just because My Drafts was opened;
- changing publication’s “advance existing personal data only” contract;
- rewriting existing null-adoption records;
- confusing archival with canonical ownership.

On first Deck publication, existing DeckData adopts version 1 and the Deck can appear in My Decks if not archived.

### Editor switching requires explicit identity

`CreatorDragLab` initializes its board and persistence instance with `useState()` initializers. It does not reset them when another Deck’s props arrive.

The edit route should key the editor by Deck ID or provide an explicit, tested session transition. Otherwise My Drafts navigation between two edit URLs risks retaining the previous Deck’s board and queue.

Detached background save jobs must not depend on a Card column remaining mounted.

## 10. Recommended implementation sequence

I recommend **three implementation prompts with review checkpoints**, containing these small coherent commits. One large session is possible, but creates unnecessary risk around recovery and publication races.

| Step | Goal and areas | Dependencies/testing | Main risk and useful browser check |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Shared lifecycle rules | Defaults module, publication helpers, zero-Card factories, fallback decisions. | Unit tests; typecheck. | Accidentally rewriting loaded content. Open old drafts and new blank Creator. |
| 2. Entity and transaction boundaries | Card-owned endpoint/resolver; atomic Add; repository publication validation. | Real Mongo integration tests. | Partial creation or weakened authorization. HTTP/integration checks matter more than manual UI here. |
| 3. Persistence coordinator | Per-entity desired/acknowledged state, structured errors, retries, creation barriers, uncertain-response recovery. | Controlled unit races plus Mongo tests. | Stale writes or cross-entity coupling. Test offline/recovery in one browser session. |
| 4. Creator autosave integration | Edit classification, removal, delete-final guard, remove Save Draft, stable async identities. | Unit and browser tests. | Losing edits during detach or targeting another Card’s upload. Manually Add/edit/remove rapidly. |
| 5. Scoped publication | Card/Deck flush, warning preparation/confirmation, recoverable Publish and leave. | Repository and browser race tests. | Wrong composition/version or duplicate publication. Exercise warning and partial failure. |
| 6. Draft discovery and membership | Approved My Drafts list/modal; null-adoption exclusion; editor session reset. | Integration/browser tests. | State leakage between edit routes. Switch repeatedly between two drafts. |
| 7. Empty working UI and compatibility | Focus/navigation guards, empty Card area, fixture updates, compatibility regression coverage. | Full verification commands. | Empty-view crash or responsive regression. Open zero-Card Deck on mobile and desktop. |

Suggested prompt boundaries:

1. **Rules and backend contracts:** Steps 1–2.
2. **Autosave and scoped publication:** Steps 3–5.
3. **My Drafts, empty working UI and full verification:** Steps 6–7.

Each prompt should repeat the locked scope exclusions and stop for review before the next. Do not mix production migration or public workflows into any of them.

## 11. Risks / regressions to guard against

| Risk | Concrete cause in current code | Guard |
|---|---|---|
| Lost or overwritten edits | Whole-board captured snapshots and full-DTO refreshes | Per-entity desired/acknowledged generations; never replace newer local content |
| Half-completed Add | Separate Card creation and Deck save | Single transaction |
| Duplicate creation/publication after timeout | HTTP outcome can be uncertain despite successful transaction | Stable IDs, immutable command snapshots and read-before-retry reconciliation |
| Detached save failure | Nested route requires current Deck membership | Card-owned mutation boundary and coordinator-held detached jobs |
| Media attached to wrong Card | Introduction callbacks use renumbered column IDs | Stable Card identity throughout upload lifecycle |
| Accidental default publication | Root existence/non-null draft currently drives cues | Shared eligibility helpers and repository enforcement |
| Silent loss on My Drafts switch | Component state initialized once; no switch guard | Explicit editor identity plus approved pending-save navigation policy |
| Wrong publication warning | Client sees local edits; server sees persisted drafts | Combine both sources and revalidate confirmation |
| Deck/Card coupling returns | Global busy/upload/save state | Entity-specific status and dependency barriers |
| Empty Deck crash | Focused view indexes Cards without existence guard | Empty navigation/focus guards and browser coverage |
| Existing content silently normalized | New defaults applied while loading old content | Defaults for creation/fallback only; preserve loaded values |
| My Drafts becomes membership | Reusing DeckData as draft-list authority | Separate ownership/work query from adopted membership |
| Step reservation regression | New queues ignore the three-entity move transaction | Dedicated barrier for Deck/source/destination; retain repository transaction |
| Responsive UI regresses again | Additional controls expand Creator header | Reuse compact controls/modals and existing mobile geometry tests |

One limitation should remain explicit: bounded browser retries cannot guarantee persistence after the tab/process is closed. This plan does not introduce durable offline storage. Attached failures remain visible; detached exhausted failures follow the agreed temporary silent policy.

---

## 12. Whether the architecture is now ready for implementation

**READY AFTER CLARIFICATIONS.**

There is no need for a new canonical schema, persisted `initialBaseline`, production migration or redesign of Phase 1.

The remaining decisions are limited to:

1. My Drafts inclusion of published Deck/Card-only work and archival interaction.
2. Previously published Card title-clearing fallback.
3. Completion of uploads after Card removal.
4. Switching drafts when visible edits cannot be saved.

The defaults, repository boundaries, atomic Add operation and queue design can be implemented independently of most of those answers. The highest-risk work is the persistence/publication coordinator; it should receive its own implementation and review checkpoint.

> Please implement only **Steps 1–2** from the Astra architecture plan:
>
> 1. Shared lifecycle rules
> 2. Entity and transaction boundaries
>
> Do not proceed into the persistence coordinator, Creator autosave integration, scoped publication UI/orchestration, My Drafts UI, or empty working-view UI yet.
>
> This is the first implementation checkpoint. I want a clean backend/foundation change that we can review before the higher-risk persistence coordinator work.
>

>

>
> Implement a shared client/server-safe defaults module, likely along the lines of:
>
> `src/lib/cards/creatorDefaults.ts`
>
> Centralize creation defaults such as:
>
> - Deck default title: `My Next Path`
> - Card default intro title: `My Next Card`
> - Theme defaults
> - default cadence
> - default Card label prefix
>
> Use pure factories where appropriate, with caller-supplied IDs.
>
> Do not rewrite existing persisted content merely because these defaults change.
>
> Existing published Decks/Cards and existing saved drafts must retain their stored content.
>
> New Creator Decks must use the new zero-Card default.
>
> New Cards must use `My Next Card`.
>

>

>

>

> #### Previously published Deck
> Clearing the title restores the latest published nonblank Deck title.
>
> If no usable published title exists, fall back to `My Next Path`.
>
> #### Previously published Card
> Clearing the Card intro title restores the latest published nonblank Card title.
>
> If no usable published title exists, fall back to `My Next Card`.

> ### F. Atomic Add Card backend operation
>
> Implement the repository/backend operation for **atomic create-and-attach** of a Card to an already-persisted Deck.

## 3. Backend/API contracts

**Canonical Card boundary**

```text
GET   /api/card-templates/{cardTemplateId}
PATCH /api/card-templates/{cardTemplateId}
```

PATCH accepts the existing `save` or `publish` operation with revision, content or optional update note. Authorization comes from Card ownership. Responses include the Card root, effective content and latest published baseline.

**Atomic Add**

```text
POST /api/deck-templates/{deckTemplateId}/cards
```

Body:

```ts
{
  revision,
  cardTemplateId,
  stepIds,
  content // proposed Deck content
}
```

The transaction creates the default Card, reserves its Steps, attaches its reference and increments the Deck revision. It returns scoped Deck and Card acknowledgements.

Exact repeated commands return the existing acknowledgement. Ambiguous recovery produces `ADD_CARD_RECOVERY_CONFLICT`; reservation collisions produce `STEP_RESERVATION_CONFLICT`.

The old nested Card mutation endpoint returns **410 before authentication or database lookup**.

> \# 1. Per-entity persistence coordinator\
> \
> Replace the current global/whole-board save orchestration with a coordinator that manages persistence independently for:\
> \
> \- the Deck;\
> \- each Card, keyed by stable \`cardTemplateId\`.\
> \
> Do not key persistence state by positional column IDs.\
> \
> Each entity lane should distinguish at least:\
> \
> \- latest desired local content;\
> \- last acknowledged saved content;\
> \- last acknowledged revision;\
> \- latest published baseline where relevant;\
> \- local edit generation;\
> \- acknowledged generation;\
> \- in-flight request;\
> \- retry state;\
> \- structured failure/conflict;\
> \- creation dependency;\
> \- publication state.\
> \
> These should remain client operational state.\
> \
> Do not add persisted queue/readiness fields.\
> \
> \## Required queue behaviour\
> \
> For each Deck/Card lane:\
> \
> 1\. Only one save request may be in flight for that entity.\
> 2\. Multiple local edits while a save is running should coalesce.\
> 3\. When a request succeeds:\
> &#x20;  \- update acknowledged content/revision;\
> &#x20;  \- do not overwrite newer local edits;\
> &#x20;  \- if newer desired content exists, save the newest state next.\
> 4\. Old responses must never replace newer local content.\
> 5\. Failure in Card A must not block Card B or the Deck.\
> 6\. Failure in the Deck must not block an independent Card save unless there is a genuine structural dependency.\
> 7\. Delayed retries must never replay stale content over newer edits.\
> \
> Use the existing revision model rather than inventing a second concurrency system.\
> \
> \---\
> \
> \# 2. Retry and failure model\
> \
> Implement bounded automatic retries for transient failures.\
> \
> Recommended sequence:\
> \
> \- immediate request;\
> \- retry after about 1 second;\
> \- retry after about 3 seconds;\
> \- retry after about 8 seconds.\
> \
> Use fake timers in unit tests.\
> \
> Differentiate:\
> \
> \### Transient failure\
> Examples: temporary network/server failure.\
> \
> \- retry automatically;\
> \- retry latest relevant desired state safely;\
> \- do not allow unlimited retry loops.\
> \
> \### Validation / authorization failure\
> \
> \- do not blindly retry;\
> \- retain local edits;\
> \- show entity-specific failure state.\
> \
> \### Genuine revision conflict\
> \
> \- stop automatic retries;\
> \- preserve the user’s local content;\
> \- do not overwrite remote state;\
> \- expose a structured conflict state.\
> \
> Do not silently “last write wins”.\
> \
> \### Uncertain outcome\
> \
> If a request may have committed but the response was lost:\
> \
> \- reconcile before retrying where the backend supports it;\
> \- do not assume failure merely because the response did not arrive;\
> \- use known stable IDs/revisions/content to determine the outcome.\
> \
> Prompt 1 introduced \`ADD_CARD_RECOVERY_CONFLICT\`.\
> \
> Treat this as a real recovery/conflict condition.\
> \
> Do NOT allocate replacement Card/Step IDs and do NOT blindly repeat attachment if the server cannot safely prove the state.\
> \
> \---\
> \
> \# 3. Add Card creation dependency\
> \
> Prompt 1 implemented atomic Card create + Deck attachment.\
> \
> Integrate it into the coordinator.\
> \
> When the user clicks Add Card:\
> \
> 1\. allocate stable \`cardTemplateId\` and Step IDs locally;\
> 2\. render immediately;\
> 3\. start the atomic Add command;\
> 4\. treat the Card as having a creation dependency until acknowledged.\
> \
> If the user edits that new Card immediately:\
> \
> \- capture the edits locally;\
> \- do not lose them;\
> \- queue them behind the Card creation acknowledgement;\
> \- after creation succeeds, save the latest desired Card content using the returned revision.\
> \
> Do not create a second Card identity.\
> \
> Deck structural changes after Add must serialize correctly behind the Add operation where required.\
> \
> Two rapid Add Card actions must not overwrite each other’s Deck composition.\
> \
> \---\
> \
> \# 4. Creator edit classification\
> \
> Refactor Creator save triggers so each completed edit saves only the relevant entity.\
> \
> Examples:\
> \
> \## Deck-scoped edits\
> \
> Save the Deck only:\
> \
> \- Deck title;\
> \- Deck introduction;\
> \- Themes;\
> \- cadence / Deck-level metadata;\
> \- Card order;\
> \- Card removal;\
> \- Card attachment structural changes.\
> \
> \## Card-scoped edits\
> \
> Save only the containing Card:\
> \
> \- Card intro title;\
> \- Card intro content/media metadata;\
> \- Step title;\
> \- Step description/content;\
> \- Step instructional media metadata;\
> \- other canonical Card content.\
> \
> Do not call whole-board save merely because one Card changed.\
> \
> Preserve existing multi-entity transactional behaviour for operations that genuinely require it, such as construction-time cross-Card Step transfer.\
> \
> Do not weaken Step reservation or move invariants.\
> \
> \---\
> \
> \# 5. Remove the top-level Save Draft button\
> \
> Remove the permanent top-level \`Save Draft\` control.\
> \
> Modal Save buttons remain.\
> \
> Their meaning is:\
> \
> \> apply the edit and close the modal\
> \
> The resulting completed edit should then autosave the relevant entity.\
> \
> Do not reintroduce permanent “Draft saved” or “Draft outstanding” labels.\
> \
> Autosave success feedback should remain subtle.\
> \
> \---\
> \
> \# 6. Entity-specific save failure UI\
> \
> After automatic retries are exhausted for an attached/visible entity:\
> \
> \- show a persistent but compact error for that entity;\
> \- expose a temporary \`Retry Save\` action;\
> \- Retry Save should retry the current latest desired state, not an obsolete snapshot.\
> \
> A failed Card save must not make every Card or the Deck look failed.\
> \
> A failed Deck save must not make unrelated Card controls unusable.\
> \
> \---\
> \
> \# 7. Removing a Card while Card save is pending\
> \
> Implement the locked V1 behaviour.\
> \
> When a Card is removed from the Deck:\
> \
> 1\. remove its reference from local Deck composition immediately;\
> 2\. enqueue/save the Deck structural change;\
> 3\. mark the Card as detached in the persistence coordinator;\
> 4\. allow the Card’s already-pending or queued save to continue independently.\
> \
> Do not cancel its save because the Card column disappears.\
> \
> If that detached Card save succeeds:\
> \- preserve its independent CardTemplate edits.\
> \
> If automatic retries ultimately fail:\
> \- fail silently for the detached Card;\
> \- do not display special recovery UI after it has disappeared;\
> \- add a clear TODO for future detached-Card recovery.\
> \
> Do not delete the CardTemplate.\
> \
> If removal happens before Add Card creation has completed:\
> \- allow the ordered Add transaction to resolve first;\
> \- then detach the Card;\
> \- do not cancel only one half of creation.\
> \
> \---\
> \
> \# 8. Stable Card identity in Creator UI and async callbacks\
> \
> Astra found a real identity bug.\
> \
> Current positional column IDs may be renumbered after Card removal and are used in:\
> \
> \- React keys;\
> \- some edit/session targeting;\
> \- introduction upload callbacks.\
> \
> Fix this in this prompt.\
> \
> Use stable \`cardTemplateId\` for:\
> \
> \- React identity where Card identity is intended;\
> \- asynchronous upload completion targeting;\
> \- Card edit-session targeting;\
> \- persistence lane identity.\
> \
> Positional column/grid IDs may still be used purely for layout/order.\
> \
> Do not persist labels such as \`Card 3\` as identity.\
> \
> Card labels remain positional and derived from Deck composition.\
> \
> Ensure an upload started for Card A cannot finish on Card B after columns are renumbered.\
> \
> \---\
> \
> \# 9. Upload integration with scoped persistence\
> \
> Do not redesign storage/security.\
> \
> Preserve the authorization model from Prompt 1.\
> \
> But remove whole-board persistence as an upload side effect.\
> \
> For Card instructional uploads:\
> \
> \- capture stable Card/Step identity before upload;\
> \- ensure any necessary Card creation/save dependency is satisfied;\
> \- on upload completion, update/save only that Card;\
> \- unrelated Cards and Deck publication should not become globally blocked by the upload.\
> \
> For Deck introduction uploads:\
> \- use the Deck persistence lane.\
> \
> If a Card is removed during an already-authorized upload:\
> \
> Locked behaviour:\
> \
> \- let the upload complete;\
> \- attach/save its metadata to the original independent Card by stable \`cardTemplateId\`;\
> \- do not attach it to another Card;\
> \- do not keep the removed Card visible merely because upload is still running.\
> \
> Keep existing abandoned/replaced video cleanup as a later TODO.\
