> \
> \# 10. Publication cues\
> \
> Update the Creator UI so Publish buttons reflect the agreed publication rules and confirmed saved state.\
> \
> A new default Card should NOT immediately show an active/dark Publish button merely because its root/draft exists.\
> \
> For a Card, distinguish:\
> \
> \- local dirty;\
> \- saved outstanding;\
> \- publishable;\
> \- publication in progress;\
> \- failed/conflicted.\
> \
> For a never-published Card:\
> \
> Publish active only when confirmed saved content satisfies the first-publication rule.\
> \
> For an already-published Card:\
> \
> Publish active when confirmed saved draft differs from latest published version.\
> \
> Likewise for Decks:\
> \
> \- first-title rule;\
> \- referenced Cards must each have at least one published version;\
> \- zero Cards is valid;\
> \- later publication based on confirmed Deck draft vs published Deck version.\
> \
> Do not use \`!dto\`, root existence, or merely \`draft !== null\` as sufficient UI readiness.\
> \
> The server remains authoritative.\
> \
> \---\
> \
> \# 11. Scoped Card Publish\
> \
> Replace whole-board pre-publication saving.\
> \
> When the user publishes a Card:\
> \
> 1\. identify it by \`cardTemplateId\`;\
> 2\. wait only for its creation dependency if needed;\
> 3\. flush only that Card’s latest completed local edits;\
> 4\. wait for that Card save acknowledgement;\
> 5\. re-evaluate publication eligibility from confirmed saved state;\
> 6\. publish that Card;\
> 7\. accept the publication acknowledgement;\
> 8\. update its published baseline/revision/draft state.\
> \
> Do not save:\
> \
> \- the Deck;\
> \- another Card;\
> \- unrelated drafts.\
> \
> An unrelated failed Card/Deck save must not block Card publication.\
> \
> If the user edits the same Card while publication is running:\
> \
> \- do not lose those edits;\
> \- publication should represent the confirmed content that was published;\
> \- newer edits should remain as subsequent outstanding draft content after the publish response.\
> \
> Handle uncertain publication outcome safely.\
> \
> Do not create duplicate immutable Card versions after a lost response/retry.\
> \
> \---\
> \
> \# 12. Scoped Deck Publish\
> \
> When publishing the Deck:\
> \
> 1\. flush only Deck content and necessary structural Add dependencies;\
> 2\. do not flush unrelated Card drafts;\
> 3\. verify Deck eligibility;\
> 4\. resolve the exact saved ordered Card references;\
> 5\. verify each referenced Card has a published version;\
> 6\. determine whether unpublished-Card-change warning is required;\
> 7\. confirm if necessary;\
> 8\. publish the Deck using the exact saved composition.\
> \
> Do not silently publish Card drafts.\
> \
> Do not create a subset Deck version.\
> \
> \---\
> \
> \# 13. Warning when Cards have unpublished changes\
> \
> Before Deck publication, warn if any currently referenced Card has changes that will not be represented by the Card version used in the Deck publication.\
> \
> The warning set should include:\
> \
> \- Card has a saved outstanding draft;\
> \- Card has known pending local edits;\
> \- Card has known failed local edits.\
> \
> Do not automatically flush or publish those Card edits merely because Deck Publish was clicked.\
> \
> Suggested minimal message:\
> \
> \> One or more Cards have unpublished changes. Publish this Deck using their current published versions anyway?\
> \
> Keep the UX minimal.\
> \
> Optionally list affected positional Card labels/titles if straightforward.\
> \
> Actions:\
> \
> \- Cancel\
> \- Publish anyway\
> \
> This is a warning, not a block.\
> \
> \## Confirmation safety\
> \
> Do not let the warning confirmation become stale.\
> \
> The confirmed publication state should be tied to relevant authoritative data such as:\
> \
> \- Deck revision;\
> \- exact ordered Card references;\
> \- Card published versions being used;\
> \- relevant Card draft/revision state.\
> \
> If any material publication state changes while the warning is open:\
> \- invalidate confirmation;\
> \- require review again rather than silently publishing a different state.\
> \
> The server should perform an authoritative recheck.\
> \
> The server cannot know unsaved browser-only failed/pending edits, so combine:\
> \- server persisted state;\
> \- client coordinator state.\
> \
> \---\
> \
> \# 14. Publish and leave\
> \
> Preserve the existing concept of independent publication transactions.\
> \
> Refactor its orchestration to use scoped persistence lanes.\
> \
> Expected flow:\
> \
> 1\. flush relevant entity queues;\
> 2\. identify outstanding publication work;\
> 3\. publish Cards individually where required;\
> 4\. publish Deck if required;\
> 5\. navigate only when requested work has completed.\
> \
> If one publication succeeds and a later one fails:\
> \
> \- keep the successful immutable version;\
> \- remain in Creator;\
> \- do not roll back success;\
> \- retry only remaining work.\
> \
> Do not re-run already successful publications.\
> \
> If the Deck itself is clean but Cards have publication work:\
> \- publish relevant Cards;\
> \- do not manufacture a new Deck version.\
> \
> If Card edits occur during the process:\
> \- do not silently claim everything is complete if newer work remains outstanding.\
> \
> For the Deck warning:\
> \- after required Card publications complete, check warning state again;\
> \- do not warn about Card drafts that Publish and leave has just successfully published.\
> \
> \---\

> That operation genuinely involves:\

Implemented **Steps 3–5 only**. Prompt 3 work remains untouched. Nothing was committed, and production Atlas was not accessed.

**1. Executive summary**

Creator now uses independent Deck/Card persistence lanes, scoped autosaving and scoped publication. The top-level Save Draft button is removed. Independent publication, stable identities, Step reservations and existing adoption semantics are preserved.

Verification is green except for pre-existing lint failures and three obsolete browser journeys detailed below.

**2. Persistence coordinator**

The new coordinator maintains operational state separately for the Deck and each `cardTemplateId`: desired content, acknowledged content/revision, edit generations, creation dependencies, retries, failures, publication and uncertain outcomes.

Each lane permits one save request at a time. Edits coalesce, older responses acknowledge their captured content without replacing newer edits, and unrelated lanes continue independently.

Construction-time Step transfers retain an explicit three-entity barrier and the existing atomic backend operation.

**3. Files changed**

These are changes from this checkpoint; existing staged work was preserved.

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| [creatorPersistenceCoordinator.ts](./src/components/creator/creatorPersistenceCoordinator.ts) | New entity lanes, creation dependencies, recovery and publication orchestration |
| [creatorRequest.ts](./src/components/creator/creatorRequest.ts) | Shared transport with structured errors and request timeout |
| [CreatorDragLab.tsx](./src/components/creator/CreatorDragLab.tsx) | Scoped autosaves/publication, stable targeting, warnings and failure UI |
| [cardArchitectureAdapter.ts](./src/components/creator/cardArchitectureAdapter.ts) | Removed obsolete whole-board persistence orchestration |
| [creatorBoardState.ts](./src/components/creator/creatorBoardState.ts) | Allows final Card removal |
| [AppShell.tsx](./src/components/layout/AppShell.tsx) | Uses extracted transport |
| [globals.css](./src/app/globals.css) | Compact, bounded Creator error feedback |
| [model.ts](./src/lib/cards/model.ts) | Ephemeral publication-review contract; no persisted fields |
| [repository.ts](./src/lib/cards/repository.ts) | Publication preparation and transactional confirmation recheck |
| [Card route](./src/app/api/card-templates/[cardTemplateId]/route.ts) | Owner-authorized immutable-version receipt retrieval |
| [Deck publication route](./src/app/api/deck-templates/[deckTemplateId]/publish/route.ts) | Review preparation, confirmation validation and receipt retrieval |
| [test-phase2.ts](./scripts/test-phase2.ts) | Optional browser-test selection |
| [creator-coordinator.test.ts](./tests/creator-coordinator.test.ts) | New coordinator unit/race tests |
| [creator-lifecycle.integration.ts](./tests/creator-lifecycle.integration.ts) | Real Mongo recovery and publication tests |
| [creator-coordinator.browser.ts](./tests/phase2/creator-coordinator.browser.ts) | New Creator browser journeys |
| [phase2.test.ts](./tests/phase2.test.ts) | Replaced obsolete whole-board assertions |
| [private-deck.browser.ts](./tests/phase2/private-deck.browser.ts) | Corrected authorization fixture; made obsolete journey failures explicit |

**4. Autosave behaviour**

Completed Deck edits save the Deck lane. Card/Step edits save their containing Card lane. Modal Save still applies the edit and closes.

Opening an untouched Creator session performs no writes. There are no permanent “Draft saved” or “Draft outstanding” labels.

**5. Retry, conflict and recovery**

Transient saves receive bounded retries after approximately **1, 3 and 8 seconds**. Retries reconcile uncertain outcomes and use the latest safe desired content.

Validation/authorization failures stop automatic retries. Revision and recovery conflicts preserve local content and stop blind retries.

Visible failed entities receive compact, entity-specific feedback. Retry Save uses their latest desired content. Conflicts do not offer an overwrite retry.

Uncertain publication recovery checks the root and immutable version receipt, including content and update note, before accepting success.

**6. Add Card dependencies**

Add renders immediately with stable caller-supplied IDs.

For an unsaved Deck, creation uses the existing graph transaction. For persisted Decks, Add uses atomic create-and-attach. Structural commands serialize; immediate Card edits wait for creation acknowledgement and then save using the returned revision.

Rapid Adds preserve both references. Recovery conflicts retain the original IDs.

**7. Detached Cards**

Removal immediately changes local composition and saves the Deck reference change. The Card lane remains alive, including pending saves and retries.

Detached failures remain hidden. A TODO records the deferred recovery UI. Card roots, versions and personal data are not deleted.

**8. Stable identity and uploads**

Card React keys, edit sessions, upload callbacks and persistence lanes use `cardTemplateId`.

Uploads complete against their original Card even after renumbering or detachment. Metadata saves only that Card. Already-authorized detached uploads can finish after SPA navigation.

Step transfers and uploads cannot overlap for the participating Cards; upload authorization also rechecks the Step’s Card after waiting for persistence.

Storage/security boundaries were not redesigned.

**9. Scoped Card Publish**

Card Publish waits for its creation dependency and flushes only that Card. It evaluates confirmed saved state, publishes independently and updates its baseline.

Newer edits remain subsequent draft work. Unrelated save failures do not block publication.

**10. Scoped Deck Publish**

Deck Publish flushes only Deck content and structural dependencies. It uses exact saved composition and requires published versions for all referenced Cards.

It neither flushes nor publishes unrelated Card drafts.

**11. Warning flow**

Deck publication combines authoritative saved Card state with known local pending/failed changes.

The warning offers **Cancel** and **Publish anyway**. Confirmation is invalidated by material client changes, and the server transaction rechecks Deck revision, ordered references and Card revisions/published versions.

Stale confirmation creates no Deck version.

**12. Publish and leave**

The aggregate flow flushes relevant lanes, publishes Cards independently, then publishes the Deck when needed.

Earlier successes survive later failures. Retry skips completed publications. Card-only publication does not manufacture a Deck version, and navigation waits until outstanding work is complete.

I inspected committed baseline `7823b28`. The working tree is clean. No files or database records were changed.

**1. Recommended scope**

I agree with your four proposed areas:

- A small Creator-only My Drafts modal backed by an authenticated, read-only query.
- My Decks filtering based on published adoption, while retaining existing null-adoption DeckData.
- Safe rendering and navigation for zero-Card working Decks.
- Updated browser journeys using explicit Add Card actions, autosave acknowledgements and independent publication.

The persistence coordinator should remain the foundation. This stage needs a small navigation wrapper around it, rather than another persistence redesign.

**2. What currently needs changing**

| Area | Current behaviour | Required change |
|---|---|---|
| My Drafts | No resolver, API or UI exists. | Add the minimal ownership-based draft list and Creator modal. |
| My Decks | `membershipDTO()` returns null-adoption records; `AppShell` explicitly renders “— Draft” tiles. | Filter out null adoption before resolving/rendering membership records. |
| Archived Decks | The archived list also accepts unpublished membership records. | Apply the same published-adoption filter to active and archived displays. |
| Draft switching | Creator state and its coordinator are initialized once. Existing navigation handles only the return link. | Save safely before switching and explicitly initialize fresh state for the selected Deck identity. |
| Zero-Card working view | Data resolution is safe, but the Card scene still renders its table, atmosphere and fixed scene height. Navigation assumes an initial index of `0`. | Render an empty Card area and guard activation, traversal and focus. |
| Browser journeys | Three legacy cases still require starter Cards or Save Draft. Further obsolete assertions are currently hidden behind those initial failures. | Rewrite the full journey and consolidate duplicate mobile coverage. |

The My Decks issue is specifically in [readModels.ts:55](./src/lib/cards/readModels.ts:55) and [AppShell.tsx:66](./src/components/layout/AppShell.tsx:66). Ownership fallback is already absent; we should preserve that.

Filtering must **not delete null-adoption DeckData**. `createPrivateGraph()` creates it, and Deck publication advances that existing adoption. Removing those records would break the established publisher flow.

A published adopted Deck should remain in My Decks even when its Deck or Cards have newer drafts. The working tile and opening flow must continue using adopted versions.

**3. My Drafts and safe switching**

The list should derive from canonical Deck ownership/content, independently of DeckData. Otherwise drafts without membership could disappear, and personal archiving would become confused with Creator ownership.

The minimal implementation would:

- Fetch on opening the modal.
- Return identifiers, stored titles and minimal metadata—not complete Cards, personal state or media.
- Use the existing owner index and batched Card/version reads where needed.
- Reopen through `/creator/edit/{deckTemplateId}`, retaining server-side ownership validation.
- Never create persistence merely to populate the list.
- Keep detached standalone Card drafts outside this Deck-focused entry point.

Do not use publication eligibility as list eligibility: an unfinished Deck with its default title still needs to be discoverable.

There are two important switching details in [CreatorDragLab.tsx:973](./src/components/creator/CreatorDragLab.tsx:973):

1. `board`, `canonical` and the coordinator are initialized through `useState`. The edit page should explicitly key Creator by Deck identity so switching cannot reuse the previous session’s coordinator.
2. Unmount currently aborts attached uploads, while authorized detached uploads continue. Safe switching therefore needs to wait for attached uploads and saves before navigation.

A narrow navigation preparation method can reuse the coordinator’s existing upload wait and `flushAll()`. Failures should retain the current board and its local edits. Selecting the currently open Deck should simply close the list.

A switch should also avoid carrying Deck A’s `returnDeckId` into Deck B. The existing plain edit route already defaults its return destination to My Decks.

**QUESTION FOR USER — What belongs in My Drafts?**

These cases are not fully settled:

| Persisted work | Recommendation |
|---|---|
| Never-published Deck with a saved draft | Include |
| Published Deck with an outstanding Deck draft | Include |
| Published Deck whose only outstanding work is in currently referenced, owned Cards | Include |
| Entirely clean published Deck | Exclude |

Including Card-only work best matches “unfinished Creator Deck work,” but requires examining referenced Card roots as well as the Deck root.

I also recommend keeping this list independent of personal `archivedAt`: archiving an adopted Deck should not make its canonical unfinished work undiscoverable.

**QUESTION FOR USER — How should selecting another draft behave?**

Two reasonable options are:

- Save pending work automatically, then switch without publishing.
- Reuse the existing leave dialog, offering saved-draft navigation or Publish and leave.

I recommend automatic **save and switch**, waiting for attached uploads and blocking the switch on unresolved save failures/conflicts. No discard option is needed for this minimal stage.

These choices affect the list query and switching interaction; the filtering and empty-view work can proceed independently.

**4. Zero-Card support and hidden dependencies**

The backend already supports empty Decks:

- Creator/working resolvers return empty Card arrays.
- Publication accepts zero references once the first-title rule passes.
- `openWorkingDeck()` creates no CardData and stores `activeCardId: null`.
- Progress returns `0`; confidence returns `null`.
- Card labels derive safely from empty ordered composition.

The remaining assumptions are concentrated in [DeckDetail.tsx:185](./src/components/decks/DeckDetail.tsx:185):

- Initial active index falls back to `0`, even without a Card.
- The final index becomes `-1`.
- Navigation can schedule an invalid transition if invoked.
- Focus rendering passes `cards[activeCardIndex]` without checking that it exists.
- Mutation permission uses `every()`, which is true for an empty array; it cannot substitute for checking an active Card.

The narrow fix is to derive `hasCards`/`activeCard`, guard navigation and focus, and omit the Card scene when empty. Keep the Deck heading, introduction, edit menu, archive and Back controls available.

[CardStack.tsx:309](./src/components/decks/CardStack.tsx:309) currently renders scene decoration even when its Card mapping is empty. Avoid mounting that scene for zero Cards; do not manufacture a placeholder Card.

[DeckTile.tsx](./src/components/decks/DeckTile.tsx) already displays zero count safely and retains its Open action. Its mini-Card preview becomes empty. No thumbnail redesign is necessary.

One consequential existing rule: opening an empty working Deck still establishes its one-time cadence anchor. Adding Cards later therefore uses that original anchor. This follows the agreed anchor contract and should be tested, not reset.

**5. Files and implementation sequence**

I recommend four reviewable steps:

1. **Read-model separation**
   - Update `membershipDTO()` and its type.
   - Remove draft tiles and Creator-opening branches from `AppShell`.
   - Add a dedicated draft-list resolver/read model and authenticated GET route, for example `/api/creator/drafts`.
   - Preserve all membership, adoption and sharing records.

2. **My Drafts and navigation**
   - Add a small `CreatorDraftsModal.tsx`.
   - Integrate its entry point into Creator’s existing bounded header.
   - Add a narrow navigation-preparation method to [creatorPersistenceCoordinator.ts](./src/components/creator/creatorPersistenceCoordinator.ts).
   - Key Creator in the [edit page](./src/app/creator/edit/[deckTemplateId]/page.tsx).
   - Preserve independent saves, detached background work and publication behaviour.

3. **Empty working view**
   - Add guards in `DeckDetail`.
   - Conditionally omit the scene.
   - Retain existing progress/confidence semantics and nullable persisted active identity.
   - Avoid broad animation/CSS changes.

4. **Browser journey repair**
   - Rewrite [private-deck.browser.ts](./tests/phase2/private-deck.browser.ts).
   - Explicitly add and rename Cards.
   - Await autosave acknowledgement instead of clicking Save Draft.
   - Use canonical Card endpoints instead of nested mutation paths.
   - Replace “Publication saved” text assertions with response/persisted-state assertions.
   - Enter unfinished work through My Drafts.
   - Ensure simulated publication failures intercept POST, rather than the new preparation GET.
   - Consolidate old mobile cases with the passing Prompt 2 mobile coverage.

No production migration or persisted schema change is needed.

The test plan should specifically cover:

- Untouched Creator sessions absent from My Drafts.
- Saved drafts reopen with identical stable IDs/content.
- Null adoption excluded from both active and archived My Decks.
- Published adoption remains visible despite outstanding canonical drafts.
- Switching waits for saves/uploads and retains the current session on failure.
- Fresh coordinator state after switching between Decks.
- Empty Deck publication, opening, reload, archive/restore and later Card addition.
- Empty progress/confidence and no invalid focus/active mutation.
- The complete private Creator → working Deck → personal state → archive/restore journey.

Update the existing integration assertion that currently expects `membershipDTO()` to return `context: "creator"`. Keep its assertions proving null-adoption DeckData is retained.

The eventual verification should run the same full commands used for Prompt 2. The goal is a green broader Phase 2 browser suite without dropping its working-state, media, adoption and archive coverage. Existing unrelated lint failures remain separate.

> \## 3. My Decks must stop showing Creator drafts\
> \
> This is an explicit product requirement for this stage.\
> \
> My Decks should represent adopted/imported working Decks, not unfinished Creator work.\
> \
> Currently null-adoption Creator DeckData is still visible as draft tiles. Remove that from both:\
> \
> \- active My Decks;\
> \- archived My Decks.\
> \
> Important:\
> \
> \- do NOT delete null-adoption DeckData;\
> \- do NOT change the established publication/adoption flow;\
> \- do NOT make internal null-adoption state inaccessible if another part of the app legitimately needs it.\
> \
> Please inspect all callers before changing the semantics of shared functions such as \`membershipDTO()\`.\
> \
> If filtering at a narrower My Decks/read-model boundary is safer than changing a broadly-used helper, prefer that. If changing the helper is cleaner after checking its callers, that is also fine.\
> \
> Use your judgment based on the code.\
> \
> A published adopted Deck should remain in My Decks even if the Deck or its Cards have newer Creator drafts. The working tile/open flow should continue using the adopted version.\
> \
> \## 4. Zero-Card working Deck support\
> \
> Finish the remaining working-view UI assumptions for Decks with zero Cards.\
> \
> The backend/domain behaviour should already support this.\
> \
> Expected behaviour:\
> \
> \- zero Cards is valid;\
> \- working Deck can open;\
> \- \`activeCardId\` may be null;\
> \- progress should remain 0;\
> \- confidence should remain null/empty;\
> \- Card navigation/focus should not execute with invalid indices;\
> \- no fake placeholder Card should be created.\
> \
> The narrow visual expectation is:\
> \
> \- keep Deck heading/introduction and normal Deck-level controls;\
> \- omit the Card scene when there are no Cards;\
> \- keep archive/restore/back/edit behaviour available where appropriate.\
> \
> Please inspect \`DeckDetail\`, \`CardStack\`, related navigation/focus state and any other hidden assumptions.\
> \
> Use the smallest robust fix rather than broad animation/CSS changes.\
> \
> Preserve the current cadence-anchor contract:\
> opening an empty working Deck may establish the one-time cadence anchor, and later Card additions should not reset it.\
> \
> \## 5. Update obsolete Phase 2 browser journeys\
> \
> The three remaining Phase 2 failures currently rely on old assumptions:\
> \
> \- starter Cards already exist;\
> \- top-level Save Draft still exists.\
> \
> Update the broader journeys to match the new architecture.\
> \
> The tests should now use:\
> \
> \- explicit Add Card actions;\
> \- autosave acknowledgements rather than Save Draft;\
> \- current canonical Card endpoints/behaviour;\
> \- current independent publication flow;\
> \- My Drafts where unfinished Creator work should be reopened.\
> \
> Please inspect the tests carefully rather than mechanically replacing selectors.\
> \
> If some older mobile tests are now duplicate coverage, consolidation is fine, but do not reduce meaningful regression coverage just to make the suite green.\
> \
> If you remove or replace an old test, preserve its distinct useful assertions unless they are genuinely obsolete.\
> \
> The broader journey should still cover the important lifecycle:\
> \
> Creator\
> → save/autosave\
> → publication\
> → working Deck\
> → personal state\
> → archive/restore\
> \
> and relevant media/adoption behaviour that those tests were previously protecting.\
> \
> \## 6. My Drafts data/query considerations\
> \
> Please investigate the most efficient and correct way to derive unfinished work.\
> \
> Do not use publication eligibility itself as list eligibility.\
> \
> For example, a persisted never-published Deck still titled \`My Next Path\` should remain discoverable in My Drafts.\
> \
> For Card-only outstanding work, only currently referenced owned Cards should make the Deck appear.\
> \
> Avoid N+1 database behaviour if a batched/root-based query is straightforward, but do not overengineer this small list.\
> \
> Return minimal metadata only; do not load complete personal state/media merely to populate the modal.\
> \
> \## 7. Preserve recent architecture\
> \
> Do not regress any Prompt 1/2 behaviour:\
> \
> \- zero-Card Creator start;\
> \- \`My Next Path\`;\
> \- \`My Next Card\`;\
> \- stable Card/Step IDs;\
> \- atomic Add Card;\
> \- scoped autosave;\
> \- per-entity persistence lanes;\
> \- bounded retries/conflict handling;\
> \- detached Card persistence;\
> \- stable \`cardTemplateId\` targeting;\
> \- scoped Card publication;\
> \- scoped Deck publication;\
> \- Deck unpublished-Card warning;\
> \- Publish and leave;\
> \- Step reservation and construction-move rules;\
> \- nullable adoption;\
> \- independent Card ownership;\
> \- immutable versions.\
> \
> No production migration.\
> \
> No new persisted workflow/readiness flags unless you discover a genuinely necessary reason and stop to discuss it first.\
> \
> \## 8. Tests\
> \
> Please add or update tests based on the actual implementation.\
> \
> At minimum, cover the following behaviours where they are not already adequately covered:\
> \
> \- untouched Creator session absent from My Drafts;\
> \- persisted never-published draft appears;\
> \- published Deck with Deck draft appears;\
> \- published Deck with only referenced owned Card draft appears;\
> \- clean published Deck does not appear;\
> \- archived personal Deck with unfinished Creator work still appears in My Drafts;\
> \- null-adoption DeckData remains stored but does not appear in active My Decks;\
> \- null-adoption DeckData does not appear in archived My Decks;\
> \- adopted published Deck remains visible despite newer canonical drafts;\
> \- switching waits for relevant saves/uploads;\
> \- failed/conflicted switch stays in current Creator;\
> \- switching initializes fresh Deck/coordinator state;\
> \- current draft selection just closes modal;\
> \- zero-Card working Deck opens safely;\
> \- reload works;\
> \- progress 0 / confidence null;\
> \- no invalid Card focus/navigation;\
> \- empty Deck archive/restore;\
> \- adding Cards later preserves cadence-anchor behaviour;\
> \- complete private Creator → working Deck → personal state → archive/restore browser journey.\
> \
> If existing tests already cover some of this well, extend them rather than duplicating unnecessarily.\

## 1. Executive summary

Prompt 3 is implemented and ready for Phase 2 final review. My Drafts, safe draft switching, adopted-only My Decks filtering and zero-Card working views are complete.

The broader Phase 2 browser suite is green. Production Atlas was not accessed, mutated, renamed or migrated. Nothing was committed.

## 2. My Drafts design and behaviour

Added a compact Creator entry point opening a modal.

The authenticated, read-only endpoint uses batched projected queries and returns minimal Deck metadata. It includes:

- Persisted never-published Deck drafts, including default-titled drafts.
- Published Decks with outstanding Deck drafts.
- Published Decks with outstanding drafts in currently referenced, owned Cards.

Clean published Decks and detached Card drafts are excluded. Personal archive status does not affect discovery. Opening the list performs no writes.

## 3. My Decks filtering change

The My Decks read model now excludes null-adoption DeckData from both active and archived lists.

Stored null-adoption records remain intact. Internal nullable-adoption resolution and publication/adoption behaviour are unchanged.

Published adopted Decks remain visible and use adopted versions despite newer Creator drafts.

## 4. Draft-switching behaviour

Selecting another draft waits for attached uploads and pending Deck/Card saves without publishing.

Save failures, conflicts and failed uploads keep the current Creator open. Selecting the current Deck simply closes the modal.

Creator instances are keyed by Deck ID, preventing board, coordinator and session state from leaking between Decks. Detached background work continues independently.

The coordinator change is limited to a navigation-preparation method using its existing upload and flush boundaries.

## 5. Zero-Card working-view changes

Empty working Decks retain their heading, introduction and Deck controls while omitting the Card scene.

Navigation/focus operations guard invalid indices. Progress remains 0, confidence remains null and persisted active Card identity remains null.

Tests verify reload, archive/restore and retention of the original cadence anchor after later Card addition.

## 6. Browser journey updates

Replaced obsolete starter-Card and top-level Save Draft assumptions with explicit Add Card actions and autosave acknowledgements.

Preserved coverage for independent publication, update notes, working-state persistence, media, adopted versions, recoverable Publish and leave, archive/restore and mobile layout.

The main issues are presentation/state derivation and inconsistent leave protection. I found no evidence of a canonical persistence or identity regression. No files or database records were changed.

### 1. Publish control state

**Cause:** [publicationState()](./src/components/creator/creatorPersistenceCoordinator.ts:250) returns eligibility booleans. [CreatorDragLab](./src/components/creator/CreatorDragLab.tsx:1045) interprets `false` as “Published”, applies the light styling and disables the button.

That boolean becomes false for several unrelated reasons: no persisted root, default title, unpublished referenced Cards, save errors or publication already running. Consequently, both the label and colour are misleading.

**Classification:** A UI state-model bug. Backend publication validation remains correct.

**Recommendation:** Derive separate properties for publication history, outstanding content, blocking reason and operational state.

| State | Presentation |
|---|---|
| Never published, unchanged/default | Light `Publish`, inactive |
| Outstanding and eligible | Dark `Publish` |
| Outstanding but blocked | Dark `Publish` plus small lock; clickable explanation |
| Actually published and clean | Light `Published` |
| Saving/publishing/conflicted | Separate operational treatment; never infer “Published” from unavailability |

For blocked controls, use a normal enabled button whose handler opens a small explanation, rather than native `disabled`, which prevents interaction. Preserve keyboard access and associate the explanation with the control. First-title restrictions should receive similarly specific explanations.

I recommend retaining the small light control for untouched entities rather than making it appear/disappear. It keeps placement predictable without suggesting publication has occurred.

**Areas:** coordinator-derived presentation state, `CreatorDragLab.tsx`, shared publication rules and button CSS.

**Risk:** Low to moderate. Keep these presentation changes separate from authoritative eligibility and scoped publication. Tests currently asserting “light means published” need updating.

### 2. Creator Card date

**Current behaviour is correct.**

`saveDateEdit()` updates the Card’s board `targetDate` field. [privateGraph()](./src/components/creator/cardArchitectureAdapter.ts:48) projects that into canonical `CardContent.suggestedTargetDate`. The Card lane saves it through the Card-owned endpoint; publication stores that content in the immutable Card version.

It does **not** directly write `CardData.targetDate`. Working-mode initialization applies the separate personal-date precedence.

**Recommendation:** Rename the Creator-facing label from **Target date** to **Suggested target date**. Internal board naming could remain for now.

**Risk:** Cosmetic only; no persistence change required.

### 3. Video upload succeeds but playback is unavailable

The traced path is:

1. Creator flushes the relevant Card.
2. The upload endpoint authorizes its Deck/Card context.
3. `videoUpload()` returns an upload URL and UID.
4. The browser POSTs the file.
5. Metadata is constructed with:
   - `assetId = uid`
   - `id = stream-${uid}`
   - `src = https://iframe.videodelivery.net/${uid}`
6. Creator saves that metadata into the Card draft; publication retains it.
7. Working playback resolves the corresponding HLS manifest.
8. Fatal HLS or native video errors produce `Video unavailable`.

**In `dev:phase2`, this is expected:** [the runner](./scripts/test-phase2.ts:19) returns synthetic `fixture-…` UIDs and accepts uploads without creating Cloudflare assets. Its status endpoint reports `ready`, but it serves no playable video. The player consequently requests a nonexistent Cloudflare manifest.

This mock path is explicitly guarded by the disposable database and loopback fixture configuration in [mediaProviders.ts](./src/lib/cards/mediaProviders.ts:7).

**Outside that configuration, the diagnosis remains unconfirmed.** Upload success means file transfer succeeded, not necessarily Stream processing completed. Working instructional playback immediately attempts HLS; it does not use the processing-status poller employed by the Deck introduction upload preview.

**Recommendation:**

- Make the mock-only playback limitation clear in the disposable development experience.
- For an actual Cloudflare asset, distinguish processing from playback failure and provide a retry/status check.
- Do not change persisted UID/URL handling without evidence of an incorrect real response.

**Areas:** runner/media provider boundary, `mediaUploadClient.ts`, `cloudflareStreamPlayback.ts`, `CloudflareHlsVideoPlayer.tsx` and working playback integration.

**Risk:** Playback changes need focused regression coverage. The inspected path does not show metadata being dropped or assigned to the wrong Card. Mocked tests do not establish successful real Cloudflare playback.

### 4. Leaving Creator / Save drafts and leave

**Why it exists:** `publication.any` delegates to `hasWork()`, which includes both:
- genuinely unsaved/in-flight work;
- fully acknowledged but unpublished drafts.

The return link therefore opens the leave dialog even when every edit is safely saved. `Save drafts and leave` calls `flushAll()`; in that acknowledged case, it performs no new save.

**Classification:** Partly useful protection, partly redundant presentation.

Protection remains necessary for pending saves, creation transactions, retries, conflicts and uploads. However, the current leave path is weaker than My Drafts switching:

- It calls `flushAll()`, not `prepareToNavigate()`.
- Its button is disabled during visible uploads rather than waiting for them.
- It does not perform the failed-upload check used during draft switching.
- These guards cover the explicit Creator return flow, not every browser/tab navigation.

**Recommendation:** Reuse one safe navigation preparation boundary for leaving and switching. Allow immediate departure when work is acknowledged; wait for pending work; remain in Creator when relevant persistence/upload failures prevent safe departure. Preserve detached background work.

**QUESTION FOR USER — Where should Publish and leave remain available?**

It currently exists only in the leave dialog. Removing that dialog for safely saved drafts would also remove its entry point.

Options:

1. Retain a publication-choice dialog, but rename the ordinary action to **Leave**.
2. Let normal leaving proceed after safe preparation, and expose **Publish and leave** separately.

I recommend option 2 given your expectation for normal leaving, but its placement requires agreement. Other fixes can proceed independently.

### 5. Current item in My Drafts

[CreatorDraftsModal](./src/components/creator/CreatorDraftsModal.tsx) receives no current Deck ID. All rows therefore use identical styling, although selecting the current Deck already correctly closes the modal.

**Classification:** Missing presentation state.

**Recommendation:** Pass the current `deckTemplateId`, apply a very subtle neutral background to its row and expose `aria-current="true"`. No checkmark, extra label or edge decoration is needed.

**Areas:** modal props, its Creator invocation and one CSS rule.

**Risk:** Very low; identity comparison must use Deck ID, never title.

### 6. Test/dev Next output separation

The override is gated by `PHASE2_BROWSER_TEST === "1"`:

- Ordinary development/build: standard `.next`.
- Interactive Phase 2: `.next-phase2`.
- Automated Phase 2: `.next-phase2-test`.

The ignore changes only exclude generated output from Git/ESLint.

**Assessment:** Correctly scoped for the intended commands. However, it is environment-gated rather than Next-phase-gated: accidentally setting the test flag during a production/Vercel build would activate the override.

**Recommendation:** Restrict it additionally to Next’s development-server phase. That makes production output independent of an accidentally inherited test flag.

There is also a small remaining isolation gap: both modes write the same generated `phase2-test-results/tsconfig.json` and `server.log`. Separate those per mode to avoid overwriting configuration/logs during concurrent sessions.

**Risk:** Tooling only; no database or application persistence implications.

### 7. Optional upload-failure notification

[useMediaUploadController](./src/components/media/useMediaUploadController.ts:104) remains generic. Its optional callback receives only the media kind; it contains no Creator, coordinator or navigation assumptions.

Its precise semantics are narrower than “any failure”: notification occurs for upload-stage failures after `onUploadStarted` succeeds. Aborts, initial file-validation failures and failures inside `onUploadCompleted` do not trigger it. Completion-persistence errors still appear through the controller error state and relevant save lane.

**Recommendation:** Keep it optional and document that contract. Creator-specific navigation decisions correctly remain in Creator.

**Risk:** Low. No generic-controller redesign is needed.

Implemented all seven final-review fixes. Backend publication, adoption and persistence rules remain unchanged. No production Atlas access and no commit.

**Changes made**

- Publish controls now distinguish outstanding changes, eligibility and publication history. `Published` appears only for genuinely published, clean entities.
- Blocked outstanding work retains the dark cue and shows a small lock. Clicking opens a reason-specific explanation with keyboard dismissal and focus restoration.
- Creator dates now say **Suggested target date**; persistence still targets canonical `suggestedTargetDate`.
- Mock videos explain that synthetic Stream IDs have no playable asset. This requires both the disposable-runner flag and a `fixture-…` ID; real Stream handling is unchanged.
- Normal leaving waits for relevant saves/uploads without a publication-choice dialog. Failures and conflicts retain the current Creator. **Publish and leave** is a separate compact action below the Deck controls, preserving recoverable independent publication.
- My Drafts subtly shades the current Deck and exposes `aria-current`.
- Test/dev output overrides now apply only during Next’s development-server phase. Generated configuration and logs are separated by mode. The optional upload-failure callback’s precise semantics are documented.

> Please correct the Publish control behaviour from the last implementation.
>
> The previous change incorrectly followed the recommendation to show a light inactive `Publish` control for untouched never-published Decks/Cards. That is NOT the product behaviour I want.
>
> Use your own judgment on the technical implementation, but preserve these product rules exactly:
>
> 1. Never-published + untouched/default
> - Hide the Publish control entirely.
> - Do not show `Publish`.
> - Do not show `Published`.
> - This applies to both a brand-new Deck and a brand-new Card when there is nothing meaningful to publish yet.
>
> 2. Never-published + meaningful unpublished changes + eligible
> - Show active `Publish`.
>
> 3. Never-published + meaningful unpublished changes + blocked
> - Show `Publish` with the lock indicator.
> - Preserve the existing dark/light cue for whether there are unpublished changes.
> - The locked control must still be clickable and explain why publishing is blocked.
>
> 4. Published + clean
> - Show `Published`.
>
> 5. Published + newer unpublished changes + eligible
> - Show active `Publish`.
>
> 6. Published + newer unpublished changes + blocked
> - Show `Publish` with the lock indicator and clickable explanation.
>
> Important:
> - `Published` must ONLY mean that at least one real published version exists and there are no newer outstanding changes.
> - “Cannot currently publish” must never be interpreted as “Published”.
> - Do not use a normal inactive `Publish` button for the untouched never-published state.
> - Keep backend publication eligibility/validation unchanged unless you find an actual bug there.
>
> Please inspect the current presentation-state derivation and adjust it cleanly rather than layering another special case on top if a clearer state model is appropriate.
>
> Update focused tests for all six states above for both Deck and Card where applicable.
>
> Run the relevant verification after the fix.
>
> Do not access production Atlas and do not commit until I review the result.
>
> If you find a genuine ambiguity in how one of these states should behave, stop and label it `QUESTION FOR USER` rather than choosing a different product rule.

Cleanup complete: the confirmed baseline was **7 errors and 21 warnings**; lint now passes with **0 errors and 6 warnings**.

The errors were addressed individually:

| Area | Change |
|---|---|
| `patch_script.js` | Converted to an explicit ES module, `patch_script.mjs`. Syntax-checked only; patch operations were not executed. |
| `BackCardFaceContent` | Reset gesture-local preview on guarded signal changes instead of setting state in an effect. Cleanup no longer updates unmounting state. |
| `DeckDetail` | Moved intro pause/collapse into the existing focus-opening handler. |
| `DeckGrid` | Moved intro collapse into the playback-state transition that hides the preview. |
| `useDeckGestures` callback ref | Update after commit using `useLayoutEffect`, rather than mutating during render. |
| `useDeckGestures` cancellation | Retained intentional cancellation with one documented, line-level suppression. Parent locks can interrupt a gesture independently of pointer events. |
| `test_gesture.ts` | Changed the unreassigned session binding to `const`. |

**Fifteen warnings were fixed:** six unused Creator declarations/handlers, three unused imports, two unused test declarations/imports, the scratch script’s comma-expression warning, two unnecessary HLS dependencies, and one obsolete suppression.

**Six warnings remain deliberately:**

- Three `<img>` warnings in `IntroMediaBlock`, `DeckTile`, and `FocusedCardView`. Image-delivery changes need separate validation.
- Two unused diagnostic `reason` arguments on the HLS imperative API. The API contract remains intact.
- One Stream SDK callback-dependency warning. Mechanically adding the dependency could reinitialize playback when the callback changes; this needs dedicated lifecycle testing.

The behaviour-sensitive changes preserve the existing reset, pause and collapse semantics. Publication UX, autosave/navigation, My Drafts, adoption, versioning and zero-Card behaviour were not changed. Browser coverage now also verifies that a failed first signal save restores **“Drag to set”** and retains a `null` reading.

**I recommend your revised sequence.** Moving a minimal Library/import flow ahead of the cross-owner Creator UI gives us a much better way to prove Bob → Alice behaviour. I would keep the split, with a few adjustments to prevent Phase 4 and Phase 5 becoming too large.

Forking can already be tested through disposable-Mongo fixtures without a Library. What the Library adds is the real discovery, adoption, navigation and editing context needed for meaningful browser and manual testing. Both layers of testing are valuable.

The current code supports this direction: the working and preview resolvers already handle foreign public Cards, while Creator deliberately rejects mixed-owner content through `FOREIGN_EDIT_DEFERRED` in [readModels.ts](./src/lib/cards/readModels.ts:10). That separation lets us introduce public consumption before enabling foreign-content editing.

I would revise the roadmap as follows.

| Phase | Recommended scope | Main proof |
|---|---|---|
| **3** | Owned reuse, Copy to…, ownership/fork backend foundations | One Card identity and one personal CardData shared across owned Decks |
| **4** | Minimal public publication, Library preview and import | Bob publishes → Alice discovers, imports and works |
| **5** | Cross-owner Creator flows, then Card Update | Alice forks safely; followers adopt updates explicitly |
| **6** | Framework configuration and direct Item tests | Explicit mappings and evidence plumbing |
| **7** | Full Library discovery experience | Improve discovery without changing import semantics |
| **8** | Progress | Aggregate the established Framework and personal-state model |

**Phase 3: keep owned reuse small, and establish complete fork transactions underneath it.**

Your proposed owned-Card reuse scope is appropriate. Copy should add a reference to the same `cardTemplateId`; it should not create CardData. Removing the source reference must leave the Card root, versions and personal state intact. Duplicate references within one Deck are already rejected by domain validation, so the new operation should consume that protection.

I would divide this phase into two reviewable checkpoints:

1. Owned Copy to… and reference removal, with real browser coverage.
2. Fork repository transactions, permissions and comprehensive integration tests, without exposing foreign editing yet.

The fork foundation has several important consequences:

- **A Card fork needs new Step IDs.** The original Card permanently reserves its published Step identities. Forking therefore needs an explicit old→new Step mapping to copy completion and signals onto the fork.
- Copy the actor’s existing CardData only; retain the original. An unpublished fork uses null adoption until its first publication.
- Preserve trusted media references and physical keys. Some references may contain the original Card ID; copying them must not weaken validation for new uploads.
- The combined Deck-and-Card fork should be atomic, including the reference swap and copied personal state.
- Stable caller-supplied identities and uncertain-response recovery should apply to these operations, as they already do to Add Card.

Cross-Card movement restrictions are substantially implemented already. This phase should verify them against reuse and fork provenance rather than build another movement model.

**Phase 4: include the smallest public publishing path, not just Library screens.**

A Library needs actual published public content. Phase 2 intentionally kept the Creator UI private, so Phase 4 must also provide a narrow, intentional way for an owner to publish a Deck publicly.

The existing repository already encapsulates visibility promotion and public-Deck validation. Reuse those transactions rather than reproducing their rules in Library or Creator components.

The minimal phase should include:

- Public, published Deck discovery.
- Template-only preview using the latest Deck version and latest published Card versions.
- Import that creates membership when absent, or reactivates existing archived DeckData without replacing its adoption.
- Preservation of existing CardData and its adopted Card version.
- Initialization of missing CardData through the agreed import/working-open lifecycle.
- Working mode using adopted versions, independently of what preview showed.
- Permission-safe working controls for foreign templates.

That last point matters: until Phase 5 exists, an imported foreign Deck must not offer an ordinary edit action that simply enters the owner-only Creator path and fails.

One concrete repository gap is that `ensureDeckData()` preserves existing membership but **does not itself reactivate archived membership**. Import needs an explicit orchestration operation; merely calling the existing ensure helpers is insufficient.

Search, elaborate filters, richer previews and Framework-aware discovery can remain in Phase 7.

**Phase 5: split cross-owner editing and Card Update into separate checkpoints.**

Your Bob → Alice examples are exactly the right acceptance journeys. I would implement and review cross-owner editing first, then Card Update.

Removing `FOREIGN_EDIT_DEFERRED` alone would be unsafe. Creator’s adapter and persistence coordinator currently assume editable owned Cards. They need to distinguish foreign published content from owned drafts, and switch to the new fork identity before subsequent saves or uploads.

For Card Update, some foundation already exists:

- Adoption-aware working resolution.
- `canUpdateCard` capability derivation.
- Chronological retrieval of intervening update notes.

What remains is the adoption mutation, working-context read model/UI, confirmation safety and state preservation.

Preserve existing personal state. Initialize new Step identities with `todo` completion and null signals; exclude removed Steps from current progress calculations without destructively erasing their historical state. Reordering existing Steps must preserve their state. This does not require introducing variable-length Step editing.

**Phase 6: remove the apparent Framework uncertainties from the older outline.**

Those decisions are already settled:

- Mappings belong explicitly inside each Framework, not Card/Deck roots or versions.
- Area → DeckTemplate IDs.
- Item → CardTemplate IDs.
- Within one Framework, a Card maps to at most one Item and a Deck to at most one Area.
- Different Frameworks may map the same entities differently.
- No Framework editor or Creator mapping UI in V1.

Include the flat user-level direct Item tests here, with Boolean results. Card-specific tests remain in CardData. Framework-aware Library discovery can be considered later without becoming a dependency of the basic Framework plumbing.

**Add an explicit production cutover gate.**

The reordered feature phases do not remove this requirement. The application remains guarded for disposable local databases, and current migration apply tooling is not a production deployment path.

Before exposing any of this against Atlas, separately approve and rehearse source planning, backup, drift checks, migration verification, rollback and deployment changes. Do not bury cutover inside “minimal Library” or simply remove the database guard.

The media-only legacy reset policy applies to the existing demo database. Once the new application has real learning state, subsequent operations must preserve it.

There are three genuine questions worth recording:

- **QUESTION FOR USER — fork source version.** When Alice edits imported content, should the fork start from her adopted version or the latest published version? I recommend the version she is actually viewing, recorded in provenance. Resolve this before cross-owner editing.
- **QUESTION FOR USER — Deck updates.** Card Update is assigned a phase, but explicit adoption of newer Deck composition still needs a home. I recommend specifying this alongside Phase 5 version adoption, even if its UI is deferred.
- **QUESTION FOR USER — Progress after archiving.** Should retained CardData continue contributing to Framework Progress after all containing Decks are archived? I recommend that it does, because Card learning state is independent of Deck membership. This can wait until Progress planning.

With those boundaries, your revised sequence is stronger than the original: it proves owned reuse first, establishes a real cross-owner consumption flow second, and then introduces the more complex editing and update behaviour.

No files or database records were changed.

> i understand, but how will forking be done in phase 3? will we be bringing in  public decks at this point?

**Phase 3 would implement forking underneath the UI, without introducing public Decks or Library yet.**

It would have two parts:

- **Visible product behaviour:** reuse your own Cards between your own Decks through `Copy to…`.
- **Backend foundation:** implement the transactions for Card forks, Deck forks and combined forks, including provenance, copied personal state, new Step identities and reference swaps.

We would test those transactions using disposable Mongo fixtures containing Alice, Bob and Bob’s public content. That proves the ownership and data-preservation rules without exposing a public workflow in the application.

Then:

- **Phase 4** introduces public publication, minimal Library and import.
- **Phase 5** connects the tested fork operations to Creator, so Alice editing Bob’s imported content triggers the appropriate fork.

So you would **not manually use foreign-content forking in Phase 3**. It would be implemented and backend-tested, then become a usable product interaction in Phase 5.

> ## Newly confirmed architecture decisions
>
> ### 1. Fork source version
>
> When Alice forks content owned by Bob, the fork starts from the exact version Alice has adopted / is currently viewing.
>
> It must NOT silently use Bob’s latest published version if Bob has published a newer version since Alice adopted the content.
>
> Principle:
>
> `fork what the user is actually viewing`
>
> The source version must be recorded in provenance.
>
> ### 2. First published version of a fork
>
> Example:
>
> - Bob Card v2 is what Alice has adopted
> - Alice forks it
> - Alice’s new Card root begins with:
>   - `latestVersion = 0`
>   - draft = exact copy of Bob Card v2
>   - provenance pointing back to Bob Card v2
> - Alice edits that draft
> - when Alice publishes for the first time, Alice Card v1 = Bob v2 + Alice’s edits
>
> Do NOT create an artificial immutable Alice v1 containing unchanged Bob v2 and then make Alice’s edited publication v2.
>
> Fork creation creates unpublished draft state; publication still creates the first immutable version.
>
> ### 3. Step lineage is required
>
> Every Step created by forking another Step gets:
>
> - a new globally unique Step ID
> - explicit provenance back to the Step it was forked from
> - enough provenance to identify the source Card/version from which the Step came
>
> A completely new Step created by Alice has no fork provenance.
>
> We need you to inspect the existing Card/Deck `forkedFrom` model and recommend the exact Step provenance shape.
>
> The key requirement is that future code must be able to reconstruct Step-level lineage.
>
> Do not assume that only `stepId` is enough without evaluating the trade-offs.
>
> Please explicitly compare at least:
>
> - source `stepId` only
> - source `stepId + cardTemplateId + cardTemplateVersion`
> - matching the existing Card/Deck provenance structure as closely as practical
> - whether `ownerUserId` should or should not be copied into Step provenance
>
> Then recommend one exact schema and explain why.
>
> ### 4. Archived Deck re-import
>
> For future Phase 4 import behaviour:
>
> - if Alice already has DeckData for a Deck and it is archived
> - importing the same Deck again should reactivate that existing DeckData
> - do not create duplicate membership
> - preserve its adoption state rather than replacing it
>
> This does not necessarily need implementation in Phase 3, but Phase 3 design must not make it harder.
>
> ### 5. Deck updates
>
> Explicit adoption of newer Deck versions/composition must be specified alongside Card Update in Phase 5.
>
> Phase 3 should preserve the architecture needed for that.
>
> ### 6. Progress after archive
>
> Retained CardData remains independent of Deck archive state and should continue to be available for future Progress aggregation.
>
> Exact Progress behaviour will be designed later.
>

> Phase 3 has TWO layers.

> ### A. User-visible product behaviour
>
> Owned Card reuse only.

> The user should be able to take one of their existing Cards and use it in another Deck through a `Copy to…` flow.

> I found two details the contract needs to address. First, Copy to… should append to the destination’s saved draft with a revision check, so it cannot overwrite edits from another tab. Second, a Deck fork preserves Card references, but the current Creator resolver displays foreign Cards at their latest published versions. The fork commands must therefore carry explicit source versions; Phase 5 will also need to preserve the viewed-version context when opening the fork.
</details>

**The revised Phase 3 is feasible on the current foundation.** Owned reuse can be a complete product feature, while foreign-content forking remains a tested repository/domain capability until Phase 5.

The main additions are:

- a reference-only Copy operation;
- explicit Step lineage;
- atomic fork transactions that use specified immutable source versions;
- precise personal-state copying and recovery rules.

There are a few product choices still requiring approval, principally destination-list inclusion and how Deck-scoped personal information behaves on forks. I identify those explicitly below. The rest can be specified firmly now.

This was a read-only inspection. I changed no files, ran no migrations and did not connect to Atlas.

## 1. Current-code investigation

### Foundations already suitable for Phase 3

| Area | Current implementation | Phase 3 consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Canonical entities | [model.ts](./src/lib/cards/model.ts) defines separate Card/Deck roots and immutable versions. | Reuse requires another Deck reference, not another Card. |
| Personal state | `PersonalUser.cardsData` and `decksData` are separate arrays. | Copy must leave both arrays unchanged. Forking may append new personal records. |
| Transactions | [mongodb.ts](./src/lib/mongodb.ts) provides `withMongoTransaction()` with snapshot reads and majority writes. | Card/Deck creation, reservations, reference replacement and personal-state copying can commit together. |
| References | `assertDeckContent()` rejects duplicate Card references; `deckReferences()` checks ownership/public access and publication of foreign Cards. | Reuse should call these existing validators. |
| Publication | `publishCard()` and `publishDeck()` are independent and advance only the publisher’s existing personal adoption. | Fork creation must not call either publication operation. |
| Removal | Creator’s `detachCard()` saves the Deck composition and keeps the independent Card lane running. | Existing removal semantics are largely correct for reuse. |
| Working resolution | `resolveWorkingDeck()` resolves adopted Deck and Card versions. | Reused Cards already resolve through global personal CardData. |
| Personal display cache | [workingCardStore.ts](./src/lib/cards/workingCardStore.ts) keys personal fields by user plus Card ID. | The cache already follows shared Card identity rather than Deck occurrence. |
| My Drafts | `creatorDrafts()` batches owned Deck roots and referenced owned Card drafts. | A shared Card draft can correctly make several owned Decks appear in My Drafts. |
| Construction moves | `moveConstructionStep()` atomically updates two Cards, the Deck revision and Step reservations. | Preserve this operation and its restrictions. |

These operations are principally implemented in [repository.ts](./src/lib/cards/repository.ts) and [resolvers.ts](./src/lib/cards/resolvers.ts).

### Existing provenance

The current root shapes are:

```ts
// Card root
forkedFrom: {
  cardTemplateId: string;
  version: number;
} | null;

// Deck root
forkedFrom: {
  deckTemplateId: string;
  version: number;
} | null;
```

They are suitable and should remain unchanged.

There is currently **no Step provenance field**. `Step` aliases `CardTemplateStep` from [types.ts](./src/components/decks/types.ts).

Furthermore, `assertCardContent()` explicitly rejects unknown Step fields. Adding lineage requires updating validation, not merely adding a TypeScript property.

### Current Step reservation protections

`createFoundationIndexes()` creates:

- unique Card root identity;
- unique Deck root identity;
- unique `(Card ID, version)` and `(Deck ID, version)`;
- a unique partial multikey index on Card root `stepIds`.

`saveCardDraft()` retains the union of existing reservations and submitted Step IDs. Published and removed identities therefore remain reserved.

The exceptional construction-time swap transfers the two current Step reservations transactionally. Historical reservations remain with their roots.

Two important details:

1. The Mongo multikey index prevents the same Step ID belonging to different Card roots.
2. `assertCardContent()` separately prevents duplicate Step IDs within one Card.

A fork must allocate fresh Step IDs and reserve them through the existing root/index mechanism.

### Current assumptions that need attention

**Creator currently supports owned Cards only.** Although `resolveCreatorDeck()` can resolve foreign public Cards, `creatorDTO()` rejects mixed ownership with `FOREIGN_EDIT_DEFERRED`. Phase 3 should retain that UI restriction.

**There is no existing-card attachment operation.** `createAndAttachCard()` creates a new default Card. It must not be repurposed for Copy to…, because that would confuse reuse with creation.

**Current initial-graph creation is not a reuse operation.** `createPrivateGraph()` expects every referenced Card to be supplied as a newly created Card. Copy destinations should therefore be persisted Decks, not anonymous unsaved boards.

**Card removal wording is misleading.** The existing modal says “Delete Card” and refers to removing its pairs. The operation actually detaches a reference. Phase 3 should change that wording to “Remove from Deck.”

**Step lineage can be lost through legacy projections unless covered.** The current private adapter preserves unedited Step fields from its baseline, but the generic board/template conversion only explicitly copies known fields. Both round trips need lineage preservation tests.

**Deck forks need careful viewed-version handling later.** A Deck version contains references, not embedded Card content. The current Creator resolver displays foreign Cards at their latest published versions. A future fork editor must not silently replace Alice’s viewed Card version with Bob’s latest version. Phase 3 must establish explicit source-version contracts; Phase 5 must consume them.

## 2. Firm Phase 3 delivery contract

### Visible product behaviour

Phase 3 will deliver:

- Copy an owned Card into another persisted owned Deck.
- Reuse the same Card identity and current canonical draft/version history.
- Append one reference to the destination’s saved Creator composition.
- Prevent duplicate occurrences within a Deck.
- Remove references without deleting canonical or personal Card state.
- Demonstrate shared personal state when the Card is worked on through multiple published Decks.
- Preserve scoped autosave, publication and navigation behaviour.

Copy will not publish either entity or create personal CardData.

### Backend/domain behaviour

Phase 3 will deliver:

- Card fork creation.
- Card fork plus replacement in an owned Deck.
- Deck fork creation.
- Combined Deck-and-one-Card fork.
- Exact immutable source-version selection.
- Card/Deck provenance and Step lineage.
- Step-ID remapping for copied personal state.
- Atomic transactions and conservative uncertain-response recovery.
- Permission, duplicate and revision protections.

These will be callable repository/application-service operations with disposable-Mongo integration tests. **No foreign-editing HTTP/UI surface is needed yet.** Keeping unused mutation endpoints unexposed reduces scope without weakening the foundation.

### Deferred

Phase 3 will not implement:

- public publication controls;
- Library, preview or import UI;
- foreign Creator editing or automatic fork UX;
- Card or Deck update adoption;
- standalone Card screens;
- Frameworks or Progress;
- production migration/cutover;
- media copying, relocation, deletion or stronger delivery privacy;
- realtime synchronization between open Creator tabs.

I recommend three checkpoints, with the first delivering the visible feature.

| Checkpoint | Work | Main files/areas | Acceptance |
