## 1. Contract changes

The following updates replace the remaining provisional policies:

- **My Decks Card-fork continuity:** carry completion/skipped, readings, target date and current reflection.
- **Historical continuity:** retain tests, chats and personal media on their original CardData; make relevant source history accessible without physically duplicating it.
- **Library-origin forks:** retain the previously approved first-publication inheritance of eligible Step state and target date, but do not automatically enable the broader My Decks continuity treatment.
- **Step edits preserve state:** description, title, video and other content changes never trigger automatic resets while Step identity continues.
- **Version mismatch:** matching stable Step identities normally carry cleanly. Intersection handling is defensive, not a new ordinary Step-add/remove workflow.
- **Self-use Deck fork:** keep both memberships; carry cadence anchor and valid/remapped active Card; initialize `openedAt` to null.
- **Deck-entry intent:** explicit backend input; no persisted authoring-intent model in Phase 3.
- **Deferred:** explicit publication reset, timestamped learning history, standalone Card membership/surfaces and optional source-Deck replacement UX.

The first-publication timing remains unchanged: no personal record during fork autosave; eligible target CardData is created directly at v1 publication.

## 2. Remaining QUESTION FOR USER items

**No product decision currently blocks Phase 3 implementation.**

The backend must distinguish My Decks continuity from Library-origin editing explicitly. Phase 3 can implement and test those paths without deciding Phase 5’s reopening/confirmation UX.

For clarity, the Library-origin path does not automatically inherit current reflection or expose source historical material as a continuation. That broader treatment is expressly scoped to My Decks continuity.

## 3. Final implementation-ready checklist

### Checkpoint 1 — Personal lifecycle foundation + My Decks ordering

**Personal records**

- [ ] Remove DeckData creation from ordinary draft/initial-graph persistence.
- [ ] Keep ordinary Card creation and drafting free of CardData creation.
- [ ] Require positive published-version pointers in normal CardData and DeckData.
- [ ] Preserve root `latestVersion = 0` for unpublished canonical work.
- [ ] Keep Creator reopening and My Drafts derived from canonical ownership/drafts.
- [ ] Handle existing disposable null records explicitly; never invent adoption by substituting latest.

**Personal entry and publication**

- [ ] First private Deck publication atomically creates its version, membership and missing CardData.
- [ ] Pin missing Card versions when the Deck enters personal use.
- [ ] Preserve existing CardData adoption and state.
- [ ] Public publication alone creates no new Deck membership.
- [ ] Existing publisher adoption continues, including archived memberships.
- [ ] When publisher Deck adoption introduces additional Card references, initialize missing CardData then.
- [ ] Working open uses established adoption; it does not choose latest for missing records.
- [ ] Preserve cadence anchoring on first successful working open.

**My Decks ordering**

- [ ] Never-opened Decks first.
- [ ] Within that group, DeckData `createdAt` descending.
- [ ] Opened Decks by `openedAt` descending.
- [ ] Stable ties.
- [ ] Restore/reactivation preserves original creation/open timestamps.
- [ ] No source/fork grouping.

The current comparator in [myDecksLayout.ts](./src/components/decks/myDecksLayout.ts) runs client-side and places never-opened Decks last. Updating that existing boundary is sufficient.

**Acceptance:** drafts remain reopenable without personal records; newly admitted Decks appear first; working versions are pinned before opening.

### Checkpoint 2 — Owned reuse / Copy to… + permanent reuse restriction

**Copy UI and persistence**

- [ ] Add the secondary action in the existing Card edit modal.
- [ ] List persisted owned unpublished, published and archived destination Decks.
- [ ] Exclude the current Deck.
- [ ] Show already-containing destinations disabled.
- [ ] No new-destination creation flow.
- [ ] Attach the same `cardTemplateId`; create no CardTemplate or CardData.
- [ ] Persist the destination draft immediately.
- [ ] Leave archived destinations archived.
- [ ] Preserve scoped autosave, stable identity and revision/conflict handling.

**Permanent construction restriction**

- [ ] Record successful reuse permanently on the Card root, using a minimal lifecycle field such as `firstReusedAt`.
- [ ] Serialize reuse and construction Step transfer through a common Card-root write.
- [ ] Prohibit cross-Card transfer after publication, published provenance or reuse.
- [ ] Removing another reference never restores permission.
- [ ] Preserve within-Card reorder and identity.
- [ ] Preserve Cards, versions, drafts and CardData when a Deck reference is removed.

**Acceptance:** one Card can serve several owned Decks with one shared personal record; copy/removal cannot reset state or permit unsafe construction movement.

### Checkpoint 3 — Canonical fork foundations + first-publication carryover

- [ ] Include the first meaningful edit in fork creation.

- [ ] Enforce fork-derived construction restrictions even at `latestVersion = 0`.

#### First Card-fork publication

- [ ] Atomically create v1, update the root and create eligible target CardData.
- [ ] Read the actor’s current committed immediate-source CardData inside the transaction.
- [ ] Map completion/skipped and readings through validated Step lineage.
- [ ] Carry personal target date.
- [ ] For My Decks continuity, carry current reflection.
- [ ] Initialize unmatched Steps with existing `todo` and null-reading values.
- [ ] Preserve source CardData unchanged.
- [ ] With no eligible source CardData, publish canonical content only.
- [ ] Never repeat inheritance during later publication or recovery.

#### Historical/event continuity

Use a small, explicit personal-history relationship and a read model rather than copying event arrays.

My recommended implementation is a lightweight source-history reference on target CardData for **My Decks continuity**, established at publication. It points to the original personal Card identity; historical records remain stored there.

This relationship is necessary because canonical provenance alone does not distinguish continuity from a Library fork. It is personal-data lineage, not persisted authoring intent.

- [ ] Resolve source histories only for the authenticated data owner.
- [ ] Return source-context segments separately from target records.
- [ ] Preserve original Card, Deck and event identifiers.
- [ ] Do not merge source chats into the new Deck’s chat container.
- [ ] Do not duplicate tests or personal media.
- [ ] Ensure source deletion/moderation changes are reflected by subsequent reads.
- [ ] Preserve existing continuity links through successive continuity forks.
- [ ] Do not automatically establish historical continuity for Library-origin forks.
- [ ] Avoid loops and repeated source segments.
- [ ] Provide backend/read-model coverage now; integrate the foreign-edit presentation in Phase 5.

The current [readModels.ts](./src/lib/cards/readModels.ts) projects only the current Card’s media/reflection and filters chats by current Deck context. It needs an explicit historical-context result rather than simply appending source arrays. It also currently omits tests from the working projection.

#### Self-use Deck publication

- [ ] Explicitly distinguish “enter My Decks” from canonical-only publication.
- [ ] Create new DeckData for the new identity.
- [ ] Keep the original source DeckData unchanged.
- [ ] Carry cadence anchor.
- [ ] Carry/remap valid active Card; otherwise null.
- [ ] Set `openedAt` null, archive state active and sharing recipients empty.
- [ ] Reuse existing CardData—including inherited fork CardData—and initialize missing records.
- [ ] Preserve independent Card/Deck transactions.

**Acceptance:** forks retain exact canonical provenance; personal continuity is correct without duplicated histories; Library-origin publication does not accidentally create Deck membership.

## 4. Publication consistency and recovery

Ordinary publication already has the essential preservation behaviour in [repository.ts](./src/lib/cards/repository.ts): it updates adoption without destructive reconciliation.

Checkpoint 3 must preserve that and use the same identity-based principles for forks:

| Operation | Continuing identity |
|---|---|
| Owner publishes revised Card content | Same Step IDs retain completion/skipped and readings |
| User explicitly adopts a later version | Same principle; adoption UI remains Phase 5 |
| Card fork | New Step IDs receive approved values through lineage |
| Defensive identity mismatch | Unmatched target Steps initialize normally |

No content-change classification, automatic reset or new reset flag belongs in Phase 3.

For uncertain publication responses:

- Keep the expected revision/version and exact attempted publication.
- Recognize the committed immutable version.
- Do not create v2 as a retry.
- Do not duplicate target CardData.
- Do not refresh inherited state after target state changes.
- Return a structured recovery conflict when the existing evidence cannot prove the outcome.

A separate receipt collection is still unnecessary. Add technical metadata only if an actual recovery test establishes the need.

## 5. Additional risks and tests

The decisions add these specific verification obligations:

- **Skipped preservation:** explicitly test `skipped`, not only `done`.
- **Content edits:** change Step title, description and video while retaining IDs; owner publication must preserve completion and readings.
- **Follower isolation:** another user stays on their adopted version with unchanged state.
- **Reflection continuity:** copy the committed reflection at publication, then verify source and target can change independently.
- **Historical visibility:** source tests remain discoverable through continuity without duplicate stored events.
- **Context correctness:** source chats retain their original Deck context.
- **Media retention:** historical personal media uses original references; canonical media remains separate.
- **Library distinction:** eligible Step-state inheritance works without automatically enabling source-history continuity.
- **Fork chains:** histories remain attributable and are returned once.
- **Concurrent learning updates:** publication copies one coherent committed snapshot.
- **Lost response:** recovery leaves subsequently edited target state untouched.
- **Deck navigation:** remap active Card only when valid; retain anchor while keeping new `openedAt` null.
- **Ordering:** newly admitted forks/imports/private Decks lead the never-opened group; restoration does not manufacture recency.

Use pure unit tests, disposable transaction-capable Mongo integration tests, and browser tests for owned reuse and the existing private lifecycle. Foreign editing remains backend-tested until Phases 4–5.

Run the established full verification commands after implementation: unit, integration, E2E, Phase 2 browser suite, typecheck, lint, build with empty Mongo variables, and both diff checks.

Deferred work now explicitly includes:

- Creator-requested Step-state resets.
- Timestamped completion, reading and reflection history.
- Progress aggregation/counting across lineage.
- Standalone Card membership and surfaces.
- Optional keep-versus-replace source Deck UX.
- Foreign editing intent/reopening UX.

**Phase 3 is implementation-ready with the existing three checkpoints.** The historical continuity addition is the main extra backend/read-model work; it does not justify another phase or a redesign of the persistence coordinator.

Checkpoint 1 is complete and ready for review. I have stopped; Checkpoints 2–3 have not begun.

**What changed**

- Canonical creation and draft saving no longer create personal records.
- CardData and DeckData require positive published-version pointers; null adoption is rejected.
- First ordinary private Deck publication atomically creates membership and missing CardData, pinning versions before first open.
- Public publication creates no new personal records. Existing publisher adoption still advances without resetting state or unarchiving membership.
- Explicit personal entry preserves existing Card adoption/state and reactivates archived membership without changing its creation time.
- Working reads require established CardData; they no longer initialize missing state or substitute latest versions.
- My Decks now places never-opened Decks first, ordered by personal creation time descending, followed by opened Decks ordered by `openedAt` descending. Ties remain stable.
- Ordinary Card publication preserves completion, including `skipped`, and signal readings across content edits and same-Card reordering.

**Files changed**

Application/foundation:

- [model.ts](./src/lib/cards/model.ts) — non-null adoption types.
- [domain.ts](./src/lib/cards/domain.ts) — positive-version validation.
- [repository.ts](./src/lib/cards/repository.ts) — personal-entry transactions and lifecycle changes.
- [resolvers.ts](./src/lib/cards/resolvers.ts) — exact adopted-version resolution.
- [readModels.ts](./src/lib/cards/readModels.ts) — remove virtual personal-state/latest-version fallbacks.
- [myDecksLayout.ts](./src/components/decks/myDecksLayout.ts) — agreed ordering.
- [plan.ts](./scripts/migration/plan.ts) — offline target-graph completeness validation.

Tests:

- [personal-lifecycle.integration.ts](./tests/personal-lifecycle.integration.ts) — ten new transaction/lifecycle regressions.
- [card-foundation.test.ts](./tests/card-foundation.test.ts) — adoption validation.
- [card-foundation.integration.ts](./tests/card-foundation.integration.ts) — publication, membership and rollback expectations.
- [creator-lifecycle.integration.ts](./tests/creator-lifecycle.integration.ts) — draft creation without personal records.
- [phase2.integration.ts](./tests/phase2.integration.ts) — working initialization and adoption expectations.
- [card-migration.test.ts](./tests/card-migration.test.ts) — complete migrated CardData coverage.
- [my-decks-layout.spec.ts](./tests/my-decks-layout.spec.ts) — ordering and stable ties.
- [creator-drafts.browser.ts](./tests/phase2/creator-drafts.browser.ts) — ordering, canonical-only drafts and publication acknowledgement.
- [private-deck.browser.ts](./tests/phase2/private-deck.browser.ts) — personal records established at Deck publication.

**Compatibility and concerns**

Existing obsolete local null-adoption records are rejected explicitly rather than silently repaired or deleted.

The offline migration planner could previously omit CardData where legacy demo state was absent. It now requires complete coverage while retaining the agreed media-only preservation policy. Previously generated incomplete plans will need regeneration before any future apply.

No unresolved product decision or Checkpoint 1 blocker remains. Production Atlas was not accessed or mutated. No production migration, cutover or commit was performed.

> ## Checkpoint 2 — Owned Card reuse / `Copy to…` + permanent reuse restriction
>
> Use the final agreed Phase 3 contract and the completed Checkpoint 1 foundation.
>
> Please implement only this checkpoint and stop afterwards for review.
>
> Scope:
>
> - Add a minimal `Copy to…` action as a secondary action in the existing Card edit modal.
> - Destination list:
>   - persisted owned unpublished Decks;
>   - persisted owned published Decks;
>   - archived owned Decks;
>   - exclude the current Deck;
>   - show Decks that already contain the Card as disabled;
>   - exclude other users’ Decks;
>   - no “create new Deck” flow.
> - Copy must reuse the same `cardTemplateId`.
> - Do NOT clone the Card.
> - Do NOT create CardData.
> - Do NOT unarchive an archived destination Deck.
> - Persist the destination Deck draft immediately and preserve the existing scoped autosave/revision/conflict model.
> - Removing a Card reference later must not delete the Card root, versions, draft, CardData, or references from other Decks.
>
> ## Permanent reuse rule
>
> Implement the agreed lifecycle rule:
>
> Cross-Card Step dragging is only allowed during exclusive initial construction.
>
> Once a Card has ever been reused in another Deck, cross-Card Step dragging involving that Card is permanently disabled, even if the extra reference is later removed.
>
> This is in addition to the existing restrictions from publication and fork provenance.
>
> Use the cleanest technical implementation you judge appropriate after inspecting the code. A field such as `firstReusedAt` was discussed, but do not use that name/mechanism blindly if the code suggests a better solution.
>
> Important:
> - Copy/reuse and construction-time cross-Card Step movement must be safe under concurrency.
> - Do not create a race where Copy and Step transfer can both commit against stale assumptions.
> - Within-Card Step reorder remains allowed.
> - Do not redesign the Creator persistence coordinator unless genuinely necessary.
> - Preserve all Checkpoint 1 lifecycle behaviour.
> - Do not pull in fork implementation, Library UI, foreign editing, standalone Cards, or Phase 4/5 work.
>
> Please use your own technical judgment based on the current codebase. If any implementation assumption in the plan is unnecessary or unsafe, improve it and explain why.
>
> Verification should include:
> - successful owned Copy-to;
> - same Card reused across multiple owned Decks;
> - duplicate destination protection;
> - archived destination stays archived;
> - unpublished and published destinations;
> - removal preserves Card/CardData;
> - reuse permanently blocks cross-Card Step movement;
> - removing the extra Deck reference does not restore movement;
> - Copy racing with cross-Card Step movement is handled safely;
> - relevant browser coverage for the Copy-to UX;
> - full regression coverage for Phase 2/Checkpoint 1 behaviour.
>
> After implementation, report:
> 1. what changed;
> 2. files changed;
> 3. exact Copy-to UX behaviour;
> 4. how permanent reuse is represented/enforced;
> 5. concurrency/retry/recovery behaviour;
> 6. tests added/updated;
> 7. verification results;
> 8. any concerns or deferred TODOs.
>
> Do not commit.
> Do not access production Atlas.
> Do not start Checkpoint 3.

Checkpoint 2 is complete and ready for review. I have stopped; Checkpoint 3 has not begun.

**What changed / exact Copy-to behaviour**

`Copy to…` is a secondary action inside the existing Card edit modal. It expands a small destination list within that modal.

The list:

- includes owned persisted unpublished, published and archived Decks;
- excludes the current Deck and foreign Decks;
- disables destinations already containing the Card;
- provides no create-new-Deck flow.

Selecting a destination immediately saves its Deck draft with the **same `cardTemplateId` appended**. It creates no Card root, version or CardData, leaves archive state unchanged, and keeps the current Creator session and modal edits intact.

Copy waits only for necessary Card creation acknowledgement. It does not flush pending Card content or unrelated Deck saves.

**Permanent reuse enforcement**

Card roots now have optional:

- `firstReusedAt`: permanent reuse marker, never cleared by removal.
- `referenceRevision`: transaction bookkeeping independent of the Card’s content revision.

Copy and existing reference-attachment paths write the Card root. Construction-time Step transfer also writes that root, so Mongo transaction conflicts serialize competing operations.

If transfer commits first, Copy references the resulting Card. If Copy commits first, transfer rejects after transaction retry. Reused Cards remain blocked after the extra reference is removed. Within-Card reorder remains allowed.

Publication and fork-provenance restrictions remain intact.

**Concurrency, retry and recovery**

- Destination revision and a server-generated content fingerprint protect the saved composition from concurrent overwrites.
- Transient Copy failures receive bounded retries after approximately 1, 3 and 8 seconds.
- Retries retain the original command.
- An exact committed append is recognised after a lost response without adding another reference.
- Subsequent destination changes or removal produce a structured conflict instead of guessed recovery.
- Conflicts show a compact error with an explicit destination-refresh action.
- No idempotency collection or coordinator redesign was introduced.

> Please make one focused amendment to Phase 3 Checkpoint 2 before we start Checkpoint 3.
>
> The existing Copy-to implementation is correct, but we want to improve the important self-use flow.
>
> PRODUCT INTENT
>
> A major future use case for `Copy to…` is outside Creator entirely:
>
> A normal user may find a useful Card somewhere and simply want to add it to an existing programme they are already following.
>
> They should not have to understand Creator or manually open the destination Deck and press Publish merely because Deck composition is versioned internally.
>
> Therefore, treat Copy-to as a reusable Deck/Card domain operation whose current UI happens to live in Creator. Do not make the backend behaviour dependent on Creator-local state in a way that would prevent the same operation later being called from Library/My Decks/etc.
>
> NEW AUTO-PUBLISH RULE
>
> When Copy-to targets an already-published owned Deck, automatically publish the resulting Deck change when ALL of these are true:
>
> 1. the destination Deck was already published;
> 2. before this Copy, the destination had no outstanding Deck-level draft changes waiting to be published;
> 3. the copied Card has an existing published version;
> 4. normal Deck publication invariants are satisfied.
>
> In that case, the user's one Copy-to action should result in the Card being added and a new published Deck version being created, so the change becomes live without requiring a separate Creator visit.
>
> IMPORTANT: “clean destination” means clean BEFORE the Copy.
>
> The Copy itself necessarily creates the composition change. That should not then make the operation classify itself as dirty and refuse auto-publication.
>
> DO NOT AUTO-PUBLISH WHEN
>
> - the destination already had unrelated unpublished Deck-level changes;
> - the destination has never been published;
> - the Card has no published version;
> - any normal publication invariant prevents publication.
>
> In those cases, retain the current behaviour:
> - save the Card reference into the destination draft;
> - do not discard or overwrite anything;
> - do not silently publish unrelated work.
>
> CARD DRAFTS
>
> Do not publish an outstanding Card draft as a side effect of Copy-to.
>
> If the Card has both:
> - an existing published version; and
> - newer unpublished Card edits,
>
> Copy-to may auto-publish the destination Deck according to the normal Deck publication rules, but must not turn this into a hidden Card-publish operation.
>
> If the Card has never been published, destination auto-publication is unavailable.
>
> USER FEEDBACK
>
> Please make the result explicit in the Copy-to UI.
>
> Conceptually distinguish:
>
> - copied and published immediately;
> - copied to destination draft, with publication still required.
>
> Use concise wording appropriate to the existing UI rather than adding a large workflow.
>
> CONCURRENCY / RECOVERY
>
> Please inspect the clean-state test, Copy transaction and Deck publication path carefully.
>
> The important guarantee is that we must never:
>
> - inspect a clean destination;
> - race with another unrelated Deck edit;
> - then publish that unrelated edit accidentally.
>
> Use your own judgment on whether Copy + publication should be one transaction or another safely coordinated operation based on the existing repository/publication architecture.
>
> Preserve the existing lost-response/idempotent recovery behaviour. A retry must not:
> - append the Card twice;
> - create an extra Deck version;
> - publish later unrelated changes;
> - reinterpret a draft-only Copy as auto-publish after circumstances have changed.
>
> If the existing architecture makes a safe implementation materially more complicated than expected, stop and report the issue rather than weakening these guarantees.
>
> TESTS
>
> Please add coverage for at least:
>
> - clean published destination (including archived) -> Copy automatically creates the next published Deck version;
> - copied Card appears in the published composition;
> - dirty published destination -> Copy updates draft only and does not publish existing changes;
> - never-published destination -> draft only;
> - Card with no published version -> draft only;
> - Card with published version plus an outstanding Card draft -> destination may auto-publish but Card draft is NOT published;
> - concurrent destination edit cannot be accidentally swept into auto-publication;
> - lost-response/retry does not duplicate Card reference or Deck publication;
> - existing duplicate protection and permanent reuse restriction still work.
>
> SCOPE
>
> This is an amendment to Checkpoint 2.
>
> Do not begin Checkpoint 3 yet.
> Do not introduce Library UI yet.
> Do not redesign the whole persistence coordinator unless genuinely necessary.
> Do not access production Atlas or perform migration/cutover work.
>
> Use your own technical judgment based on the codebase.
>
> After implementation, stop and report:
> 1. exact auto-publish eligibility logic;
> 2. how “destination was clean before Copy” is established safely;
> 3. transaction/concurrency/recovery behaviour;
> 4. UI feedback for auto-published versus draft-only results;
> 5. files changed;
> 6. tests and verification results;
> 7. any concern that affects the future non-Creator Copy-to use case.
>
> Do not commit.

Implemented the Checkpoint 2 amendment. Ready for review; nothing committed.

1. **Auto-publication eligibility**

Copy automatically publishes the destination when it was already published, had no Deck draft **before Copy**, the copied Card has a published version, and normal publication prerequisites pass. Otherwise, Copy saves the reference into the destination draft.

Outstanding Card drafts are preserved and never published by Copy.

2. **Clean-state and concurrency safety**

The clean-state check, reference attachment, permanent reuse marker and optional Deck publication run in **one Mongo transaction**, using the existing publication service.

Destination revision and content hash are checked before attachment. Concurrent edits trigger conflict/revalidation; their changes cannot be swept into auto-publication.

3. **Recovery**

Auto-created immutable Deck versions carry a small Copy receipt. Exact retries return the original outcome without appending again or creating another version.

Draft-only retries remain draft-only even if the Card later publishes. Subsequent destination changes produce a recovery conflict rather than replaying the operation. Transaction failures roll back the entire Copy/publication.

Normal publisher adoption applies, including missing CardData initialization where membership requires it. Archived destinations remain archived.

4. **UI feedback**

The existing Copy modal now reports either:

- “Copied and published in the destination Deck.”
- “Copied to the destination draft. Publish that Deck to make it live.”

5. **Files changed by this amendment**

- `src/lib/cards/repository.ts` — atomic Copy/publication and shared publication implementation.
- `src/lib/cards/model.ts` — optional immutable Copy receipt.
- `src/lib/cards/cardReuse.ts` — explicit result contract.
- `src/components/creator/CreatorCopyTo.tsx` — outcome-specific feedback.
- `tests/card-reuse.integration.ts` — eligibility, concurrency, rollback and recovery coverage.
- `tests/phase2/card-reuse.browser.ts` — feedback and lost-response publication coverage.

6. **Verification**

| `npm run test:unit` | 205 passed |
| `npm run test:integration` | 78 passed |
| `npm run test:e2e` | 124 passed |

| Both diff checks | Passed |

No skipped tests. Coverage includes archived destinations, dirty/unpublished cases, untouched Card drafts, concurrent edits, duplicate protection and permanent reuse restrictions.

7. **Future non-Creator use**

The backend operation has no dependency on Creator-local state. It remains owned-Card/owned-Deck only; future public-Card Copy will need its separately agreed authorization extension.

> The Checkpoint 2 amendment looks good.
>
> One technical clarification before we close it:
>
> You mention that auto-created immutable Deck versions now carry a small Copy receipt for exact lost-response recovery.
>
> Please explain briefly:
> 1. the exact shape/purpose/lifetime of that receipt;
> 2. whether it is treated purely as operational recovery metadata rather than meaningful Deck content;
> 3. confirm that it does not affect semantic Deck equality/content comparison, normal version/adoption behaviour, Library/provenance behaviour, or future Deck Update logic except where explicitly needed to recognise the exact Copy operation.
>
> If that is already cleanly isolated, no change is required.
>
> Do not start Checkpoint 3 yet.

1. The receipt is an optional field on the immutable Deck version:

```ts
{
  cardTemplateId: string;
  revision: number;     // destination Deck revision before Copy
  contentHash: string;  // hash of the exact pre-Copy Deck draft/composition
}
```

It exists only on a Deck version produced by Copy auto-publication. Its lifetime matches that immutable version, allowing a retry after a lost response to prove that the exact Copy command already created that version.

2. Yes. It is purely operational recovery metadata. It is not part of `PublishedDeckContent`, the Deck draft, Card references, identity, ownership, provenance, or user-visible version content.

3. Confirmed. The receipt:

- is excluded from Deck content equality and draft comparison;
- does not affect publication eligibility;
- does not affect version adoption or working-mode resolution;
- does not participate in Library, visibility, provenance, or fork behaviour;
- does not alter Card version pinning;
- should not affect future Deck Update comparisons or adoption logic.

Repository recovery inspects it only when retrying the corresponding Copy command. All other version consumers continue to use the `content` field and ignore the optional receipt. No change is required, and Checkpoint 3 has not started.

>
> ## Checkpoint 3 — Canonical fork foundations + first-publication carryover
>
> Use the final agreed Phase 3 contract and the completed Checkpoints 1–2.
>
> Please implement only this checkpoint and stop afterwards for review.
>
> Scope:
>
> ### Canonical fork creation
>
> Implement backend/domain support for:
>
> - Card fork;
> - Deck fork;
> - combined Deck + Card fork where required.
>
> Requirements:
>
> - fork from the exact immutable source version the user is actually viewing/adopted;
> - first meaningful autosave creates the owned canonical fork and includes that edit;
> - fork roots begin unpublished with `latestVersion = 0`;
> - use stable caller-supplied target identities for safe retry/recovery;
> - Card forks receive new globally unique Step IDs;
> - record explicit immediate-source Step lineage:
>   {
>     cardTemplateId: string;
>     version: number;
>     stepId: string;
>   }
> - preserve canonical media references;
> - replace only the intended Deck draft reference;
> - unchanged Cards retain their original Card identities;
> - canonical fork creation must not create DeckData or CardData;
> - fork-derived Cards are permanently ineligible for construction-time cross-Card Step movement, even while unpublished.
>
> ### First Card-fork publication
>
> On first publication of a forked Card:
>
> - atomically create immutable Card v1 and update the Card root;
> - if the actor has eligible CardData for the immediate source Card, create target CardData in the same successful publication transaction;
> - read the actor’s current committed source CardData inside that transaction;
> - preserve source CardData unchanged;
> - never create null-adoption CardData;
> - with no eligible source CardData, publish canonical content only.
>
> State carryover:
>
> For My Decks continuity:
> - completion, including `skipped`;
> - signal readings;
> - personal target date;
> - current reflection.
>
> For Step-specific state:
> - map through validated Step lineage;
> - under the current product model, source published Card versions normally retain the same Step identities, so all three should normally map;
> - treat identity intersection only as defensive handling where a source Step identity is genuinely absent;
> - unmatched target Steps initialize with normal todo/null-reading defaults;
> - do not title-match or position-match Steps.
>
> Do not repeat inheritance on later publications or recovery.
>
> ### Historical/event continuity
>
> For My Decks-origin continuity forks:
>
> Historical/event data should remain stored once in its original context and remain accessible without physically duplicating it:
>
> - tests;
> - chats;
> - personal media.
>
> Implement the smallest clean personal-history relationship/read model needed for this.
>
> Important:
> - canonical fork provenance alone is not sufficient to decide personal continuity;
> - Library-origin forks must not automatically receive the broader My Decks historical-continuity treatment;
> - preserve original Card/Deck/event context;
> - do not merge old chats into a new Deck chat container;
> - do not duplicate tests or personal media;
> - source deletion/moderation changes should naturally be reflected on later reads;
> - continuity chains must not produce loops or repeated history segments.
>
> This checkpoint needs backend/read-model support only where foreign-edit UI is not yet available. Do not build Phase 5 UI.
>
> ### Library-origin fork distinction
>
> Keep this explicit:
>
> - My Decks-origin fork = usually continuity.
> - Library-origin fork = not automatically continuity.
>
> The already-agreed first-publication inheritance of eligible Step state / target date may still apply where source CardData exists, but do not automatically expose source reflection/history as though the Library fork were a continuation of the user's active programme.
>
> ### Self-use Deck fork publication
>
> When publishing a self-use Deck fork intended to enter My Decks:
>
> - explicitly distinguish “enter My Decks” from canonical-only publication;
> - create new DeckData for the new Deck identity;
> - keep the source DeckData unchanged and active;
> - do not auto-archive or replace the source Deck;
> - carry cadenceAnchorDate;
> - carry/remap valid activeCardId where possible, otherwise null;
> - set `openedAt = null`;
> - new fork starts active, with no inherited sharing recipients;
> - reuse existing CardData where Card identities are unchanged;
> - reuse any target CardData already created for forked Cards;
> - create only missing CardData;
> - preserve independent Card/Deck publication transaction boundaries as previously agreed.
>
> ### Publication consistency
>
> Preserve ordinary Card publication behaviour from Checkpoint 1:
>
> - continuing Step identity preserves completion/skipped;
> - continuing Step identity preserves signal readings;
> - content edits must not automatically reset user state.
>
> Do not implement content-change classification or reset flags.
>
> ### Recovery
>
> Preserve existing publication recovery principles:
>
> - recognise exact committed immutable v1 after lost response;
> - do not create v2 as retry;
> - do not duplicate target CardData;
> - do not refresh inherited state on retry after target state has subsequently changed;
> - return a structured conflict if the committed outcome cannot be proven.
>
> Use technical metadata only if actual recovery tests demonstrate a need.
>
> ### Deferred — do not implement now
>
> Do not implement:
>
> - Creator reset-progress controls;
> - timestamped learning event/history log;
> - full Progress aggregation;
> - Card/Deck Update UX;
> - Library UI;
> - foreign editing UI;
> - standalone Card collection membership/surfaces;
> - keep-vs-replace source Deck UX;
> - production migration/cutover.
>
> ### Verification
>
> Please add coverage for at least:
>
> - exact viewed-version Card fork;
> - exact viewed-version Deck fork;
> - combined fork;
> - new Step IDs and correct lineage;
> - unchanged Cards retaining original identities;
> - no personal records created by canonical fork autosave;
> - first Card-fork publication with and without source CardData;
> - preservation of completion, including `skipped`;
> - preservation of signal readings;
> - target-date carryover;
> - My Decks reflection carryover;
> - Library-origin distinction;
> - defensive Step-identity mismatch;
> - source CardData unchanged;
> - historical tests/chat/media discoverable without duplication;
> - original chat Deck context preserved;
> - continuity chains returned once with no loops;
> - self-use Deck fork creates separate membership while retaining source;
> - cadence/activeCard continuity;
> - `openedAt = null`;
> - lost-response recovery;
> - concurrent source-state updates produce one coherent committed snapshot;
> - all existing Phase 2 and Checkpoint 1–2 behaviour remains intact.
>
> Run the established full verification commands after implementation:
> - unit;
> - integration;
> - E2E;
> - Phase 2 browser suite;
> - typecheck;
> - lint;
> - build with empty Mongo variables;
> - both diff checks.
>
> Use your own technical judgment based on the current codebase.
>
> If you encounter a meaningful unresolved product or architecture choice, stop and label it clearly:
>
> QUESTION FOR USER
>
> with:

> - available options;
> - your recommendation;
> - why it matters.
>

> 5. historical-continuity design;
> 6. My Decks vs Library-origin distinction;
> 7. self-use Deck fork behaviour;
> 8. tests and verification results;
> 9. concerns or deferred TODOs.
>
> Do not commit.
> Do not access production Atlas.
> Do not begin Phase 4.

   | [repository.ts](./src/lib/cards/repository.ts) | Transactional fork creation, publication, recovery and personal entry |
   | [model.ts](./src/lib/cards/model.ts), [domain.ts](./src/lib/cards/domain.ts), [types.ts](./src/components/decks/types.ts) | Contracts and validated Step lineage |
   | [readModels.ts](./src/lib/cards/readModels.ts) | Actor-scoped historical continuity |
   | [Card fork route](./src/app/api/card-templates/[cardTemplateId]/fork/route.ts), [Deck fork route](./src/app/api/deck-templates/[deckTemplateId]/fork/route.ts) | Authenticated fork endpoints |
   | [Deck publication route](./src/app/api/deck-templates/[deckTemplateId]/publish/route.ts) | Explicit fork personal-entry intent and scoped acknowledgement |
   | [History route](./src/app/api/cards-data/[cardTemplateId]/history/route.ts) | Read-only personal-history endpoint |
   | [Unit tests](./tests/card-forks.test.ts), [integration tests](./tests/card-forks.integration.ts), [browser tests](./tests/phase2/fork-foundations.browser.ts) | Focused checkpoint coverage |

3. **Fork transactions and recovery**

   Creation validates source access, exact source version, target identities, Step reservations and any Deck attachment revision. Combined creation and reference replacement commit in one transaction.

   Stable-ID retries recognize the exact unchanged result; conflicting outcomes return structured errors.

   First fork publication stores a small operational receipt outside canonical content. Exact retries recognize committed v1, without creating v2 or repeating inheritance—even after target personal state changes. Deck recovery also checks entry intent and publication consent.

4. **Personal-state carryover**

   First Card-fork publication creates v1 and eligible target CardData atomically. It reads source CardData transactionally and leaves it unchanged.

   Completion—including `skipped`—and readings follow validated immediate-source Step lineage. Target dates carry. Unmatched Steps receive normal `todo`/null defaults. Mapping never uses titles or positions.

   Later publication does not repeat inheritance. Ordinary owner publication continues preserving state for continuing Step identities.

5. **Historical continuity**

   My Decks continuity records an immediate personal-history source relationship. The read model follows that chain and returns tests, chats and media once, retaining original Card/Deck context.

   Nothing is physically copied or merged. Later source moderation/deletion is reflected on subsequent reads. Cycles are rejected, and deleted source records stop traversal.

6. **My Decks versus Library origin**

   Fork origin is retained separately from canonical provenance.

   My Decks-origin forks carry current reflection and expose historical continuity. Library-origin forks may inherit eligible completion/readings/target dates, but do not automatically inherit reflection or broader history.

   A Library-only Deck can therefore have no DeckData while a published forked Card inside it has inherited CardData.

7. **Self-use Deck forks**

   First publication explicitly declares whether the fork enters My Decks.

   Personal entry creates separate active DeckData, preserves the source membership, carries the cadence anchor, retains/remaps a valid active Card, and leaves `openedAt` null. Sharing recipients and archive state are not inherited.

   Existing CardData is reused; only missing records are initialized. Card and Deck publication remain independent transactions.

8. **Tests and verification**

   Added **5 unit, 13 Mongo integration and 2 authenticated HTTP/browser tests**, including concurrency, rollback, lineage chains, source-state preservation and exact retry recovery.

   | Command | Result |
   |---|---|
   | `npm run test:unit` | 210 passed |
   | `npm run test:integration` | 91 passed |
   | `npm run test:e2e` | 124 passed |
   | `npm run test:phase2` | 35 passed |
   | `npm run typecheck` | Passed |
   | `npm run lint` | 0 errors; 6 unchanged baseline warnings |
   | `MONGODB_URI='' MONGODB_DB='' npm run build` | Passed |
   | `git diff --check` | Passed |
   | `git diff HEAD --check` | Passed |

   No skipped tests. Mongo verification used disposable local databases; Cloudflare browser boundaries were mocked.

   Baseline warnings remain: three image-element warnings, two unused `reason` warnings and one Stream-player effect dependency warning.

9. **Concerns and deferred work**

   Historical continuity is backend/read-model support; foreign-edit UI remains deferred. Existing historical records lack precise event-time version attribution, so history segments identify the source record’s current adoption rather than inventing event versions.

   Full event logging, Progress, reset controls, Update UX and Library/foreign-edit UI remain deferred. No known Checkpoint 3 blocker remains.

Below is a technical handoff you can give Claude. It separates implemented behaviour from future plans and identifies the areas where a second opinion would be most useful.

One numbering clarification: the agreed revised roadmap has **Phase 6: Framework + direct Item tests**, **Phase 7: full Library**, and **Phase 8: Progress**. This report covers Phases 1–7 as requested, with Progress mentioned only where it affects earlier technical choices.

---

**Technical review brief for Claude**

Please review the current codebase alongside this report. Challenge the implementation and proposed technical approach; do not assume that passing tests prove the architecture correct.

Separate your findings into:

- concrete implementation defects;
- missing tests or insufficient guarantees;
- architectural risks that warrant changes before deployment;
- reasonable trade-offs that can remain;
- unresolved product decisions requiring clarification.

Product journeys will be supplied separately. The current implementation has **not been migrated into production**, and production Atlas must not be accessed or modified during this review.

Some repository documentation predates this refactor. In particular, older architecture documents describing prototype/mock-data phases or embedded legacy Deck/Card structures are not authoritative descriptions of the current model.

**1. Core architecture now implemented**

Canonical content and personal learning state have separate lifecycles.

| Entity | Meaning |
|---|---|
| CardTemplate root | Stable Card identity, ownership, visibility, current draft and publication pointer |
| CardTemplateVersion | Immutable published Card content |
| DeckTemplate root | Stable Deck identity, ownership, visibility, current draft and publication pointer |
| DeckTemplateVersion | Immutable Deck content and ordered Card references |
| DeckData | A user’s adopted Deck, personal membership, navigation, archive and cadence state |
| CardData | A user’s adopted Card version and current personal learning state |

**Important physical-storage detail:** canonical roots and versions have separate Mongo collections. DeckData and CardData are currently separate embedded arrays within User documents, rather than separate collections.

There is one CardData per user/CardTemplate identity, irrespective of how many Decks reference that Card. CardData survives Deck archive and reference removal.

Canonical roots can exist with `latestVersion = 0`. Normal personal records must point to an existing positive published version; normal null-adoption DeckData/CardData has been removed.

Steps remain embedded within Card content. They have globally unique stable IDs; there is no StepTemplate collection.

Principal entry points:

- `src/lib/cards/model.ts`
- `src/lib/cards/domain.ts`
- `src/lib/cards/repository.ts`
- `src/lib/cards/resolvers.ts`
- `src/lib/cards/readModels.ts`

**2. Phase 1 — Foundation and migration tooling**

Phase 1 established canonical roots, immutable versions, repositories, explicit resolution contexts, ownership boundaries, transactions and migration tooling.

**Identity and versioning**

A Card’s identity is `cardTemplateId`, independent of title, position or Deck membership. A Deck stores ordered references to Cards.

Published Deck references additionally record `cardVersionAtPublish`. This supports exact historical reconstruction, but does not replace a user’s independent Card adoption.

Resolution contexts are deliberately different:

- Creator: current owned drafts, with published baselines.
- Working: adopted Deck version and each Card’s globally adopted personal version.
- Preview: published template content without personal-state creation.
- Historical: exact Deck version and recorded Card-version references.

Working mode must never silently substitute the latest version.

**Step reservations**

Card roots contain a `stepIds` reservation array. A unique partial multikey index prevents another Card root reserving the same Step ID.

Published/history-associated reservations remain held even when later content no longer contains that Step. The construction-time transfer operation is the narrow exception that transfers reservations between genuinely eligible unpublished Cards.

Mongo’s multikey index does not independently prohibit repeated values inside one document; domain validation also checks duplicate Step identities.

**Publication boundaries**

Card publication creates only a Card version. Deck publication creates only a Deck version and does not publish Card drafts.

Publication uses revision checks and Mongo transactions. Publishing advances the publisher’s existing personal adoption where applicable, including archived memberships, without resetting learning state or unarchiving.

Other users do not silently advance.

**Migration tooling**

The raw-data audit and migration planner use current live legacy content, rather than authentication normalization or old saved versions.

The legacy migration policy is deliberately different from normal learning continuity:

- preserve canonical content and personal back-of-Card media;
- preserve sharing metadata;
- reset legacy demo completion to `todo`;
- reset signals to Step-linked null readings;
- discard other agreed legacy demo learning state.

Planning records source fingerprints, stable generated mappings and a validated target graph. Reusing a plan preserves allocated IDs and rejects source drift.

The current apply utility:

- permits explicitly named disposable local targets only;
- refuses conflicting or partial targets;
- creates indexes separately;
- inserts the target document graph in one transaction;
- validates the resulting target;
- recognizes an already identical target.

There is no production apply/cutover mode. The planner’s database-source CLI is also currently local-only; read-only Atlas planning remains a future cutover task.

Review files:

- `scripts/audit-pre-library-migration.mjs`
- `scripts/migrate-first-class-cards.ts`
- `scripts/migration/plan.ts`
- `scripts/migration/apply.ts`

**3. Phase 2 — Private vertical slice and scoped persistence**

Phase 2 moved the actual private Creator → publication → working Deck flow onto these boundaries.

**Creation and drafts**

New Creator sessions start locally with a stable Deck ID and zero Cards. Opening an untouched session creates nothing in Mongo.

Shared defaults are centralized:

- Deck: `My Next Path`
- Card: `My Next Card`
- themes and cadence defaults.

Repeated saves update one current draft, without creating draft history.

First publication requires a nonblank, outer-trimmed title different from the appropriate default. Internal whitespace is not normalized. Later publication compares saved draft content with the latest published baseline.

There is no content-completeness requirement. Sparse Steps, duplicate Card titles and zero-Card Decks are valid. Every referenced Card must nevertheless have a published version before Deck publication.

**Per-entity persistence coordinator**

Creator has one persistence lane for the Deck and one per stable Card identity.

Each lane tracks desired content, acknowledged content/revision, edit generations, in-flight work, retries, creation dependencies and publication recovery.

Key guarantees:

- one save in flight per entity;
- newer edits coalesce;
- old responses cannot overwrite newer local content;
- transient retries are bounded, approximately 1/3/8 seconds;
- validation/auth failures are not blindly retried;
- revision conflicts preserve local edits and stop automatic overwrites;
- uncertain outcomes reconcile before replay.

Atomic Add Card renders immediately, then creates the Card/default draft, reserves Step IDs and attaches the reference transactionally. Immediate Card edits wait behind creation. Rapid structural operations serialize.

Detached Cards continue saving independently. Exhausted detached failures currently have no special recovery UI; that is an explicit deferred limitation.

**Scoped publication**

Individual Card publication flushes that Card and necessary creation dependencies.

Deck publication flushes Deck composition and structural dependencies, not unrelated Card drafts.

A warning combines persisted Card drafts with known pending/failed local Card changes. Confirmation is tied to Deck revision, ordered references and relevant Card publication/draft state; the server rechecks persisted state.

“Publish and leave” coordinates independent transactions. Earlier successful publications survive later failures; recovery should publish only remaining work.

**Read models and navigation**

My Drafts derives unfinished owned canonical work, independently of personal membership. Switching waits for relevant saves/uploads and stays in Creator if local work cannot be preserved.

My Decks uses personal membership and adopted versions, not ownership. Empty working Decks retain Deck controls but omit the Card scene.

The cadence anchor is established once on the first successful working open, including an empty Deck.

**Media boundaries**

Canonical media and personal CardData media are distinct. New personal image paths use stable user/Card identity.

Async upload targeting uses stable Card/Step identity, so removal or positional renumbering cannot redirect a completion callback to another Card.

Cloudflare services are mocked in disposable browser testing. Real provider processing, cleanup and delivery-security behaviour are not proven by those mocks.

Principal files:

- `src/components/creator/creatorPersistenceCoordinator.ts`
- `src/components/creator/CreatorDragLab.tsx`
- `src/components/creator/cardArchitectureAdapter.ts`
- `src/lib/cards/creatorDefaults.ts`
- `src/lib/cards/publicationRules.ts`
- `src/lib/cards/creatorDrafts.ts`
- `src/lib/cards/uploadAuthorization.ts`
- `src/lib/cards/workingCardStore.ts`

**4. Phase 3 — What is now implemented**

Phase 3 had three checkpoints.

**Checkpoint 1: personal lifecycle correction**

Canonical creation, drafting and ordinary Card publication do not create personal records merely because content exists.

Personal Deck entry transactionally establishes DeckData and missing CardData, pinning versions before the user opens the Deck.

Existing CardData wins over a newly encountered version of the same Card. Existing archived DeckData is reactivated without replacing adoption.

Ordinary first private Deck publication is the approved exception that also enters the owner’s My Decks. Public publication alone creates no new membership.

My Decks ordering is:

1. never opened first;
2. those ordered by DeckData creation time descending;
3. opened Decks ordered by `openedAt` descending;
4. stable ties.

**Checkpoint 2: owned Card reuse**

`Copy to…` attaches the same Card identity to another owned persisted Deck. It does not clone canonical content or duplicate personal state.

Destinations include published, unpublished and archived owned Decks; current Deck is excluded and already-containing destinations are disabled. Copy never unarchives.

Copy automatically publishes the destination change only when:

- the destination was published and clean before Copy;
- the copied Card has a published version;
- normal publication prerequisites pass.

Copy plus eligible publication occurs in one transaction, preventing an unrelated concurrent Deck edit being swept into publication.

An outstanding Card draft is not published as a side effect. Draft-only Copy creates no personal records; auto-publication into an existing personal Deck can initialize missing CardData through normal membership/publication handling.

An immutable operational Copy receipt identifies the exact auto-publication outcome. It is outside semantic content comparison.

**Permanent construction restriction**

Cross-Card Step movement ends permanently after publication, published-source fork provenance, or successful reuse.

`firstReusedAt` records the permanent lifecycle fact. `referenceRevision` provides a common Card-root write for reference mutations so reuse and Step movement cannot both commit against stale exclusive-construction assumptions.

Removing another Deck’s reference never restores eligibility. Within-Card reordering retains identity.

**Checkpoint 3: canonical fork foundations**

Backend operations support:

- Card fork;
- Deck fork;
- combined Deck + edited Card fork;
- Card fork attached through exact replacement in an owned Deck draft.

There is no foreign-edit UI yet.

Fork creation:

- uses the explicitly selected immutable source version;
- includes the first meaningful edit;
- creates owned unpublished roots/drafts;
- uses stable caller-supplied target identities;
- creates no DeckData/CardData;
- preserves canonical media references;
- retains unchanged Card identities.

Each forked Step receives a new ID and immediate-source lineage:

```ts
forkedFrom: {
  cardTemplateId: string;
  version: number;
  stepId: string;
}
```

Owner identity is not duplicated in Step provenance. Fork-of-fork lineage points to the immediate source, permitting chain traversal.

**First Card-fork publication**

The successful transaction creates immutable v1, updates the root and, where eligible immediate-source CardData exists, creates target CardData pointing directly to v1.

It reads the actor’s committed source state transactionally at publication time, rather than freezing a snapshot at first autosave.

Completion—including `skipped`—signals and target date carry by validated stable identity. Missing mappings initialize normally. Rewording or replacing media does not reset continuing Step state.

My Decks-origin continuity additionally carries current reflection and establishes historical continuity. Library-origin forks do not automatically receive reflection or broader history continuity.

A Library-only Deck fork may therefore have no DeckData while one of its published forked Cards has inherited CardData.

**Historical continuity**

A personal `historySourceCardTemplateId` relationship connects immediate source records.

The actor-scoped history endpoint returns tests, chats and personal media in separate original-context segments:

- no physical duplication;
- no chat-container rewriting;
- source moderation/deletion reflected on subsequent reads;
- cycles rejected;
- segments returned once.

The response explicitly distinguishes current adoption from missing event-time attribution:

```ts
currentAdoptedCardTemplateVersion: number;
eventVersionAttribution: "not-recorded";
```

This is a history read model, not a full learning-event log.

**Self-use Deck forks**

First publication explicitly chooses personal entry versus canonical-only publication.

Personal entry creates separate DeckData, retains the original membership, carries cadence and valid/remapped active Card, leaves `openedAt` null, and inherits neither archive state nor sharing recipients.

Existing CardData is reused; missing records are initialized.

Card and Deck publication remain independent. The containing Deck cannot publish before its new forked Card has a published version.

First-publication receipts recognize exact committed v1 after lost responses. Recovery must not create v2, duplicate target personal data or refresh inherited values over subsequent target edits.

Review files:

- `src/lib/cards/cardReuse.ts`
- `src/lib/cards/forks.ts`
- fork/publication/history API routes;
- `tests/card-reuse.integration.ts`
- `tests/card-forks.test.ts`
- `tests/card-forks.integration.ts`
- `tests/phase2/fork-foundations.browser.ts`

**5. Phases 4–7 — Technical preview**

These are agreed directions, not completed implementations or fully specified contracts.

| Phase | Intended technical work | Main risk |
|---|---|---|
| **4: public publication + minimal Library** | Wire existing visibility/publication rules, template-only preview and authenticated Import/Get Started personal entry | Mixing preview/latest versions, historical pins and existing global Card adoption |
| **5: cross-owner editing + Card/Deck Update** | Connect foreign editing to first-autosave fork transactions; add explicit adoption transitions and history-aware working presentation | Wrong fork source, state leakage between identities, partial multi-entity recovery |
| **6: Framework → Area → Item + direct Item tests** | Introduce taxonomy identities, Card mappings and assessment boundaries | Conflating content placement, reusable Card identity and assessed learning identity |
| **7: full Library/discovery** | Add search/filtering, richer previews, themes/categories and potentially Framework-aware discovery | Query/index growth, private-data exposure and denormalized search drift |

**Phase 4 specifics**

Import and Get Started share the same transactional personal-entry operation; only navigation differs.

Entry must preserve existing CardData adoption. Encountering Card v3 through a new Deck must not silently advance existing CardData at v1.

Archived re-import preserves the existing adoption and reactivates membership.

Public visibility is monotonic. Public Decks must not expose private Cards. Owned private references can be promoted through valid public publication; foreign references must already be public.

An important review point is current version selection:

- preview resolves latest published Cards;
- historical Deck resolution uses `cardVersionAtPublish`;
- entry initializes missing CardData from current published Card roots;
- existing CardData preserves its own adoption.

Claude should verify that these distinctions give coherent preview-to-import behaviour under concurrent publication.

**Phase 5 specifics**

Editing foreign content should fork what the user is actually viewing, not automatically the latest source version.

The existing private Creator DTO intentionally rejects foreign editing. It must be extended deliberately rather than bypassed.

Coordinator integration must handle the identity transition from source Card to owned fork, including queued saves/uploads, new Step IDs, reference replacement and uncertain creation outcomes.

Card Update changes global per-user adoption for that Card identity across Decks. Deck Update changes Deck composition independently. Both must preserve appropriate existing personal state, retained CardData and archive semantics.

Normal Step identity continuity preserves completion/signals. Defensive identity intersection handles exceptional mismatches; title/position matching is prohibited.

**Phase 6 specifics**

No final taxonomy schema is implemented. Claude should evaluate:

- whether mappings attach to stable Card roots, immutable versions or another explicit relation;
- how taxonomy changes affect historical interpretation;
- the distinction between direct Item tests and existing Card-level test history;
- avoidance of duplicate evidence/counting across reused and fork-related Cards.

Progress aggregation remains later work.

**Phase 7 specifics**

The minimal Library’s import/publication semantics should already be proven. This phase should primarily improve discovery.

Search infrastructure, pagination and indexes should follow actual query requirements. Personal data must not enter public search projections. Any denormalization needs explicit invalidation and version semantics.

**6. Highest-value second-opinion questions**

These are review targets, not assertions that defects exist.

1. **Mongo snapshot isolation versus stronger concurrency guarantees.**
   Examine publication consent checks and reference invariants for write-skew opportunities. Test dependency changes during the transaction, not only changes before revalidation. Which guarantees need common writes or stronger checks?

2. **Embedded personal arrays.**
   Assess User-document growth, Mongo’s document-size limit, contention between unrelated Card writes, and uniqueness enforcement. The current conditional updates are not equivalent to separate collection compound unique indexes.

3. **Uncertain-outcome recovery.**
   Verify that receipts and revision/content comparisons identify exact outcomes, including after later edits/publications. Ensure a retry cannot reinterpret an earlier draft-only result or replay inheritance.

4. **Coordinator interleavings.**
   Review creation, coalescing, publication locks, uploads, structural operations, detachment and navigation as a state machine. Look for dropped edits or unresolved promises that successful journeys may miss.

5. **Permanent reuse safety.**
   Verify every reference-adding path participates in the Card-root locking/marker protocol—not just Copy. Assess historical-reference query cost as version counts grow.

6. **History semantics.**
   Validate actor isolation, cycle protection, original context and deletion behaviour. Also examine the consequences of live source-history reads, including events added to a source after a fork.

7. **Media reuse and ownership.**
   Canonical forks retain original asset references. Future replacement/deletion must not destroy assets still referenced elsewhere. Review whether current upload authorization can safely support later foreign-edit integration.

8. **Version-resolution consistency.**
   Review latest preview, historical composition, global Card adoption and fork-source selection together. These are distinct concepts that must not collapse into one “current version”.

9. **Query scaling.**
   Canonical resolution and list queries are largely batched, but working-open preparation still performs per-Card lookups. History currently loads the actor’s personal arrays. Assess realistic scaling before proposing infrastructure changes.

10. **Production cutover readiness.**
    The local migration apply transaction is not a production strategy. Review transaction limits, index sequencing, drift detection, backups, validation, rollback and deployment coordination at the separate cutover gate.

**7. Verification evidence and limitations**

The recorded full Checkpoint 3 verification was:

- 210 unit tests;
- 91 disposable-Mongo integration tests;
- 124 E2E tests;
- 35 Phase 2 browser tests;
- passing typecheck, empty-Mongo build and both diff checks;
- zero lint errors, six existing warnings.

The subsequent history-response clarification reran unit tests, Phase 2 browser tests, typecheck, lint and diff checks successfully.

These are previous verification results, not tests rerun for this handoff.

Integration tests use transaction-capable disposable Mongo. Browser tests use mocked Cloudflare boundaries. Foreign editing is backend-tested; there is no real Library → foreign Creator browser journey yet.

Please prioritize missing invariants and adversarial interleavings over adding more tests that merely repeat successful flows.

**8. Deferred boundaries to preserve**

The following remain outside the completed architecture:

- production migration/cutover;
- foreign-edit and Update UI;
- standalone Card collection membership;
- full timestamped learning-event history;
- creator-requested Step-state resets;
- Progress aggregation;
- stronger Cloudflare delivery/privacy design;
- abandoned/replaced video cleanup;
- explicit keep-versus-replace source Deck UX.

CardData must not be treated as standalone Card collection membership. It represents personal state and may legitimately exist without any active Deck reference.

Please challenge technical mechanisms where a safer or simpler implementation exists, while keeping these identity, adoption, continuity and lifecycle requirements explicit.

> - The visibility change becomes effective only when that public version is successfully published.
> - Saving a draft must therefore not expose an invalid half-public state.

> ## P3 / P9 — public Decks cannot contain private Cards
>
> Firm product rule:
>
> - A public Deck may contain only public Cards.
> - A private Deck MAY contain public Cards.
> - The system must NOT automatically promote a private Card to public merely because it is added to or published inside a public Deck.
> - Copying a private Card into a public Deck must not silently expose it.
> - It is acceptable for such a Card to be present in the destination Deck draft if that is coherent with the current Creator model, but publication must remain blocked until the Card is explicitly made public.

> - completion / skipped
> - signal readings
> - reflection
> - target date
>
> Historical/contextual personal records are NOT physically copied:
> - chats
> - tests
> - personal media

> Instead, those records remain stored once against their original source CardData/context but must be DISPLAYED on the forked Card through the personal source/continuity relationship.
>
> If the user has no CardData for the source Card, there is naturally no personal state/history to inherit. This will be the normal Library case.

> Crucially:
> - this relationship and all of this personal data belong only to the forking user;
> - if the forked Card or Deck is public, other Library users must never see the forker’s completion, signals, reflection, target date, chats, tests or media;
