### Checkpoint 2 — Canonical Library read models and privacy boundary

**Objective**

Provide trustworthy canonical data and isolated viewer status before connecting Library UI.

**Scope and code areas**

- [resolvers.ts](./src/lib/cards/resolvers.ts)
- [readModels.ts](./src/lib/cards/readModels.ts)
- [versionAccess.ts](./src/lib/cards/versionAccess.ts)
- Library-specific read-model/DTO modules and authenticated API routes.
- Minimal query/index changes justified by the implemented queries.

**Implementation approach**

Create distinct canonical Library entry points rather than invoking an owner-capable preview resolver and hoping callers suppress privileges.

Canonical detail resolution will:

- require authentication;
- require eligible public canonical content even for its owner;
- resolve the latest published public Deck composition;
- resolve latest published public versions of its referenced Cards;
- enforce immutable-version visibility;
- return a coherent immutable selection and preview manifest;
- query no personal learning records.

A read-only snapshot transaction is an appropriate way to obtain a coherent detail selection. It creates no personal state and does not guarantee that the preview stays current after the response—that is checkpoint 4’s responsibility.

Construct DTOs explicitly from allowed fields. Include canonical content, identity/version information, presentation attribution and required media metadata. Exclude drafts, draft intent, authoring revisions, recovery receipts, private fork context, personal ancestry, account internals and Mongo internals.

The preview manifest contains the Deck identity/version and exact ordered Card identity/version selections. The server verifies it later; it is not trusted as authorization.

Collection ordering uses successful public publication timestamps and a stable Deck identity tie-breaker. Root draft edits must not reorder Library. Bounded/cursor reads must preserve access to the eligible collection without adding discovery features or silently imposing a product limit.

Keep viewer-specific status separate. It provides membership state and eligible Card destinations without attaching learning data to canonical responses. Namespace it by authenticated user and disable shared caching initially.

Broken public content receives a safe unavailable entry where public eligibility can be established. Do not expose uncertain/private content merely to retain an entry. Authentication/database failures remain explicit errors.

**Deliverables**

- Authenticated canonical collection/detail APIs.
- Explicit public-only DTOs and preview manifests.
- Separate viewer-status API/read model.
- Publication-based ordering.
- Safe unavailable-content responses.

**Verification**

- Owner and non-owner Library reads reject private content.
- Private-era and missing-visibility versions fail closed.
- Draft intent/content and operational metadata are absent, including nested structures.
- Personal learning/history data never enters canonical responses.
- Empty public Decks resolve successfully.
- Draft saves do not affect ordering; timestamp ties are stable.
- Broken eligible entries remain diagnosable; database/authentication failures do not produce an empty Library.
- Batched reads avoid per-Card attribution/status queries.
- Existing privacy, fork, adoption and history integration suites.
- Typecheck, lint, build and diff checks.

**Acceptance criteria**

Canonical Library reads require authentication, contain no personal layer, select the agreed versions and create no records. Viewer status is isolated by user. No owner exception bypasses the public-only boundary.

**Risks and safeguards**

Avoid reusing database-shaped sanitized responses as the DTO. Avoid promising snapshot pagination across a changing catalogue: use stable cursors and identity handling without treating browsing as a locked dataset.

**Review gate**

Report DTO examples, query behaviour, privacy tests, ordering tests, indexes introduced and unavailable/error distinctions. No Library UI is required yet.

Keep effective visibility distinct in DTOs and UI. Visibility selection stages the next publication; successful publication alone changes effective access. Public-to-private demotion remains rejected server-side and unavailable in the control.

Use the compact Creator header areas for entity-specific controls, preserving the mobile layout and board-only panning.

### Checkpoint 4 — Add, Restore, preview freshness and targeted working open

**Objective**

Implement the canonical-to-personal transition with safe concurrency and recovery.

**Scope and code areas**

- [repository.ts](./src/lib/cards/repository.ts)
- Personal-entry command/result types and HTTP errors.
- Library Add/Restore routes.
- Existing archive/restore and working-open routes.
- Viewer destination eligibility read model.
- Disposable Mongo integration fixtures.

**Implementation approach**

**Add**

Within one transaction:

1. Authenticate and validate the user/model.
2. Handle existing membership without resetting adoption or turning Add into Restore.
3. For new entry, validate the displayed Deck/Card manifest and public-version access.
4. Perform real guard writes against the displayed roots.
5. Revalidate through transaction retries.
6. Create DeckData and only missing CardData.
7. Preserve every existing adopted Card version and personal state.
8. Return the adoption result captured by the transaction.

New CardData selects the latest published version verified for the preview. Existing CardData wins even when older. `cardVersionAtPublish` remains unchanged historical information.

Add leaves the Deck unopened, with no cadence anchor or cadence-generated dates. Existing initialization of canonical suggested dates remains governed by the current priority rules.

**Concurrency**

Use deterministic ordering for guard writes and examine overlapping Copy, construction and publication transactions. Preserve composition order independently.

Guard writes must not increment semantic authoring revisions or make Creator lanes stale. Publication conflicts through writing the same root documents; it need not modify the guard field.

Test actual controlled interleavings. A retry rechecks the manifest; it must not silently adopt a newly published selection.

**Restore and archive recovery**

The current entry helper also reactivates archives. Separate the command semantics while reusing safe initialization helpers.

Introduce the smallest membership lifecycle precondition needed for Archive/Restore retry safety—an internal counter is appropriate. Opening must not change that counter.

- Add retries never unarchive.
- Restore is deliberate and preserves adoption/state.
- Old Restore retries cannot reverse a later Archive.
- Validate retained canonical versions before successful Library Restore.
- Unavailable retained content produces a structured failure without deleting membership or switching versions.

No durable operation collection is planned.

**Targeted opening**

Extend normal `openWorkingDeck()` with optional `targetCardTemplateId`.

Validate active membership and the exact Card identity in its adopted composition before mutation. Perform normal first-open cadence/date initialization and set the requested Card active in the same operation.

Destination eligibility requires existing CardData plus an active eligible DeckData membership. Ownership, retained CardData alone and provenance similarity do not qualify.

**Deliverables**

- Freshness-safe Add and explicit Restore.
- Archive-safe retry/recovery.
- Transaction-captured adopted versions.
- Authoritative Card destination validation.
- Normal working opening directly at a selected Card.
- Zero-Card entry/open support.

**Verification**

Integration tests cover:

- stale Deck or any stale previewed Card blocks new Add;
- both orderings of Add versus Card/Deck publication;
- Copy auto-publication versus Add;
- concurrent same-Deck and shared-Card Adds;
- transaction rollback without partial records;
- lost Add response followed by Archive;
- lost Restore response followed by Archive;
- older CardData preservation and latest adoption for missing data;
- unavailable retained versions;
- zero Cards;
- unopened targeted opening, cadence/date priority and adopted versions;
- stale chooser destinations, archived membership and absent CardData.

Run existing adoption, personal lifecycle, Step reservation/reuse and privacy regressions, plus targeted working browser checks and standard static/build checks.

**Acceptance criteria**

No partial personal graph, duplicate personal record, silent upgrade, accidental restore or stale-preview entry occurs. Targeted opening follows normal first-open rules.

**Risks and safeguards**

This is the highest-risk transaction checkpoint. Guard writes add contention to shared roots; counters and acknowledgements must remain operational metadata. Test repeated transaction execution without external side effects.

**Review gate**

Report command contracts, guard/write ordering, lifecycle metadata, captured results, recovery outcomes and controlled concurrency evidence.

### Checkpoint 5 — Library surface, attribution, actions and media

**Objective**

Wire the approved user experience entirely through the verified shared presentation and backend contracts.

**Scope and code areas**

- Authenticated Library route and shell.
- Shared collection/detail/Card components from checkpoint 1.
- Library action, refresh and destination chooser components.
- Viewer-status/session integration.
- Attribution resolver/component.
- Published-media status authorization and existing player/readiness components.
- Working navigation integration.

**Implementation approach**

**Library presentation**

Use the existing collection and Deck scene, including introduction and instructional playback, responsive geometry, focus and appropriate animations.

Library shows no personal learning data and cannot flip to a personal back face. Canonical viewing performs no personal mutations.

Use canonical version/surface identity for presentation resets. Keep viewer-status state user-scoped and discard delayed responses from an earlier account.

**Primary Deck action**

| State | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Never added | **Add to My Decks** |
| Adding | **Adding to My Decks…** |
| Added/already active | **Open in My Decks** |
| Archived | **Restore to My Decks** |

Add and Restore remain in Library. Their success changes the primary action to Open.

On stale-preview rejection, show **Refresh preview / Cancel**. Refresh reloads the latest canonical selection and restarts at the beginning. Cancel preserves the current preview and creates nothing personal.

No personal Update action or temporary older-adoption explanation is introduced.

**Card-level opening**

- No eligible active destination: omit the action.
- One: open directly at that Card.
- Several: show the chooser.
- Distinguish identical titles using approved user-facing context, including creator/cover information.
- Revalidate the chosen destination on opening.

Opening displays adopted working content, even if Library showed a newer version. It neither imports the previewed Deck nor restores/updates anything.

**Attribution**

Display the current creator subtly at the bottom centre of every Card front. Fork attribution reveals only the immediate source owner. Resolve accounts in batches; missing accounts use a neutral fallback without exposing IDs.

Keep this separate from personal-history ancestry.

**Instructional media**

Add published-version-authorized status reads for canonical media. Verify that the requested asset belongs to the accessible immutable version.

Reuse existing playback. Poll only relevant active media while processing; stop appropriately. Do not poll every tile or mount personal readiness/upload interfaces.

Preserve the known mocked-media explanation and existing working playback behaviour.

**Deliverables**

The complete Bob/Alice public publication → preview → Add → working Deck journey, including Restore, Card navigation, attribution and safe processing-media presentation.

**Verification**

Browser tests cover:

- authenticated access and canonical-only preview;
- no personal mutation requests during full preview navigation;
- Add without opening or cadence initialization;
- Restore without opening/updating;
- stale preview Refresh/Cancel;
- one/multiple/no Card destinations;
- unopened targeted navigation;
- adopted versions differing from Library versions;
- account switches with delayed status responses;
- Library → My Decks → Library state isolation;
- zero-Card public Decks;
- unavailable public content;
- creator/immediate-source attribution and missing accounts;
- processing/ready/failed media and unauthorized status probing;
- no polling fan-out across tiles.

Repeat mobile/desktop geometry comparisons and full working gesture, flip, upload, date and learning-state coverage. Run all relevant integration and browser suites plus static/build checks.

**Acceptance criteria**

Library is visibly and functionally another surface of the shared presentation system. Its permitted differences match the product contract; My Decks remains unchanged apart from the approved attribution addition.

**Risks and safeguards**

Avoid stale session responses, accidental personal mounting, navigation-to-wrong-version and geometry drift. Compare the same content across surfaces rather than relying only on screenshots or selector presence.

**Review gate**

Report the complete journeys, responsive/geometry evidence, network absence-of-write assertions, attribution/media behaviour and any remaining diagnostics. You manually review Library and My Decks.

## D. Risk and dependency assessment

| Risk | Addressed in | Safeguard |
|---|---|---|
| Working presentation or gesture regression | 1, 5, 6 | Baseline geometry; shared components; navigation/mutation separation; complete working browser coverage |
| Personal side effects during Library rendering | 1, 2, 5 | Structural exclusion; isolated store/queues; canonical DTOs; network assertions |
| Visibility autosave/publication races | 3, 6 | Complete save snapshots; generation-aware confirmation/recovery; immediate-publication tests |
| Stale preview accepted during publication | 4, 6 | Root guard writes; authoritative manifest validation; controlled transaction interleavings |
| Add/Restore retry reverses Archive | 4, 5 | Distinct commands; membership lifecycle preconditions; lost-response tests |
| Adopted version silently advances | 2, 4, 5 | Separate canonical/personal resolution; existing CardData precedence; immutable-version regressions |
| Private-era content exposure | 2–5 | Public-only Library boundary; immutable-version authorization; fail-closed metadata |
| Account/cross-surface contamination | 1, 2, 5 | User-scoped status, delayed-response rejection, version/surface presentation identity |
| Video status becomes arbitrary UID probing | 5 | Authorize referenced assets through accessible immutable content |
| Excessive transaction/query cost | 2, 4, 5 | Batched reads; bounded collection queries; measured guard contention; lazy media requests |

Preserve current embedded personal storage. Document document-size/write-contention debt without redesigning it in Phase 4.

Asset delivery security remains deferred: application authorization cannot revoke a previously known public delivery URL. No newly discovered immediate exposure should be dismissed under that limitation.

Phase 5 continues to own foreign-edit identity handoff, personal Update and adoption UX. Phase 7 owns full discovery. Neither is required to make this phase internally correct.

| Approved amendment category | Checkpoints |
|---|---|
| Shared presentation and personal-component isolation | **1**, verified again in 5–6 |
| Content-plus-visibility persistence and publication | **3**, integrated in 5–6 |
| Preview freshness, guard writes and transaction ordering | **4**, exercised through 5–6 |
| Distinct Add/Restore and safe personal adoption/recovery | **4**, user flows in 5 |
| Targeted normal working opening | **4**, chooser/navigation in 5 |
| User/session and working-store isolation | **1–2**, end-to-end verification in 5 |
| Batched attribution and authorized lazy media status | Data boundary in **2**, functionality in **5** |
| Race, privacy, geometry and working regressions | Embedded in **every checkpoint**, complete gate in **6** |

The additional review findings are also covered:

- absent dates silently becoming today → checkpoint 1;
- Step navigation depending on completion callbacks → checkpoint 1;
- sanitized database responses versus allow-listed DTOs → checkpoint 2;
- stale chooser eligibility → checkpoints 4–5;

No uncovered blocker or new `QUESTION FOR USER` remains.

> # Phase 4 — Begin Checkpoint 1: Shared Presentation Foundation
>
> I approve your final six-checkpoint Phase 4 implementation plan.
>
> You are now authorized to **implement Checkpoint 1 only: Shared Presentation Foundation**, as described in Section C of your approved plan.
>
> Do not begin Checkpoint 2 or any subsequent checkpoint until I explicitly authorize it.
>
> ## Your objectives
>
> Implement the shared presentation foundation that will support both My Decks and Library without duplicating the existing Card and Deck UI.
>
> This checkpoint must preserve the current My Decks experience while enabling canonical content to be presented independently of personal learning state.
>
> Follow the approved plan, including its acceptance criteria, verification requirements and review gate.
>
> ## Implementation priorities
>
> ### 1. Establish the baseline first
>
> Before modifying components:
>
> - Inspect the current working tree and branch.
> - Identify any existing uncommitted changes; do not overwrite unrelated work.
> - Run the relevant existing verification suites and record their results.
> - Capture representative My Decks layout and geometry baselines at mobile and desktop widths.
> - Identify the current ownership and lifecycle of working upload controllers, media players, queues, Card gestures and navigation.
>
> This baseline is important because My Decks must not suffer visual or functional regressions.
>
> ### 2. Separate canonical presentation from personal learning state
>
> Introduce explicit, well-typed presentation inputs that distinguish:
>
> - Canonical Deck/Card content and instructional media.
> - Optional personal learning projections.
> - Navigation capabilities.
> - Personal mutations and working-only functionality.
>
> Do not fabricate DeckData, CardData, target dates, completion states or progress values to make canonical content fit existing working interfaces.
>
> Preserve existing Card/Deck calculations and behaviour for My Decks.
>
> Use the simplest coherent architecture supported by the repository. Prefer typed props and composition before adding Context or new architectural abstractions.
>
> ### 3. Isolate personal functionality
>
> Ensure canonical rendering does not mount or initialize:
>
> - Personal back-face content.
> - Personal editors.
> - Upload controllers.
> - Personal mutation queues.
> - WorkingCardStore integration.
> - Personal learning-state effects.
>
> The shared presentation system should remain capable of supporting a future canonical back face without enabling the personal working back face.
>
> Do not remove or disrupt the existing working functionality.
>
> Preserve in-flight uploads, player state and appropriate component lifetimes.
>
> ### 4. Separate Step navigation from completion
>
> Canonical users must be able to navigate instructional Steps without having personal mutation capabilities.
>
> Remove the existing dependency between Step navigation gestures and completion callbacks.
>
> Do not use fake completion callbacks as a workaround.
>
> Preserve existing Step navigation, touch behaviour, completion interactions and positioning in My Decks.
>
> ### 5. Preserve presentation geometry
>
> Canonical presentation must omit personal indicators without shifting the remaining content.
>
> Pay particular attention to:
>
> - Deck tiles and collection layout.
> - Card headers.
> - Card progress indicators.
> - Step progress indicators.
> - Personal date slots.
> - Introduction and instructional content.
> - Focused Card positioning and transitions.
>
> No invented dates, zero-progress indicators, signals or hidden interactive personal controls should appear in canonical rendering.
>
> Preserve existing animation and gesture behaviour.
>
> Avoid broad CSS changes or unrelated visual redesign.
>
> ### 6. Use canonical fixtures, not a temporary Library
>
> Create the tests and fixtures necessary to demonstrate that canonical Cards and Decks render correctly through the shared presentation system.
>
> Do not implement a temporary Library page, Library data APIs, publication controls or Add/Restore functionality during this checkpoint.
>
> Those belong to subsequent approved checkpoints.
>
> ## Verification requirements
>
> Run the verification specified in your Checkpoint 1 plan, including:
>
> - Unit/component tests for canonical versus working presentation.
> - Tests showing navigation works without completion mutation.
> - Assertions that canonical rendering does not initialize working-only controllers, queues or stores.
> - Tests proving absent personal information cannot leak into canonical rendering.
> - Mobile and desktop geometry comparisons against the recorded baseline.
> - Relevant existing My Decks browser regressions.
> - Working gestures, flips, Step interactions, dates and instructional media.
> - Personal upload functionality and in-flight lifecycle behaviour.
> - Typecheck, lint, empty-Mongo build and applicable diff checks.
>
> Use the existing test infrastructure where practical.
>
> If a baseline test already fails before your changes, document it rather than silently changing unrelated functionality.
>
> ## Implementation discipline
>
> This is a foundational refactor, so prioritize controlled changes over unnecessary restructuring.
>
> - Work within the approved Checkpoint 1 scope.
> - Reuse and preserve working code wherever possible.
> - Avoid introducing a new generalized rendering framework.
> - Do not duplicate Card/Deck presentation components for canonical use.
> - Do not modify the personal data model unnecessarily.
> - Do not change established product rules.
> - Do not start implementing later checkpoints opportunistically.
> - Do not make unrelated fixes without explaining why they are necessary.
> - Do not use broad global CSS replacements or speculative cross-component edits.
>
> If you discover a material architectural conflict that cannot be resolved within the approved plan, explain it and ask before making a significant departure.
>
> For ordinary technical decisions within scope, use your judgment and proceed.
>
> ## Completion report and stopping point
>
> When Checkpoint 1 is complete, provide:
>
> 1. **Implementation summary:** What changed and the resulting shared presentation boundary.
> 2. **Files changed:** Important files and their responsibilities.
> 3. **Tests:** Exact verification commands, results and any failures.
> 4. **Geometry evidence:** Mobile/desktop baseline comparisons and any intentional differences.
> 5. **My Decks regression assessment:** Gestures, dates, flips, Step navigation, media, uploads and working state.
> 6. **Canonical rendering evidence:** Confirmation that it renders without personal data, personal controllers or mutation effects.
> 7. **Deviations and risks:** Any unresolved problems or follow-up work.
> 8. **Manual review checklist:** Exactly what I should inspect in the running application.
>
> Keep the changes reviewable and leave the working tree in a clearly reported state.
>
> **Stop after Checkpoint 1. Do not begin Checkpoint 2, even if all tests pass. Wait for my explicit approval.**

Checkpoint 1 is complete and ready for review. **No Checkpoint 2 work has begun, and nothing has been committed.**

1. **Implementation summary**

   Canonical and working Decks now share the existing presentation components.

   Canonical inputs contain content and immutable version identity without fabricated personal records, dates or progress. Working state, persistence, editors and uploads remain behind working-only adapters. Step navigation works independently of completion callbacks.

2. **Important files changed**

   - [presentation.ts](./src/components/decks/presentation.ts): typed canonical/working inputs and identities.
   - [DeckScene.tsx](./src/components/decks/DeckScene.tsx): shared Deck layout, navigation, gestures and introduction player.
   - [DeckDetail.tsx](./src/components/decks/DeckDetail.tsx) and [useWorkingDeck.ts](./src/components/decks/useWorkingDeck.ts): working adapter, optimistic state, store integration and mutation queues.
   - [FocusedCardView.tsx](./src/components/decks/FocusedCardView.tsx) and [WorkingFocusedCardView.tsx](./src/components/decks/WorkingFocusedCardView.tsx): shared focused presentation separated from personal back faces, editors and uploads.
   - Existing Deck tiles, Card fronts, Step components and semantic anchors now accept canonical content.
   - [globals.css](./src/app/globals.css): narrow, non-interactive layout placeholders.
   - Tests, canonical fixtures and recorded geometry baselines added. `esbuild` is now an explicit test dependency.

3. **Verification**

   The starting working tree was clean on `refactor/first-class-cards-phase-4-7`. All baseline suites passed.

   | Command | Result |
   |---|---|
   | `npm run test:unit` | 229 passed |
   | `npm run test:integration` | 111 passed |
   | `npm run test:e2e` | 124 passed |
   | `npm run test:phase2` | 42 passed |
   | Focused presentation browser suite | 3 passed, including expanded media checks |
   | `npm run typecheck` | Passed |
   | `npm run lint` | 0 errors; 6 unchanged baseline warnings |
   | `MONGODB_URI='' MONGODB_DB='' npm run build` | Passed |
   | Both diff checks | Passed |

   Existing warnings concern three image elements, two unused player diagnostic arguments and one Stream-player effect dependency. No suppressions were added.

4. **Geometry evidence**

   Comparisons passed at **390×844** and **1440×900**, within a one-pixel tolerance against the recorded working baseline.

   Canonical comparisons cover collection layout, Card placement, visible titles, introduction content and Step geometry. Personal indicators are omitted; empty slots preserve spacing.

   - Mobile: [working](<./phase2-test-results/artifacts/presentation-foundation.br-e7450-g-presentation-geometry-390/working-390.png>) · [canonical](<./phase2-test-results/artifacts/presentation-foundation.br-e7450-g-presentation-geometry-390/canonical-390.png>)
   - Desktop: [working](<./phase2-test-results/artifacts/presentation-foundation.br-1af18--presentation-geometry-1440/working-1440.png>) · [canonical](<./phase2-test-results/artifacts/presentation-foundation.br-1af18--presentation-geometry-1440/canonical-1440.png>)

5. **My Decks regression assessment**

   Existing browser coverage passed for completion, signals, dates, reflection, personal media, flips, history, reopening and archive/restore.

   A new controlled-upload test proves that navigating between focused Cards does not cancel the upload or move its metadata onto another Card. Media checks also confirm that introduction viewing and instructional Step navigation preserve native player identity.

6. **Canonical isolation evidence**

   Canonical browser fixtures:

   - navigate Steps without completion callbacks;
   - display no personal dates, progress or mutation controls;
   - mount no personal back face or editors;
   - make no personal API requests.

   A bundle check rejects dependencies on the working store, working adapters, personal back-face component, upload controller or mutation queue.

7. **Deviations and remaining risks**

   No backend, schema, publication, adoption or personal-lifecycle changes were required. No Library route or API was introduced.

   Media delivery is mocked in automated checks; live Cloudflare playback still deserves manual confirmation. Geometry coverage is representative rather than exhaustive across every device and content length.

8. **Manual review checklist**

   In My Decks, check mobile and desktop:

   - collection → Deck → focused Card positioning;
   - vertical Card gestures and horizontal flips;
   - Step opening, Previous/Next and completion controls;
   - date adjustments, signals and reflection editing;
   - introduction/instructional playback and enlargement;
   - start an upload, close its modal, navigate Cards, then confirm the upload remains on its original Card.

   Canonical fixtures can be inspected using:

   ```bash
   npm run test:phase2 -- presentation-foundation.browser.ts --headed
   ```

All changes remain uncommitted. I’m stopping here pending your review and explicit authorization for Checkpoint 2.

Retained only test synchronization fixes in [presentation-foundation.browser.ts](./tests/phase2/presentation-foundation.browser.ts):
- Measure stable rendered frames, ancestor transforms and animation completion instead of accepting two identical timer samples.
- Wait for the media modal to leave the DOM before dragging.

**Established cause:** the old helper could accept an unfinished animation as settled. Headed execution exposed this more readily. Content viewport dimensions and device scale matched; native browser-window dimensions did not explain the failures.

**Verification:**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Final original headless run | **3/3 passed** |
| Headed with frame synchronization | **2/3 passed**—upload/navigation and desktop |
| Headed mobile without tracing | Passed once; not conclusive |
| Targeted lint, typecheck, both diff checks | Passed |

**Remaining reliability issue:** headed mobile sometimes retains a scene-frame height of **640px versus 633.7px**, despite settled transforms. Evidence points toward timing-sensitive scene-height measurement during the opening animation, but its precise cause remains unresolved. Tracing affects timing; disabling trace screenshots alone did not fix it.

Experimental trace settings and fixture changes were reverted. Application code, baselines and the **1px tolerance** remain unchanged. No commit, production access or Checkpoint 2 work.

Checkpoint 2 is complete and ready for review. **No Library UI or Checkpoint 3 work was implemented.** Nothing was committed, and no production/Atlas database was accessed.

**Implemented functionality**

Three authenticated, read-only APIs are available:

| Endpoint | Result |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/library/decks?limit=20&cursor=…` | Paginated public Library collection |
| `GET /api/library/decks/:deckTemplateId` | Latest canonical public Deck and Cards, plus preview manifest |
| `GET /api/library/viewer-status?deckTemplateId=…&cardTemplateId=…` | Current user’s membership/adoption metadata and eligible Card-opening destinations |

Canonical responses use explicitly allow-listed nested DTOs compatible with Checkpoint 1’s shared presentation components. They exclude drafts, authoring revisions, recovery receipts, personal learning state, personal history and internal ownership identifiers.

Preview manifests record the displayed immutable Deck version and ordered Card identities/versions.

**Privacy and version guarantees**

- Library applies public-only authorization even when the viewer owns the content.
- Private-era versions and versions without provable public visibility cannot supply Library content.
- Preview uses the latest published public Card versions. Historical `cardVersionAtPublish` values and existing personal adoption remain unchanged.
- Reads create no DeckData/CardData, cadence anchors, dates or opened-state updates.
- Canonical content is identical across authenticated viewers. Viewer status is a separate, user-scoped response.
- All Library responses use `Cache-Control: private, no-store`.

Collection ordering uses the immutable publication timestamp, descending, with Deck identity as a stable tie-breaker. Draft saves cannot reorder it.

Broken public content retains a safe unavailable entry. Responses do not reveal inaccessible Card identities/content or internal exceptions. Authentication and database failures propagate as errors rather than masquerading as an empty Library.

**Consistency and viewer status**

Read-only Mongo snapshot transactions keep Deck selection, Card versions and manifests coherent during concurrent publication. Queries batch roots, versions and attribution rather than loading them separately per Deck.

Viewer status derives Card-opening destinations from **active personal memberships and their adopted compositions**. It excludes archived Decks, ownership-only destinations and retained CardData without an eligible active Deck. Missing/inaccessible adopted versions cannot authorize an opening destination.

Attribution resolves current creator usernames and immediate-source creator usernames in batches, with `"Unknown creator"` as the neutral fallback.

**The ordering timestamp represents publication, not draft creation.** I verified that `publishedAt` is assigned inside the successful Deck publication transaction. Library sorts by that timestamp. See [publication code](./src/lib/cards/repository.ts:541) and [Library ordering](./src/lib/cards/libraryReadModels.ts:123).

Your example therefore orders correctly:

- **Monday:** Create/save a private draft. No immutable version exists yet.
- **Friday:** Publish publicly. The new immutable version receives Friday’s `publishedAt`, placing it ahead of Thursday’s publication.

If Monday instead meant **publishing a private immutable version**, Friday’s public publication creates a **new immutable version**, timestamped Friday. Monday’s version remains private permanently.

Draft saves do not change the ordering timestamp. No files were changed.

**Checkpoint 3 is complete and ready for review.** No Checkpoint 4 work or Library UI was implemented. Nothing was committed, and no production/Atlas database was accessed.

**What changed**

- Added compact Private/Public controls in the Deck header and each Card header.
- Visibility selects **next-publication intent**. Saving public intent does not expose content.
- Visibility now participates in each existing persistence lane’s dirty detection, generations, save snapshots, acknowledgements and uncertain-response reconciliation.
- Content and visibility changes coalesce safely. Older responses cannot replace newer local intent.
- First public publication requires an irreversible-publication confirmation. Cancel retains the saved draft.
- Publish and leave confirms the number of Cards and Decks becoming public, publishes Cards before the Deck, and retains earlier successes after a later failure.
- Retry excludes entities already successfully published. Changed public-publication generations require fresh review.
- Public controls become fixed after successful public publication; backend demotion protection remains authoritative.

Publish and leave remains available through the existing return-to-Decks flow, not as a separate page action.

**Privacy and compatibility**

The existing backend publication rules needed no changes:

- Public-intended drafts remain private until publication succeeds.
- Public Deck publication cannot promote private Cards.
- Private-era immutable Card and Deck versions remain private.
- Public publication alone creates no personal membership.
- Ordinary publication preserves completion/skipped state and signal readings.
- Successfully published content resolves correctly through Checkpoint 2’s canonical Library APIs.

No schema changes, migration, persisted confirmation flags or recovery receipts were introduced.

Checkpoint 4 is complete and ready for review. Changes are uncommitted. Checkpoint 5 and Library UI have not been started.

**Implementation and lifecycle guarantees**

- **Add:** `POST /api/library/decks/[deckTemplateId]/add` accepts the canonical preview manifest. It creates the Deck membership and missing CardData atomically, without cloning canonical content.
- **Existing personal state:** Matching CardData is reused unchanged, including older adopted versions, completion/skipped, signals, reflection, target dates, chats, tests and media.
- **Stale previews:** A new Add validates the displayed Deck version and every displayed Card version. A mismatch returns HTTP 409 with `LIBRARY_PREVIEW_CONFLICT`, `refreshRequired` and the latest safe manifest for the later Refresh/Cancel UI.
- **Restore:** A separate command restores the retained adopted composition. Missing or inaccessible retained versions prevent restoration without partial writes or silent upgrades.
- **Two-stage initialization:** Add/Restore do not establish cadence anchors, record opening, or generate cadence-based dates. Existing suggested-date and personal-date precedence remain intact.
- **Targeted opening:** The normal working-open endpoint accepts an optional `cardTemplateId`. It validates that exact identity against the active membership’s adopted Deck composition, performs normal first-open initialization, then selects the requested Card.
- **Empty Decks:** Add, Restore and opening work with no Cards and a null active Card.

**Concurrency and recovery**

Add acquires Card-root guards in stable identity order, followed by the Deck guard and personal writes. Deck publication and Copy auto-publication participate in that ordering. Competing publication forces transaction retry and renewed freshness validation.

These guards do **not** change Creator authoring revisions, content, visibility, publication timestamps or Library ordering.

Restore uses an optional `membershipRevision`, with absent existing values treated as zero. Archive/Restore advance it. Consequently:

- Concurrent requests cannot create duplicate personal records.
- An Add retry never restores an archived membership.
- A delayed Restore retry cannot reverse a later Archive.
- Results report the transaction’s actual adopted versions and authenticated viewer ID.

No migration, new collection or index is required.

**Files changed**

The 15 changed/new files cover:

- [repository.ts](./src/lib/cards/repository.ts): entry transactions, ordered guards and targeted opening.
- [libraryEntry.ts](./src/lib/cards/libraryEntry.ts): manifest validation, structured conflict and acknowledgement contracts.
- [model.ts](./src/lib/cards/model.ts): optional operational counters.
- New Library Add/Restore routes; existing working-open and membership routes.
- `http.ts`, `libraryReadModels.ts` and `readModels.ts`: error responses and membership revision metadata.
- [AppShell.tsx](./src/components/layout/AppShell.tsx): existing Restore sends its observed revision; presentation is unchanged.
- Three new test files and one updated personal-lifecycle regression assertion.

> cat > src/components/media/publishedVideo.ts <<'EOF'
> import type { CloudflareStreamVideoMediaItem } from "@/lib/media";
> export type VideoLoadGuard = (media: CloudflareStreamVideoMediaItem, signal: AbortSignal) => Promise<void>;
> // Created only for a selected canonical version. No mount-time requests or shared
> // personal cache. Polling lives only as long as this playback request does.
> export function publishedVideoGuard(kind: "card" | "deck", templateId: string, version: number): VideoLoadGuard {
>   const ready = new Set<string>();
>   return async (media, signal) => {
>     if (ready.has(media.assetId)) return;
>     while (!signal.aborted) {
>       const query = new URLSearchParams({ kind, templateId, version: String(version), assetId: media.assetId });
>       const response = await fetch(`/api/library/media/stream-status?${query}`, { signal, cache: "no-store" });
>       if (!response.ok) throw new Error("Published video status unavailable");
>       const status = await response.json() as { status: "ready" | "processing" | "failed" };
>       if (status.status === "ready") { ready.add(media.assetId); return; }
>       if (status.status !== "processing") throw new Error("Published video unavailable");
>       await new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => {
>         const cancel = () => { clearTimeout(timer); reject(new DOMException("Aborted", "AbortError")); };
>         const timer = setTimeout(() => { signal.removeEventListener("abort", cancel); resolve(); }, 2000);
>         signal.addEventListener("abort", cancel, { once: true });
>         if (signal.aborted) cancel();
>       });
>     }
>     throw new DOMException("Aborted", "AbortError");
>   };
> }

Checkpoint 5 is implemented and ready for review. **No commit was created, and Checkpoint 6 has not begun.**

**Implementation**

- Added authenticated `/library` collection and Deck detail pages using the existing `DeckGrid`, `DeckScene`, Card fronts, Steps, gestures and media players.
- Library renders canonical content only. Browsing does not initialize personal controllers, mount back faces, overlay learning state or issue personal writes.
- Added Add/Restore actions. Both remain in Library; successful actions change to **Open in My Decks**.
- Stale Add attempts show **Refresh preview / Cancel**. Refresh reloads canonical content and restarts navigation; Cancel preserves the preview.
- Added **Open Card in My Decks**, with eligibility revalidation, a destination chooser and normal targeted first-open initialization. Existing adopted versions remain unchanged.
- Added subtle Card creator attribution, with immediate-source attribution on request and neutral account fallbacks.
- Added safe empty/unavailable states and retained publication ordering.

**Implementation adjustments**

Published-video status reads now authorize the exact public immutable version and its media identifier. Requests start only when instructional playback is requested. Rerenders cannot restart authorization or accidentally retry failed reads.

Library actions also include a session-bound check: switching accounts between the browser’s authentication check and Add/Restore cannot apply the previous account’s action to the newly authenticated user. Background status responses cannot overwrite completed actions.

No publication, adoption, scheduling or personal-storage rules were changed.

**Important files**

- [LibraryShell.tsx](./src/components/library/LibraryShell.tsx), `LibraryDialog.tsx`, `libraryClient.ts`: Library actions, dialogs and request handling.
- [Library pages](./src/app/library/page.tsx): authenticated collection/detail, loading and error states.
- `DeckGrid`, `DeckScene`, `FocusedCardView`, `ActiveCardFront`, `DeckCard`: small shared-presentation extensions.
- [CardCreatorAttribution.tsx](./src/components/cards/CardCreatorAttribution.tsx), `creatorAttribution.ts`, `readModels.ts`: attribution rendering and batched account resolution.
- `AppShell`, `OverviewMenu`: Library navigation and targeted working opening.
- [libraryMedia.ts](./src/lib/cards/libraryMedia.ts), Stream-status route, `publishedVideo.ts`, `CloudflareHlsVideoPlayer`: authorized canonical playback readiness.
- `libraryHttp.ts`, Add/Restore routes: session checks.
- [Library browser tests](./tests/phase2/library-ui.browser.ts), unit/integration tests and shared geometry helper.

The investigation found a significant infrastructure gap, so I’ve stopped before changing application code, as requested.

**QUESTION FOR USER — how far should this amendment extend Creator?**

The fork backend exists, but the requested workflow is not fully supported:

- **Creator rejects foreign Card references.** [creatorDTO](./src/lib/cards/readModels.ts:21) raises `FOREIGN_EDIT_DEFERRED`. A correctly forked Deck retaining Bob’s Cards would therefore open as “Template not found.” This also affects an owner’s Deck containing another owner’s Cards.
- **Fork creation requires a meaningful edit.** [createDeckFork](./src/lib/cards/repository.ts:278) rejects an unchanged copy. Confirming Edit would need an explicit extension to this contract.
- **Creator’s persistence lanes assume editable owned Cards.** Safely editing a retained foreign Card requires the identity handoff previously deferred to Phase 5.
- **Creator publication is not wired for Deck forks.** It omits the required personal-entry choice and expects a different response shape from the existing fork publication endpoint.

Simply adding the menu action would produce a broken Creator experience.

The realistic options are:

1. **Limited Deck editing:** enable the confirmed Deck fork, structure editing and publication, while keeping foreign Card content read-only until Phase 5. This introduces a user-visible restriction requiring your approval.
2. **Complete editing:** bring forward the necessary foreign-Card editing and persistence handoff from Phase 5. This is substantially larger than a menu amendment.

**My recommendation:** option 1 for this checkpoint, with foreign Cards clearly read-only. If “editable copy” must include editing those Cards now, option 2 is necessary. Please confirm which scope you want before I proceed.

The underlying fork operations already preserve public Card references, enforce immutable-version authorization and avoid creating personal records during fork creation.

The approved Phase 4 plan did not include Library Edit. It focused on browse, preview, Add, Restore, and navigation into existing personal Decks. Cross-owner editing was deliberately reserved for Phase 5. Owner Edit from Library was not explicitly assigned to either phase, so that part is a planning omission rather than a regression.

| Stage | Owner editing | Non-owner editing |
|---|---|---|
| Now | Available from My Decks and by direct Creator URL in limited cases | Backend fork primitives only |
| End of approved Phase 4 | No planned change; Library still has no Edit action | Still unavailable through Library UI |
| End of Phase 5 | Should support normal same-identity editing | Planned seamless foreign editing with internal forks |
| End of all planned phases | Should remain available across applicable Library surfaces | Fork-based editing remains, with the fuller Library arriving in Phase 7 |

## 1. User owns the content

For an owned Deck, Creator saves and publication already retain the same `deckTemplateId`. Publishing creates the next immutable Deck version rather than a fork. Owned Cards likewise retain their `cardTemplateId` and publish independent new Card versions.

The Creator route does not require DeckData or My Decks membership. [CreatorEditPage](./src/app/creator/edit/[deckTemplateId]/page.tsx:27) resolves the canonical owned Deck directly. Therefore an owner can edit an owned public Deck without first adding it to My Decks.

There is one significant current limitation: [creatorDTO](./src/lib/cards/readModels.ts:21) rejects the entire Creator Deck when any referenced Card belongs to someone else. Consequently:

- An owner can currently edit a Deck without membership when all its Cards are also owned by them.
- An owner cannot currently open their Deck in Creator if it reuses another owner’s public Card.
- This conflicts with the established first-class ownership model and must be resolved as part of foreign-Card Creator support.

My Decks already exposes Edit for an editable Deck through [DeckMenu](./src/components/decks/DeckMenu.tsx:11). Library does not mount that menu.

For Cards, the backend supports ownership-based editing independently of Deck membership through [resolveCreatorCard](./src/lib/cards/resolvers.ts:114). However, there is no standalone Card Creator page. Card editing is currently reached through a Deck’s Creator board.

Classification:

- **Implemented:** Same-identity owner save/publication; membership-independent owner Deck route; ownership-based Card APIs.
- **Missing from Phase 4 UI:** Owner Edit action in Library.
- **Not implemented:** Standalone Card editing surface.
- **Genuine limitation:** Creator cannot currently open an owned Deck containing foreign public Cards.

## 2. User does not own the content

The backend foundations are substantial:

- Exact immutable source-version selection.
- Card, Deck, and combined Deck/Card fork transactions.
- New stable caller-supplied identities and retry recovery.
- Deck forks retaining unchanged original Card identities.
- Individual Card forks with new Step IDs and immediate-source lineage.
- Version-level authorization preventing private-era versions from being forked.
- Canonical fork creation without DeckData or CardData.
- Immediate-source attribution and immutable provenance.
- First publication producing fork version 1.

These are implemented in [repository.ts](./src/lib/cards/repository.ts:197) and exposed by the existing Card and Deck fork API routes.

What remains for Phase 5 is the Creator integration:

- Opening foreign content as an editable Creator session.
- Creating the Deck fork on the first meaningful persisted change.
- Transitioning the Creator coordinator from the foreign source identity to the new owned identity without losing edits.
- Keeping unchanged Cards as shared references.
- Forking an individual foreign Card only when that Card is edited.
- Switching the Deck reference to the new Card fork safely.
- Publishing forked Decks and Cards through the normal Creator controls.
- Handling retries, conflicts, uploads, navigation, and lane identity handoff.
- Adding the foreign Edit confirmation and Library/My Decks entry points.

The existing fork API deliberately requires meaningful edited content. [createDeckFork](./src/lib/cards/repository.ts:278) rejects an unchanged fork. That matches the earlier Phase 5 contract: pressing Edit begins a continuous editing experience, while the first meaningful autosave creates the fork.

## Planning gaps requiring a decision

1. **Owner Edit from Library**

   This was absent from the approved Phase 4 Checkpoint 5 scope and is not inherently Phase 5 work. The desired owner action is only an authorized link into the existing Creator route, subject to the foreign-Card limitation above. If it must exist at the end of Phase 4, it needs to be added explicitly to Phase 4 closeout.

2. **Non-owner fork timing**

   The established Phase 5 contract creates the fork on first meaningful autosave. The recent request said confirmation should precede “creating a fork,” which is compatible if confirmation occurs before entering the editable experience and creation still waits for the first edit. Creating an unchanged fork immediately on confirmation would change the established contract and backend invariant.

3. **Library-origin personal-state inheritance**

   Canonical fork creation creates no personal records. Under the previously locked Phase 3 contract, first publication of a Card fork may carry the forking user’s eligible source CardData, even for a Library-origin fork. The recent phrase “never copy personal learning data” is consistent if it refers only to opening/creating the canonical fork. If it is intended to prohibit the already-agreed publication-time carryover, that would be a product-policy change requiring an explicit decision.

4. **Standalone Card Edit**

   The backend supports independent Card ownership and forks, but the current UI is Deck-centered. A standalone Library Card/Edit surface is conceptually anticipated in the deferred standalone-Card work, but it is not firmly assigned to Phase 5 or Phase 7. Editing a Card encountered inside a Deck can be covered by Phase 5; independent Card editing remains an unassigned roadmap item.

5. **Owner Decks containing foreign Cards**

   The intended behaviour is clear: the owner edits the Deck identity normally, foreign Cards remain shared until individually edited. The current Creator blocks this. It belongs naturally with Phase 5’s foreign-Card Creator work, but the Phase 5 checklist should name it explicitly.

No code or files were changed during this clarification.

**Attribution positioning and scaling**

The focused attribution was positioned relative to the content container, whose height ends after the Steps. That placed the username around the middle of the physical Card.

I moved it directly into the focused Card’s front face, matching the active/past structure. Attribution now uses:

- **14px bottom spacing** at the Card’s base dimensions.
- The existing whole-Card scaling for focused and past views.
- A bounded, ellipsized label for long usernames, retaining the full accessible name and title.

Only these attribution-specific CSS selectors changed:

- `.card-creator-attribution`
- `.card-creator-attribution .card-creator-name` — new

Shared Card geometry and layout selectors were unchanged.

**Library-origin return navigation**

Library’s Edit link now passes `returnTo=library`. Creator maps that explicit origin to `/library` through its existing leave workflow.

Autosave previously replaced the URL and removed return parameters. It now preserves them, so the destination survives saves and reloads. My Decks entry retains its existing return destination; direct Creator entry returns to My Decks.

No persistence, leave-dialog or publication safeguards were bypassed.

> SUMMARY OF HIGH-LEVEL UNDERSTANDING
>
> My understanding is that Phase 5 is about allowing users to adopt updates to Cards and Decks, and to edit content created by other people through a seamless forking process.\
> \
> Phase 4 made published content available in Library, with Add/Restore and navigation into My Decks. Phase 5 should complete two important parts of that relationship: keeping adopted content up to date and making it possible to build on somebody else's work.\
> \
> \## 1. What users will be able to do\
> \
> \### A. Update Cards and Decks they have already added\
> \
> Imagine I add somebody else's basketball Deck to My Decks. A week later, its creator improves one of the Cards and publishes a new version.\
> \
> I should be able to:\
> \
> \- See that an update is available.\
> \- Review the update information before deciding whether to adopt it.\
> \- Update my existing Deck without having to remove and add it again.\
> \- Keep my existing progress, reflections, signals and other personal learning data.\
> \
> This applies independently to Cards and Decks.\
> \
> For example, a creator might update the instructions on a Card without changing the Deck structure. Alternatively, they might add, remove or reorder Cards within a Deck.\
> \
> The important distinction: publishing an update does not automatically force every follower onto the new version. Each user has their own adopted versions.\
> \
> Where a user is jumping across several published versions, we've previously agreed that the confirmation should show the non-empty update notes from all intervening versions, in chronological order.\
> \
> \### B. Edit somebody else's Deck\
> \
> Suppose I find a public Deck in Library that I like, but I want to adapt it.\
> \
> Original Deck\
> \
> Owned by another creator\
> \
> My editable Deck\
> \
> Created on first meaningful edit\
> \
> The intended user experience is:\
> \
> 1\. I choose Edit on somebody else's Deck.\
> 2\. I receive a confirmation explaining that editing will create my own version.\
> 3\. I enter Creator and make my changes.\
> 4\. On the first meaningful saved change, the system creates a new Deck owned by me.\
> 5\. I can continue editing and publish it through the normal Creator workflow.\
> \
> I don't have to manually duplicate the Deck and then navigate to the copy.\
> \
> Crucially, the original Deck is untouched. My Deck has a new identity, while retaining attribution to its immediate source.\
> \
> \### C. Reuse Cards without unnecessarily copying them\
> \
> This is particularly important to the first-class Card architecture.\
> \
> Imagine a public Deck containing four Cards:\
> \
> Original Deck — four shared Cards\
> \
> A\
> \
> B\
> \
> C\
> \
> D\
> \
> My adapted Deck — only Card B edited\
> \
> A\
> \
> B′\
> \
> C\
> \
> D\
> \
> Cards A, C and D remain references to the originals. Only B becomes a new owned Card.\
> \
> That means:\
> \
> \- Editing the Deck title, description or structure need not copy its Cards.\
> \- Unchanged public Cards remain shared references.\
> \- Editing another creator's Card creates a Card fork.\
> \- The new Deck is updated to reference that fork.\
> \- The new Card receives its own identity, while its Steps receive new identities as appropriate.\
> \
> This avoids unnecessary duplication and lets Cards genuinely be reused across many Decks.\
> \
> \### D. Editing your own Decks that contain other creators' Cards\
> \
> This is an important current limitation that Phase 5 should remove.\
> \
> As an owner, I should be able to open my Deck in Creator even when it includes Cards published by somebody else.\
> \
> I can change my own Deck normally. If I edit one of the borrowed Cards, the system should fork that Card and replace its reference in my Deck.\
> \
> My Deck itself does not need to be forked, because I already own it.\
> \
> \### E. Preserve personal learning progress\
> \
> The editing process must keep the distinction between canonical content and personal state.\
> \
> Creating a fork should not automatically create DeckData or CardData. Publishing a fork may invoke the previously agreed rules for carrying forward eligible personal CardData, but that is separate from creating the canonical fork.\
> \
> Similarly, adopting an update should reconcile existing user progress rather than discard it.\
> \
> \## 2. How I expect it to work technically\
> \
> There is already substantial backend support. Phase 5 is not starting from scratch.\
> \
> \| Area                | Expected approach                                                                                                                       |\
> \| ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\
> \| Immutable versions  | Every publish creates a new canonical Card or Deck version.                                                                             |\
> \| Adopted versions    | User state records which Card and Deck versions have been adopted.                                                                      |\
> \| Update discovery    | Compare the adopted version against the latest eligible published version.                                                              |\
> \| Update adoption     | Reconcile changed Card/Deck structures against existing DeckData and CardData, retaining applicable state.                              |\
> \| Deck forking        | Create a new owned Deck identity on first meaningful edit, referencing unchanged Cards.                                                 |\
> \| Card forking        | Create a new owned Card identity when a foreign Card is edited, then update the Deck reference.                                         |\
> \| Creator integration | Transparently switch from the source identity to the newly owned identity without losing edits or interrupting the Creator experience.  |\
> \| Safety              | Handle conflicting edits, retries, publication versions, media uploads and authorization, including protection of private-era versions. |\
> \
> The most delicate engineering work is likely to be the Creator identity handoff and update reconciliation, especially when a user has already completed Steps that a creator subsequently edits, removes or reorders.\
> \
> \## 3. What is outside Phase 5?\
> \
> As I understand the current roadmap, these remain separate:\
> \
> \- Standalone Card surfaces: independently displaying Cards in Library and My Decks, together with standalone Card editing in Creator. We have deliberately parked this as one piece of work.\
> \- Phase 7 Library discovery: broader browsing and discovery functionality.\
> \- Creator Preview Draft: previewing unpublished changes without first publishing them.\
> \- Test-history interface: displaying the historical test information stored in CardData.\
> \
> \## 4. Two distinctions worth confirming against the approved Phase 5 plan\
> \
> Our recent Codex investigation strongly established that foreign editing, fork-on-first-meaningful-change, and Creator identity handoff belong in Phase 5.\
> \
> The update-adoption functionality also belongs there based on our earlier architecture decisions, but I haven't independently checked the detailed Phase 5 checkpoint breakdown in this conversation.\
> \
> Likewise, the exact presentation of update availability — badges, menu actions, comparison views, and so on — is not something I would treat as already agreed unless it appears in that plan.\
> \
> Overall, I see Phase 5 as the point where published Cards and Decks become genuinely reusable and maintainable: creators can improve their work, followers can choose to adopt improvements, and other creators can build on it without overwriting or unnecessarily copying the original content.
