The agreed Phase 5 scope matches your understanding: **explicit Card/Deck Update adoption, plus seamless editing of foreign content through internal forks**. The main gaps are the Creator identity transition, follower adoption operations and several user-facing decisions that were deliberately deferred.

There is one documentation limitation: **I could not find a saved, approved Phase 5 checkpoint breakdown** in the current repository or its available Markdown/text history. I found the roadmap decisions and the explicit Phase 5 handoff requirement, but not a detailed implementation contract. The checkpoint sequence below is therefore a proposal for approval.

No files were changed, and no tests or database operations were run.

## Planning sources and current implementation

The most relevant planning record is [outstanding-tasks.md](./docs/design/outstanding-tasks.md:3). It explicitly assigns seamless first-edit identity handoff to Phase 5 and preserves the deferred history/reset work.

Some documentation conflicts with subsequent decisions:

- [README.md](./README.md:154) still describes null adoption, personal records created during drafting and automatic private-Card promotion.
- The older attached roadmap placed Card Update in Phase 4 and Frameworks in Phase 5.
- The current code and later approvals supersede those descriptions: positive personal adoption only, no personal records from canonical drafting, no implicit promotion, and Updates/foreign editing in Phase 5.

These are documentation discrepancies, not recommendations to restore earlier behaviour. Correcting the affected documentation should accompany the approved implementation.

The implementation is at the following point:

| Area | Already implemented | Phase 5 work remaining |
|---|---|---|
| Versions and adoption | Immutable versions, positive personal pointers, publisher adoption advancement | Explicit follower Card/Deck adoption commands |
| Update discovery | Membership update metadata and Card capability flags | Working-view actions, review and confirmation |
| Update notes | Notes stored on Card/Deck publications; chronological Card-note retrieval | Reviewed-version bounds, equivalent Deck retrieval and UI |
| Fork creation | Exact-version Card, Deck and combined transactions; stable IDs; lineage; recovery | Connect these operations to real Creator editing |
| Personal continuity | First-publication carryover and viewer-owned historical projection | Preserve these guarantees through the interactive workflow |
| Mixed ownership | Lower-level resolver can load foreign published Cards | Creator DTO currently rejects them |
| Creator persistence | Scoped saves, publication recovery, upload/navigation safeguards | Safe source-to-owned identity transition |
| Library Edit | Eligible owners can open existing content | Foreign editing and removal of the mixed-ownership restriction |

Relevant boundaries include [creatorDTO](./src/lib/cards/readModels.ts:21), [fork transactions](./src/lib/cards/repository.ts:184), [Card-note retrieval](./src/lib/cards/repository.ts:71) and the [persistence coordinator](./src/components/creator/creatorPersistenceCoordinator.ts:161).

## Proposed checkpoint plan

The product requirements below preserve our approvals. The checkpoint grouping, operation shapes and implementation mechanisms are recommendations. Each checkpoint would end with a report and require your approval before continuing.

| Checkpoint | Purpose | Dependency |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Update adoption foundations | Safe review and adoption contracts for Cards and Decks | Resolve Update policy questions |
| 2. My Decks Update experience | Expose independent Card/Deck Updates through working presentation | Checkpoint 1 |
| 3. Foreign Creator session and identity handoff | Extend Creator safely around existing fork transactions | Resolve editing-context questions |
| 4. Foreign editing, publication and reopening | Complete Library/My Decks editing journeys | Checkpoint 3 |
| 5. Full verification and acceptance | Validate the combined Phase 5 behaviour and prior phases | Checkpoints 1–4 |

### Checkpoint 1 — Update adoption foundations

**Previously approved behaviour**

- Card Update changes the user’s adopted version of the same Card identity.
- Because CardData is global per user/Card, that update applies everywhere the Card appears.
- Deck Update changes adopted Deck composition independently.
- Existing CardData remains intact, including older Card adoption when a newly added Deck reference encounters an already-used Card.
- Missing CardData is initialized for newly encountered Cards.
- Removed Deck references do not delete CardData.
- Continuing Step IDs preserve completion, skipped status and readings regardless of wording or media changes.
- Review includes non-empty intervening update notes chronologically.
- Library remains canonical-only and has no personal Update action.

**Recommended implementation**

Introduce explicit review and adoption operations alongside the current personal-data repositories. Do not revive the legacy reconciliation route.

A review should identify the current adoption, proposed immutable target, permitted update notes and—for Decks—the composition changes. Adoption must revalidate access and the reviewed preconditions transactionally.

Use field-level updates to the current personal records. Do not accept a client-supplied replacement CardData or DeckData. Preserve reflection, dates, media, chats, tests and history relationships.

For defensive Step reconciliation:

- Retain existing state by stable Step ID.
- Initialize genuinely missing current Step entries.
- Preserve retained state for identities no longer displayed.
- Never match by title or position.

The current model requires three Steps per Card. This work does **not** introduce a new Step add/remove interface.

Retries must not downgrade adoption, replay state initialization over later learning activity, duplicate records or reverse Archive. Exact repeated outcomes can be acknowledged; conflicting later transitions must return an explicit result.

**Tests and acceptance**

Cover skipped versions/notes, shared Cards across Decks, changed content with unchanged Step IDs, defensive identity changes, empty Decks, missing/private versions, concurrent learning edits, concurrent adoption, transaction rollback and lost responses.

No canonical content changes and no unrelated personal state is reset.

### Checkpoint 2 — My Decks Update experience

**Previously approved behaviour**

Updates are explicit and independent. The user reviews information before adoption; publishing upstream never forces follower adoption. Update controls belong in My Decks.

**Recommended implementation**

Reuse the existing Deck menu, working Card presentation and modal conventions. Exact placement and review detail need your decision below.

The confirmation should make the scope clear:

- Card Update affects that Card across the user’s Decks.
- Deck Update changes this membership’s composition and preserves existing Card adoption.
- An Update does not merge upstream changes into a separately forked identity.

Before replacing working content, safely settle relevant personal writes and uploads. A Deck Update that removes a Card must not invalidate an upload still depending on that Deck context.

Refresh affected working projections after success without resetting unrelated navigation or replaying stale cached state. Existing [workingCardStore](./src/lib/cards/workingCardStore.ts:11) version separation helps, but it does not itself implement an adoption transition.

**Tests and acceptance**

Browser coverage should include Card-only and Deck-only updates, shared Card effects, cancellation, pending/failed personal saves, uploads, repeated requests, archived membership races and navigating Library → older My Decks content → updated content.

Existing geometry, gestures, flips and personal media/history remain intact. Library receives no Update controls or personal overlay.

### Checkpoint 3 — Foreign Creator session and identity handoff

This is the highest-risk checkpoint.

**Previously approved behaviour**

- Edit opens a session; opening or cancelling does not create a fork.
- First meaningful persistence creates the necessary owned roots/drafts and includes the edit.
- Fork from the exact viewed immutable source.
- Every forked Step receives a new identity and immediate-source lineage.
- Unchanged Cards retain their identities.
- No personal records are created by fork autosave.
- Editing continues without reloads, lost keystrokes, duplicate Cards or misdirected uploads.

**Recommended implementation**

Extend the existing coordinator with a focused identity transition. Preserve the current save lanes and scoped recovery model.

Separate stable editing-session identity from canonical persistence identity. On a successful fork:

- Bind the existing editing session to the returned target identity.
- Install acknowledgements for the exact committed generation.
- Preserve and subsequently save newer local edits.
- Update Card/Step bindings, modal targets and upload ownership coherently.
- Update the URL without remounting the active Creator session.

Use one coordinated Deck-creation operation when several edits arrive before the first fork completes. A second Card edit must not create a second Deck fork.

The backend already supports first edited Card forks and reference replacement. It needs targeted extensions for gaps exposed by the real UI:

- **Add Card as the first change:** atomically create the new owned Card and forked Deck composition.
- **Media as the first change:** authorize/stage the upload for the intended owned target without writing to the foreign source or persisting an unchanged placeholder fork.
- **Mixed-ownership publication review:** expose published information for foreign Cards without disclosing their private draft state. Preserve stricter saved-generation checks for owned Cards.
- **Fork publication acknowledgements:** align the existing backend response with the coordinator’s acknowledgement/recovery contract.

The current [upload authorization](./src/lib/cards/uploadAuthorization.ts:6) requires an existing owned context, so media-first editing cannot simply reuse the current upload call unchanged.

**Tests and acceptance**

Exercise typing during delayed fork creation, multiple first edits, lost responses, duplicate requests, Card-only attachment, combined forks, Add-first and upload-first changes, cancellation, reference removal during an upload, publication during handoff and navigation with failures.

No request may mutate the foreign root. No successful retry may create an extra identity.

### Checkpoint 4 — Foreign editing, publication and reopening

**Previously approved behaviour**

- Owners continue editing existing identities.
- Owners can edit Decks containing foreign published Cards.
- Editing a foreign Card forks only that Card and replaces the intended Deck reference.
- Editing foreign Deck composition forks the Deck without cloning unchanged Cards.
- Public/private visibility and first-public confirmation retain their existing rules.
- Card and Deck publication remain independent.
- First Card-fork publication inherits eligible current personal state once, regardless of Library/My Decks origin.
- Historical events remain source-stored and viewer-private.
- Self-use Deck forks retain the source membership, carry approved cadence/navigation continuity and begin unopened.

**Recommended implementation**

Connect the approved entry points to Checkpoint 3’s session model and reuse the existing Creator board and edit modals.

Persist enough context to resume correctly through My Drafts. The policy for foreign Card versions on reopening needs confirmation; current Deck draft references contain only Card identities.

Use the existing explicit `forkEntry` publication boundary rather than inferring membership from ownership or source CardData. Wire it into publication and recovery according to the entry policy you approve.

Publish and leave must:

- Settle the relevant saves/uploads.
- Publish only owned outstanding entities.
- Never attempt to publish an unchanged foreign Card.
- Respect private-Card blockers on public Decks.
- Preserve successful partial publication and retry only unfinished work.

Keep immediate-source attribution and the permanent cross-Card movement prohibition for published, reused or fork-derived content.

**Tests and acceptance**

Complete two-user journeys from Library and My Decks, including owned Deck/foreign Card, foreign Deck/foreign Card, multiple edited Cards, untouched cancellation, abandoned drafts, reopening, mixed personal state, private-era access, partial publication and source-history privacy.

The foreign-content restrictions introduced for Phase 4 can then be removed where the new workflow supports them.

### Checkpoint 5 — Full verification and acceptance

Audit the implemented contract and run:

```text
npm run test:unit
npm run test:integration
npm run test:e2e
npm run test:phase2
npm run typecheck
npm run lint
MONGODB_URI='' MONGODB_DB='' npm run build
git diff --check
git diff HEAD --check
```

Include mobile/desktop geometry, two-account privacy, concurrent adoption/publication, account switching, interrupted fork recovery and media lifetimes.

Retain the known headed-mobile reliability exception and real-media verification limit unless separately resolved. All database verification remains disposable/local.

The completion report should distinguish application blockers, test limitations and deferred work. No production cutover or additional phase would begin automatically.

## Comparison with your summary

Your account of the overall scope is correct. These refinements matter:

| Your understanding | Alignment or clarification |
|---|---|
| Card and Deck updates are independent | Agreed. A Deck update must not silently update existing CardData. |
| Users retain their adopted versions | Agreed for followers. Existing publisher personal adoption already advances when that owner publishes; preserve this established exception. |
| Intervening notes appear chronologically | Agreed policy. Only Card retrieval exists today; Deck review support is unfinished. |
| Foreign editing creates owned content on first meaningful edit | Agreed. Clicking Edit alone must remain read-only. |
| Only edited foreign Cards fork | Agreed. Every Step in a forked Card gets a new ID, not merely the edited Step. |
| Step changes are a major reconciliation risk | Identity preservation is central, but normal Creator still has three fixed Steps. Defensive reconciliation must not become a new Step-management feature. |
| Fork publication may carry personal state | Already implemented: current completion/skipped, readings, reflection and target date; historical events remain source-stored. |
| Update may keep an adaptation current | Only against newer versions of the **same identity**. Updating a fork from its ancestor would be a different merge feature and is outside this phase. |
| Owners can edit mixed-ownership Decks | Explicit Phase 5 work; the current restriction is intentional, not a Phase 4 regression. |
| Standalone Cards, Preview Draft and test-history UI remain separate | Correct. None is needed to implement this scope. |

Your summary also leaves out several preserved requirements: source Deck membership remains active after a self-use fork, first-public confirmation applies to the new identity, cross-Card movement remains permanently restricted, and retained CardData/history must survive reference removal.

The unresolved areas are chiefly user experience and context selection—not a need to redesign first-class Cards.

## QUESTIONS FOR USER

**1. Can this proposed five-checkpoint sequence become the Phase 5 implementation structure?**

I found no detailed approved sequence to preserve. I recommend using the sequence above, with review after each checkpoint. If the earlier breakdown exists elsewhere, the alternative is to reconcile against that document first. **Blocks final approval of the plan, not the established scope.**

**2. Where should Update appear, and how much review should it show?**

Placement and comparison depth are not documented. I recommend a Deck Update action in the existing Deck menu and a compact Card Update action in the focused working Card. The modal would show chronological notes; Deck review would also summarize added, removed and reordered Cards. Card confirmation would explain that adoption applies across the user’s Decks.

Alternatives are additional overview/active-Card indicators or a richer content comparison. **Blocks Checkpoint 2; richer comparison can be deferred.**

**3. What happens if another version is published while an Update confirmation is open?**

The system must never silently substitute unreviewed content. I recommend Refresh/Cancel, consistent with the Library freshness pattern, when the proposed adoption selection becomes stale. The alternative is to adopt the exact reviewed version and immediately offer another Update.

For Deck review, this also affects newly encountered Cards whose latest versions change during confirmation. **Blocks the review/adoption contract in Checkpoint 1.**

**4. What should Deck Update do when it removes the active Card or changes cadence?**

Existing working opening falls back to the first Card when the saved active Card is invalid, and preserves the established cadence anchor and existing dates.

I recommend retaining those rules: keep a surviving active Card; otherwise select the first remaining Card, or null for an empty Deck. Preserve existing dates/anchor; initialize missing dates through the normal working-open path using the adopted composition and cadence.

The alternative is selecting the nearest surviving Card or introducing scheduling review. **Blocks Deck Update acceptance semantics in Checkpoint 1.**

**5. Should an unfinished Creator draft retain its selected foreign Card versions across reopening?**

Within a session, exact viewed-version forking is settled. Across reopening, the existing Creator resolver selects latest foreign publications, while Deck drafts store only Card IDs.

I recommend retaining the authoring session’s foreign-version selections across reload/My Drafts reopening, without turning those selections into personal adoption or permanent published Deck pins. The alternative is to load newer foreign content on reopening, which can visibly change an unfinished programme. **Blocks Checkpoint 3’s session/context design.**

**6. What should happen when a Library-origin fork is published privately?**

Currently fork roots start private, and Library-origin publication can explicitly avoid My Decks entry. A clean private publication with no membership would disappear from all three current discovery surfaces: Library, My Decks and My Drafts.

I recommend an explicit private-publication path that also adds that Deck to My Decks, while public Library-origin publication remains canonical-only. This would be an additional, approved exception for private fork publication—not a general rule that publication creates personal data.

Alternatives include blocking private Library-only publication or adding another owned-content surface; the latter would expand scope. **Blocks Checkpoint 4.**

**7. Where should foreign-edit confirmation occur, and do visibility-only changes count as the first fork edit?**

Confirmation before entering a foreign Deck is part of your understanding. The missing detail is editing a foreign Card inside an already-owned Deck.

I recommend confirming before that Card’s first editing session, using the existing Creator modal, with no repeated prompt for later edits to the same owned fork. Visibility intent should be treated consistently as meaningful work, but the current fork commands only accept a content difference and need an explicit contract for this case.

Alternatives include one broader confirmation covering borrowed Cards when entering Creator, or deferring visibility editing until the content fork exists. **Blocks the final interaction contract for Checkpoints 3–4.**

**8. What happens when the Card is already mine but the containing Deck belongs to someone else?**

This mixed case is not explicitly resolved. Card ownership normally means editing the same Card identity; its publication affects that shared Card everywhere.

I recommend preserving that ownership rule: edit the owned Card normally, and fork the foreign Deck only when its own composition/content changes. The confirmation must make clear that the Card is already yours. The alternative is also creating a Deck adaptation when the first owned-Card edit occurs. **Blocks this mixed-ownership branch of Checkpoints 3–4.**

**9. Where should Publish and leave go after publishing a self-use Deck fork?**

Keeping both memberships is settled; the destination is not. Existing Creator return state points to the source Deck.

I recommend opening the newly published personal Deck after Publish and leave from a My Decks-origin adaptation. Saving an unpublished draft and leaving would return to the original context. Library-origin editing would continue returning to Library.

Alternatives are always returning to the source or to the My Decks collection. **Blocks Checkpoint 4 navigation tests.**

**10. Does Phase 5 include `Copy to…` for another creator’s public Card?**

The roadmap includes cross-owner reuse, but the current Copy operation is explicitly owned-Card-only. Retaining unchanged shared references during a Deck fork does not by itself provide this action.

I recommend allowing reference-only Copy for eligible public foreign Cards through the existing Creator Card modal, retaining the approved destination and auto-publication rules. I would leave new Library/working-Card Copy entry points for later.

Alternatively, defer foreign Copy entirely and limit Phase 5 reuse to references retained through adaptation. **This is a scope decision; it can be deferred if that narrower boundary is explicit.**

The two areas where I would most value a second technical opinion are the **Creator identity/upload handoff**, particularly first-edit uploads and simultaneous edits, and the **Update transition while personal mutations are in flight**. Both need precise integration with existing lifetimes and recovery; neither warrants replacing the working architecture wholesale.

I’ll wait for your answers before treating this as the final Phase 5 contract or beginning implementation.

The five-checkpoint structure is now agreed. The plan below incorporates your decisions and preserves the existing first-class Card/Deck architecture.

I recommend **Refresh/Cancel when an Update confirmation becomes stale**. The existing Library Add implementation already provides the relevant freshness guards and transaction ordering. Reusing that approach also protects version selection for newly introduced Cards during Deck Update. Refresh reloads the confirmation; it never adopts anything automatically.

The working tree is clean. This review made no changes.

## Governing contract

Phase 5 delivers two connected capabilities:

- Explicit adoption of newer Card and Deck versions in My Decks.
- Continuous Creator editing across ownership boundaries, creating owned canonical content on the first meaningful persisted change.

The following rules govern every checkpoint:

| Operation | Result |
|---|---|
| Card Update | Advances the user’s adoption of that Card identity wherever it appears. |
| Deck Update | Advances that Deck’s adopted composition; existing CardData keeps its adopted versions and state. |
| Edit owned content | Preserves its identity and uses normal draft/publication behaviour. |
| Edit foreign Deck content or composition | Creates an owned Deck draft containing the meaningful change. |
| Edit foreign Card | Creates an owned Card draft with new Step IDs and lineage; replaces the intended Deck reference. |
| Edit an owned Card inside a foreign Deck | Changes the owned Card; does not automatically create a Deck copy. |
| Copy a public foreign Card | Adds the same Card identity to an owned destination Deck. |
| First Card-copy publication | Publishes v1 and performs eligible personal-state inheritance once. |

Canonical creation and drafting create no personal learning records. Personal adoption remains positive-version-only. Card and Deck publication remain independent.

## Checkpoint 1 — Update adoption foundations

**Objective**

Establish explicit, transactional review and adoption operations before exposing Update controls.

**User-facing behaviour established by this checkpoint**

- Card and Deck updates remain independent.
- Existing personal progress, skipped status, readings, reflection, target date, media, chats, tests and history relationships are preserved.
- Reviews include every non-empty update note between the adopted and proposed versions, in publication order.
- A stale review requires Refresh or Cancel.
- Removed Deck references leave retained CardData intact.
- Existing active Card selection survives if still present; otherwise it becomes the first remaining Card or null.
- Cadence anchors and existing dates survive Deck Update.

**Technical work**

Extend [repository.ts](./src/lib/cards/repository.ts) with explicit Card/Deck review and adoption operations. Add equivalent Deck-note retrieval and bound both note queries to the reviewed target version.

A review response will identify:

- Entity identity and title.
- Current adopted version.
- Proposed immutable version.
- Intervening non-empty notes.
- Preconditions required to apply that review safely.

For Deck Update, the server also captures the composition and version selections needed for missing CardData. These are internal validation inputs; the modal will not become a structural comparison interface.

Adoption transactions will:

1. Authenticate and validate the personal context.
2. Validate access to the exact immutable versions.
3. Revalidate the reviewed selection.
4. Preserve existing personal records.
5. Initialize only missing state.
6. Advance the appropriate adoption pointer.
7. Return the actual committed adoption result.

Reuse the existing deterministic Card-root-before-Deck guard ordering where publication must be serialized with adoption. Technical guards must not change authoring revisions or Library ordering.

For Card state reconciliation:

- Continuing Step IDs retain completion, including `skipped`, and readings.
- Newly encountered identities receive normal defaults.
- Retained state for no-longer-displayed identities is not destructively removed.
- Matching never uses titles or positions.
- Content changes never trigger automatic resets.

The current three-Step Creator model remains unchanged.

For Deck Update:

- Existing CardData wins, including older adopted Card versions.
- Missing CardData adopts the latest eligible publication selected by the transaction.
- `cardVersionAtPublish` remains historical information.
- Missing scheduled dates are initialized through the established working-open process.
- Adoption alone does not turn an unopened Deck into an opened one.

**Recovery**

Repeated requests must not downgrade adoption, duplicate records or replay initialization over subsequent learning changes. A completed request is acknowledged from the committed personal state. Later conflicting adoption or archive transitions return a structured result without overwriting them.

An already-completed adoption must be recognized before treating a later upstream publication as a stale original request.

**Documentation**

Correct the obsolete lifecycle and promotion descriptions in [README.md](./README.md:154) and affected architecture documentation. Record the approved Phase 5 contract without rewriting unrelated design material.

**Tests and acceptance**

Integration coverage includes:

- Skipped-version notes and blank notes.
- Card Update shared across several Decks.
- Deck Update retaining existing Card adoption.
- New, removed and reordered Deck references.
- Empty Decks and removed active Cards.
- Stable Step state through content edits and reorder.
- Defensive Step-identity differences.
- Concurrent publication, learning changes, adoption and Archive.
- Transaction rollback and lost-response retry.
- Missing/private-era versions and unauthorized requests.

Acceptance requires atomic adoption, preserved personal state and no canonical-content mutation.

**Review gate**

Report operation contracts, schema changes, concurrency/recovery evidence, documentation corrections and verification results before proceeding.

## Checkpoint 2 — My Decks Update experience

**Objective**

Expose the adoption foundation through the approved minimal controls and confirmation modal.

**User-facing deliverables**

- Small Deck Update button alongside Completion and Confidence in the detail header.
- Small Card Update button in the bottom-left of the active Card front, clear of the centred creator attribution.
- Consistent compact icon-and-label styling.
- Controls appear only for eligible updates.
- Confirmation identifies the entity, shows chronological notes and provides Cancel/Update.
- With no notes, it simply explains that a newer version is available.
- Confirmation explains preserved personal progress.
- Card confirmation explains that adoption affects the Card wherever the user uses it.
- Stale confirmation offers Refresh/Cancel.

No detailed comparison, structural-change renderer or future Card-header features are included.

**Technical work**

Use the shared presentation components and explicit working capabilities. Library receives no personal Update control.

Extend the working read models with the metadata needed by the controls. Use narrowly scoped action slots and selectors so the buttons do not reposition titles, Steps, media, dates or attribution.

Before applying an Update, settle relevant pending personal mutations and uploads. In particular, a Deck Update must not remove the working context required by an unfinished upload.

After success:

- Replace the affected working projection with acknowledged server state.
- Refresh relevant adoption metadata and the user-scoped working cache.
- Preserve valid navigation.
- Run normal working initialization where needed.
- Avoid remounting upload owners unnecessarily or installing stale responses.

The existing [workingCardStore](./src/lib/cards/workingCardStore.ts:11) already distinguishes users and adopted versions; it will remain part of this boundary.

**Tests and acceptance**

Browser tests cover:

- Eligible controls appearing and disappearing.
- Notes, no-note confirmation, cancellation and stale refresh.
- Independent Card/Deck adoption.
- Shared Card state across Decks.
- Pending saves, failed saves and in-flight uploads.
- Removed active Card and empty Deck behaviour.
- Library/My Decks navigation with different versions.
- Account changes and delayed responses.
- Button hit areas not triggering Card drag, focus or flip.
- Mobile/desktop geometry, including clearance from attribution.

Existing geometry anchors retain the established tolerance. No baselines will be regenerated merely to accommodate unintended movement.

**Review gate**

Report rendered controls, lifecycle behaviour, geometry evidence, test results and a focused manual-review checklist.

## Checkpoint 3 — Foreign Creator session and identity handoff

**Objective**

Enable mixed-ownership editing while preserving Creator’s save, upload and component lifetimes.

This is the highest-risk checkpoint.

**User-facing contract**

- Entering Creator creates no copy.
- Cancellation before meaningful persistence creates no copy.
- First meaningful autosave creates the necessary owned draft and includes the change.
- Editing continues without a reload, lost keystrokes, duplicate Cards or a visible technical identity transition.
- Owned Cards retain their identities regardless of the containing Deck’s owner.
- Foreign Card selections remain exact across reload and My Drafts reopening.

**Technical work**

Extend the existing [Creator persistence coordinator](./src/components/creator/creatorPersistenceCoordinator.ts:161), retaining entity-scoped desired state, generations, acknowledgements and recovery.

Introduce a focused source-to-owned binding:

- Stable editing-session identity preserves component lifetime.
- Canonical target IDs are allocated once.
- The first operation freezes its exact source, target identities and submitted generation.
- Successful acknowledgement binds the session to the target.
- Newer local edits remain queued and are saved afterwards.
- Card/Step bindings, modal targets and upload sessions are updated together.
- URL changes retain navigation origin and do not remount the active session.

Serialize first Deck creation so simultaneous edits cannot create several Deck copies.

Extend the existing fork transactions for the actual first-edit cases:

- Deck content/composition change.
- Foreign Card edit inside an owned Deck.
- Combined foreign Deck plus foreign Card edit.
- Add Card as the first change.
- Visibility-only change.
- Intro or Step media as the first change.

**Visibility-only creation**

The backend will accept an explicit visibility-intent operation as meaningful even when canonical content is unchanged.

Default private intent alone never triggers persistence. A confirmed explicit change creates the owned identity; reversing the selection afterwards edits that owned identity and never reattaches the original.

**First-edit uploads**

The current [upload authorization](./src/lib/cards/uploadAuthorization.ts:6) assumes an existing owned Creator context. Extend it with narrowly authorized staging for prospective owned targets.

Staging must be bound to the authenticated actor, exact accessible source and allocated target. Successful media attachment participates in the meaningful fork save. It must not write to the source or require an unchanged placeholder fork.

Owned Card uploads inside foreign Decks will be authorized by Card ownership independently of Deck ownership. Personal-upload authorization remains separate.

**Persisted foreign selections**

Add minimal private authoring metadata for selected foreign Card versions. It will:

- Be validated against exact-version access rules.
- Survive reload and draft reopening.
- Remain outside canonical published content and Library DTOs.
- Create no CardData or personal adoption.
- Prevent later personal adoption or upstream publication from silently changing the editing source.

These selections govern authoring and exact fork sources. They do not redefine published Deck reference semantics.

**Tests and acceptance**

Cover:

- Typing during delayed first save.
- Simultaneous Deck and multiple Card edits.
- Exact-version selection after newer publications.
- Reload and My Drafts reopening.
- Visibility confirmation cancellation and reversal.
- Media-first and Add-first creation.
- Lost response, duplicate retry and uncertain recovery.
- Upload completion during identity transition.
- Reference removal during upload.
- Navigation/publication during pending handoff.
- Unauthorized and private-era sources.

Acceptance requires one canonical outcome per operation, correct edit targeting and no personal records from fork creation.

**Review gate**

Report the handoff design, transaction extensions, upload authorization, persisted authoring metadata and adversarial test results.

## Checkpoint 4 — Foreign editing, publication and reopening

**Objective**

Complete the approved Library/My Decks editing journeys using Checkpoint 3’s foundation.

**Editing and confirmation**

- Foreign Deck Edit explains that changes create the user’s own copy while leaving the original unchanged.
- User-facing language avoids “fork”.
- Foreign Card editing inside an owned Deck receives the corresponding confirmation before the first operation requiring a copy.
- Cancel saves nothing and creates nothing.
- Owners edit existing identities, including Decks containing foreign published Cards.
- Editing an owned Card inside a foreign Deck preserves that Card and does not automatically copy the Deck.

The existing [Creator DTO restriction](./src/lib/cards/readModels.ts:21) will be replaced by explicit per-entity ownership and capabilities. Foreign content responses will expose authorized immutable content without private drafts or authoring metadata.

**Publication and personal entry**

| First Deck-copy publication | Personal result |
|---|---|
| My Decks-origin, private or public | New personal membership; source membership retained. |
| Library-origin, private | New personal membership. |
| Library-origin, public | Canonical publication only; no automatic Deck membership. |

Existing memberships remain preserved on subsequent publication.

For My Decks continuity, carry the approved cadence anchor and valid/remapped active Card. The new membership starts active and unopened, without copied sharing recipients.

For every first Card-copy publication with eligible source CardData:

- Copy current completion/skipped, readings, reflection and target date once.
- Read source state transactionally.
- Preserve the source record.
- Establish the personal history relationship.
- Keep chats, tests and personal media stored once in their original context.
- Apply the same inheritance regardless of Library/My Decks origin.

With no source CardData, Card publication remains canonical-only.

Publish and leave publishes only owned outstanding entities. Foreign references do not become foreign save/publication lanes. Public Deck publication requires genuinely published public Cards; private intent alone never qualifies.

Use consistent publication acknowledgements and existing immutable receipts to preserve exact recovery, including personal-entry outcomes.

**Copy foreign public Cards**

Extend the existing Creator Card-modal Copy workflow and domain operation to eligible public foreign Cards.

Preserve:

- Same Card identity and original ownership.
- Owned destinations, including archived and unpublished Decks.
- Duplicate prevention.
- No automatic unarchive.
- Permanent reuse restriction.
- Clean-destination auto-publication rules.
- Exact draft-only versus published recovery and concise feedback.
- No implicit Card publication or visibility promotion.

Draft-only Copy creates no personal data. Where auto-publication advances an existing personal Deck, its normal missing-CardData initialization remains part of that publication lifecycle.

**Return navigation**

The current [Creator route](./src/app/creator/edit/[deckTemplateId]/page.tsx) maps Library origin to `/library`. Replace that with an explicit original Library Deck identity.

Keep this navigation origin separate from the editable target identity and provenance:

- Library-origin Creator returns to `/library/{originalDeckId}`.
- This applies to owners and non-owners.
- Identity handoff and reload retain the original destination.
- Self-use Deck-copy Publish and leave opens the newly published personal Deck through normal working initialization.
- Existing direct-entry and other My Decks defaults remain intact.

Every exit continues through the existing save/upload, cancellation and publication safeguards.

**Tests and acceptance**

Two-account browser journeys cover:

- Owner and non-owner Library Edit.
- Owned Deck with foreign Cards.
- Foreign Deck with owned and foreign Cards.
- Only the edited foreign Cards receiving new identities.
- Visibility-only editing and cancellation.
- Public and private publication entry policies.
- Source membership retained.
- Personal inheritance/history privacy.
- Copy auto-publication, dirty destinations and archived destinations.
- First-public confirmations and partial publication recovery.
- Exact Library-detail return after save, publish, reload and handoff.
- Self-use Publish and leave opening the new Deck.
- Draft reopening with pinned foreign versions.

**Review gate**

Report the complete journeys, permission boundaries, navigation evidence, recovery results and manual acceptance checks.

## Checkpoint 5 — Full verification and acceptance

Audit the final implementation against this contract and run:

```bash
npm run test:unit
npm run test:integration
npm run test:e2e
npm run test:phase2
npm run typecheck
npm run lint
MONGODB_URI='' MONGODB_DB='' npm run build
git diff --check
git diff HEAD --check
```

Verification includes:

- Independent Card/Deck adoption.
- Stable Step-state preservation.
- Privacy of private-era versions and personal history.
- Concurrent publication, adoption, learning edits, Copy and Archive.
- First-edit uploads and simultaneous Creator edits.
- Exact lost-response recovery.
- Account switching and delayed responses.
- Library canonical-only behaviour.
- First-open cadence and one personal target date per Card.
- Mobile/desktop presentation, gestures, flips, media and uploads.
- All existing Phase 1–4 regressions.

Use disposable local databases. No production migration or Atlas access is included.

The final report will identify application blockers, baseline warnings, manual verification limits and deferred work. The existing headed-mobile reliability issue and real Cloudflare playback limitation remain explicitly recorded unless separately resolved.

## Principal risks and safeguards

| Risk | Safeguard |
|---|---|
| Handoff loses edits or misdirects uploads | Stable session lifetime, frozen first command, atomic binding and generation-aware subsequent saves. |
| Simultaneous edits create duplicate copies | One Deck-creation barrier, stable target IDs and exact transaction recovery. |
| Visibility-only editing creates an accidental copy | Explicit action and confirmation; default intent never triggers creation. |
| Draft reopening silently changes foreign content | Persisted, authorized immutable authoring selections. |
| Update overwrites newer personal work | Transactional current-state reads and field-level updates; relevant pending work settled first. |
| Retry reverses Archive or replays inheritance | Expected personal state, explicit completed outcomes and existing first-publication receipts. |
| Foreign draft metadata leaks through publication review | Ownership-aware, allow-listed review information. |
| New controls disrupt layout or gestures | Scoped action slots, pointer/keyboard tests and unchanged geometry tolerances. |

Standalone Card surfaces/editing, Creator Preview Draft, broader discovery, test-history UI, learning event logs and reset-progress controls remain deferred.

**QUESTIONS FOR USER**

No further product decision currently blocks this plan. The outstanding implementation risks above can be addressed within the approved behaviour and reviewed at their checkpoint gates.

This is the definitive Phase 5 plan for your approval. Checkpoint 1 will begin only after your explicit authorization.
